They control the collection of payments from their customers and manage the credit department of a bank.

candidates.title: contract manager
candidates.description: Contract managers oversee the respect of awarded contracts to ensure that services are delivered as foreseen and that each step of the delivery is properly documented. They act as the main point of contact for suppliers on contractual matters and report back to their leadership. They implement financial and operational controls and ensure compliance with all reporting requirements.

description: The Actuarial Valuation Manager leads and oversees actuarial valuation activities to assess the financial impact of risks and liabilities, particularly within insurance companies, pension funds, and related financial institutions. The role applies actuarial and statistical methods to evaluate current and future obligations, ensuring valuations are accurate, compliant with regulatory and professional standards, and suitable for financial reporting. It also provides analytical and strategic insights to support organisational decision-making and regulatory submissions.
tasks: Lead and manage actuarial valuation teams, ensuring effective delivery of valuation activities. Conduct periodic actuarial valuations of pension schemes, insurance contracts, and other financial liabilities. Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and accounting standards, including IFRS 17 and Solvency II. Develop and implement actuarial valuation methodologies and frameworks to support accurate financial assessments. Analyse actuarial and financial data using statistical models and ICT tools to identify trends, correlations, and risks. Prepare detailed actuarial reports for senior management, regulators, and auditors. Collaborate with finance and risk management functions to support integrated financial planning and decision-making. Identify and assess actuarial and financial risks that may impact organisational outcomes, and implement mitigation measures. Supervise and mentor junior actuaries and analysts.

candidates.title: actuarial consultant
candidates.description: Actuarial consultants analyse, manage and provide guidance on financial impact of risks. They can work in fields related to insurance, pension, investment, banking, healthcare etc. Actuarial consultants apply technical and statistical models and theories to give strategic, commercial, and financial advice.

candidates.title: actuarial assistant
candidates.description: Actuarial assistants perform statistical data research in order to set premium rates and insurance policies. They review the possibility of accidents, injuries and property damage by using statistical formulas and models.

candidates.title: financial risk manager
candidates.description: Financial risk managers identify and assess potential risk areas threatening the assets or capital of organisations and give advice on how to deal with them. They specialise in either credit, market, operational or regulatory risk analysis. They use statistical analysis to evaluate risk, make recommendations to reduce and control financial risk and review documentation for legal compliance.

candidates.title: accounting manager
candidates.description: Accounting managers assume responsibility for all accounting activities relating to financial reporting. They develop and maintain accounting principles and procedures to ensure timely and accurate financial statements, supervise accounting staff and manage the accounting activities within the appropriate time frame and budget.

candidates.title: financial manager
candidates.description: Financial managers handle all the matters in reference to the finance and investments of a company. They manage financial operations of companies such as the assets, liabilities, equity and cash flow aiming to maintain the financial health of the company and operative viability. Financial managers evaluate the strategic plans of the company in financial terms, maintain transparent financial operations for taxation and auditing bodies, and create the financial statements of the company at the end of the fiscal year.

candidates.title: real estate manager
candidates.description: Real estate managers handle and oversee the operational aspects of commercial or residential properties such as private apartments, office buildings and retail stores. They negotiate contracts for lease, identify and plan new real estate projects and construction of new buildings by partnering with a developer to identify the appropriate site for new buildings, coordinate the feasibility study for new constructions and supervise all the administrative and technical aspects involved in expanding the business. They maintain the premises and aim to increase its value. They hire, train and supervise personnel.

candidates.title: corporate risk manager
candidates.description: Corporate risk managers identify and assess potential threats and opportunities to a company, and give advice on how to deal with them. They create preventive plans to avoid and reduce risks, and put plans in place for when the company is threatened. They coordinate risk management aspects across the different functions of an organisation and are responsible for technical activities such as risk assessment, risk mapping and insurance purchase. They report on risk issues to the senior management and the company's board.

candidates.title: asset manager
candidates.description: Asset managers invest the money of a client into financial assets, through vehicles such as investment funds or management of individual clients’ portfolios. This includes the management of the financial assets, within a given investment policy and risk framework, the provision of information, and the assessment and monitoring of risks.

description: Transfer Pricing Manager plans, directs and oversees an organisation’s transfer pricing activities to ensure that intercompany transactions comply with domestic and international tax regulations. The role involves analysing cross-border transactions between related entities, developing and maintaining transfer pricing policies, and advising management on the tax implications of pricing arrangements. It also includes liaising with tax authorities and external advisers to support compliance, documentation and alignment with applicable guidelines.
tasks: Design and implement transfer pricing policies for intercompany transactions. Prepare and review transfer pricing documentation and reports in compliance with local tax regulations and guidelines. Oversee and manage a portfolio of transfer pricing projects. Conduct financial analysis to support transfer pricing policies and reporting requirements. Advise management on the impact of transfer pricing on business operations and strategies. Perform risk assessments and internal reviews to ensure compliance with transfer pricing regulations. Collaborate with tax authorities during audits and resolve transfer pricing issues. Stay updated on developments in transfer pricing regulations across relevant jurisdictions. Coordinate with external consultants and legal advisors on complex transfer pricing matters.

candidates.title: pricing specialist
candidates.description: Pricing specialists analyse production prices, market trends and competitors in order to establish the right price, taking brand and marketing concepts into consideration.

candidates.title: move manager
candidates.description: Move managers coordinate all the resources and activities comprised in moving services. They work together with clients to define the requirements of the service and adapt it to their demands. They manage communication with shipping companies, planners, and movers to assure compliance, business efficiency, and client satisfaction.

candidates.title: purchasing manager
candidates.description: Purchasing managers are in charge of buying goods, equipment and services for their company, and try to ensure the most competitive prices. They are also responsible for negotiating contracts, reviewing the quality of products and analysing suppliers, and for the use and resale of goods and services.

candidates.title: destination manager
candidates.description: Destination managers are in charge of managing and implementing the national/regional/local tourism strategies (or policies) for destination development, marketing and promotion.

candidates.title: property acquisitions manager
candidates.description: Property acquisitions managers ensure land or property acquisitions transactions. They liaise with relevant stakeholders concerning financial aspects and risks arising from the acquisition of property. Property acquisitions managers ensure compliance with legal requirements for purchasing property and take care of all documentation and closure techniques needed.

candidates.title: promotion manager
candidates.description: Promotion managers plan and implement promotional programs in the point-of-sale of products. They coordinate all efforts from personnel, below-the-line (BTL) advertising material, and conventional advertising efforts in order to raise awareness of a specific promotion.

candidates.title: bid manager
candidates.description: Bid managers are responsible for researching and selecting tenders, analysing tenders and submitting tenders. They take into account the requirements of the tendering company and the possibilities for implementation. They take care of both the calculation of costs and the estimation of possible risks. Bid managers are responsible for communication with the contracting company or institutions. They work together with project managers serve as an interface to customers in larger companies. They are often the primarily responsible for the offers (proposals) and their presentation.

candidates.title: forwarding manager
candidates.description: Forwarding managers plan and organise cargo shipments within national and international areas. They communicate with carriers and negotiate the best way to send the cargo to its destination which can be a single customer or a point of distribution. Forwarding managers act as experts in supply chain management. They know and apply the rules and regulations for each specific type of cargo and communicate the conditions and costs to the clients.

description: The Occupational Safety and Health Manager plans, implements and oversees organisational safety and health policies, programmes and management systems to prevent workplace hazards and ensure compliance with legal, regulatory and industry requirements. The role coordinates safety and health initiatives across worksites, monitors performance through inspections, audits and incident investigations, and recommends preventive and corrective actions to improve risk control and emergency preparedness. It also liaises with regulatory authorities and internal stakeholders to support statutory compliance and promote continuous improvement in workplace safety and health practices.
tasks: Develop and implement workplace safety and health policies and procedures. Conduct risk assessments, safety audits, and accident investigations, and recommend corrective actions. Lead safety training sessions, emergency drills, and employee awareness programmes. Ensure compliance with occupational safety and health regulations and applicable standards. Oversee the implementation and performance of safety and health programmes across the organisation. Maintain safety records, certifications, and regulatory documentation. Promote and reinforce a positive safety culture across the workplace through continuous engagement initiatives. Advise management on safety improvements, compliance issues, and risk mitigation strategies.

candidates.title: health safety and environmental manager
candidates.description: Health, safety and environmental managers design and execute corporate policies and procedures related to occupational health and safety and environmental protection. They analyse business processes to ensure compliance with government and environment legislation, conduct risk assessment in the domain of occupational health and safety, evaluate the environmental impact of economic activities and design the appropriate measures for the improvement of work environments and cultures. They coordinate the implementation of an integrated health, safety and environmental management system, defining effective indicators, organizing audits and eventually participating in accident investigation and reporting. They promote an integrated approach to sustainability and occupational health within business organisations, liaising with corporate and line managers and training employees. They are responsible for drafting technical documentation related to the compliance with health and safety and environmental legislation.

candidates.title: occupational health and safety inspector
candidates.description: Occupational health and safety inspectors perform workplace audits to ensure compliance with government and environment legislation. They also investigate work accidents. Occupational health and safety inspectors interview employees to ensure the work environment is compliant with health and safety rules, inspect the physical work site and analyse legal paperwork.

candidates.title: health and safety officer
candidates.description: Health and safety officers execute plans for the improvement of work environments and cultures. They assess risks and interview employees to ensure the work environment is compliant with health and safety rules, as well as ensuring the interaction within the workplace occurs in a positive and productive manner. If employed in a healthcare facility the health and safety officer has to investigate infections spreading across a facility and advice all employees how to combat and prevent infections. Furthermore health physics is applied at facilities where people are exposed to ionizing radiation such as nuclear power plants and research institutions.

candidates.title: construction safety manager
candidates.description: Construction safety managers inspect, enforce and control health and safety measures at construction sites. They also manage workplace accidents and take action to make sure that safety policies are correctly implemented.

candidates.title: health and safety inspector
candidates.description: Health and safety inspectors investigate the implementation and application of labour standards and policies in a workplace. They advise employers as well as employees on the improvement of policy and legislation implementation, ensure that the law is adhered to, and that matters of equality and labour rights are respected. They write reports and communicate with authorities.

candidates.title: health and safety engineer
candidates.description: Health and safety engineers design objects and programs by combining engineering principles and health and safety requirements. They envision the protection and well-being of the people using designed objects or performing work under designed health and safety programs. They assess facilities and the risks that they might pose (e.g. contaminant materials, ergonomics, handling of dangerous substances, etc.) in order to design and improve health and safety measures.

candidates.title: transport health and safety inspector
candidates.description: Transport health and safety inspectors are responsible for maintaining safety standards, reducing risk to company, staff and customers and achieving industry standards. They evaluate existing security systems to determine potential risks in all transport sectors such as road and sea transport, and develop policies and procedures that minimise the risk to properties, employees and computer systems.
candidates.matched_label: road occupational health and safety manager

candidates.title: airside safety manager
candidates.description: Airside safety managers supervise the airside operations' safety and security and advise the civil aviation authorities on the airport information systems changes. They write safety analysis reports, ensure compliance with standards and regulations and improve the airside safety procedures.

role_title: Supply Chain and Logistics Management Manager
cleaned_title: Supply Chain and Logistics Management Manager
description: The Supply Chain and Logistics Management Manager plans, directs and coordinates end-to-end supply chain and logistics activities to ensure efficient flow of goods from procurement through production, storage and distribution. The role focuses on optimising cost, quality, timeliness and reliability by developing and implementing strategies that improve operational performance, manage risks and align supply chain activities with organisational objectives.
tasks: Develop and implement supply chain, procurement, and logistics strategies to ensure efficient sourcing, production support, and delivery of goods. Plan, coordinate, and monitor transportation, warehousing, and distribution activities to ensure timely and cost-effective movement of materials and products. Manage supplier and vendor relationships, including negotiating pricing, contracts, and delivery terms. Oversee inventory management and demand forecasting to maintain optimal stock levels and minimise shortages or overstocking. Supervise warehouse operations, including receiving, storage, stock control, and dispatch of goods. Analyse supply chain and logistics data to identify process improvements, cost reductions, and operational efficiencies. Ensure compliance with relevant laws, regulations, and safety standards related to logistics, transportation, and storage. Collaborate with internal departments, including procurement, production, sales, and finance, to coordinate supply chain activities. Manage, supervise, and develop supply chain, logistics, and warehouse personnel to ensure effective operations. Prepare operational reports, forecasts, and performance indicators to support planning and decision-making.

candidates.title: supply chain manager
candidates.description: Supply chain managers plan, manage and coordinate all activities related to the sourcing and procurement of supplies needed to run manufacturing operations from the acquisition of raw materials to the distribution of finished products. The supplies can be raw materials or finished products, and it can be for internal or external use. Moreover, they plan and commission all the activities needed to be performed in manufacturing plants and adjust operations to changing levels of demand for a company's products.

candidates.title: logistics and distribution manager
candidates.description: Logistics and distribution managers take decisions on logistic services, operations and provisions. They take internal and external variables into consideration for effective and successful organisational logistic services. They give appropriate support to all the activities of the supply chain from the beginning to the end. These professionals organise the storage and distribution of goods and ensure that the right products are delivered to the right location on time and at a good cost.

candidates.title: intermodal logistics manager
candidates.description: Intermodal logistics managers manage and oversee commercial and operational aspects of intermodal logistics for an organisation.

candidates.title: supply chain assistant
candidates.description: Supply chain assistants work closely together with managers in the operations processes, namely purchasing, manufacturing, and distribution processes. They help with administrative and pragmatic follow up of actions such as invoicing, drafting and preparation of contracts and purchasing orders, reconciliation of inventory against documents, and communication with distribution channels.

candidates.title: logistics analyst
candidates.description: Logistics analysts streamline product manufacturing, transportation, storage and distribution. They assess production and supply chain problems to determine economically efficient solutions. They assists company managers in decision-making processes and direct programs designed to provide subcontractors, managers and customers with logistic technology.

candidates.title: logistics engineer
candidates.description: Logistics engineers design and implement systems aimed to optimise the time and efforts invested in transportation activities. They ensure that systems allow for micro-tracking and smooth communication across transport methods and stages.

candidates.title: warehouse manager
candidates.description: Warehouse managers assume the responsibility for storage facilities. They manage the operations and the staff within.

candidates.title: industrial production manager
candidates.description: Industrial production managers oversee the operations and the resources needed in industrial plants and manufacturing sites for a smooth running of the operations. They prepare the production schedule by combining the requirements of clients with the resources of the production plant. They organise the journey of incoming raw materials or semi finished products in the plant until a final product is delivered by coordinating inventories, warehouses, distribution, and support activities.

description: Technology Manager plans, directs and coordinates an organisation’s technology operations to ensure information systems and digital infrastructure effectively support business objectives. The role involves setting and implementing technology strategies, overseeing the delivery and maintenance of IT services, and managing specialist teams and projects to ensure systems are reliable, secure and fit for purpose. The Technology Manager works with other functions to align technological capabilities with operational and strategic requirements.
tasks: Develop and implement the organisation’s technology and IT strategy in line with business objectives. Oversee and manage IT infrastructure to ensure reliability, security, and operational efficiency. Plan, direct, and coordinate technology projects, including software development and hardware implementation. Lead, supervise, and develop IT personnel to ensure effective performance and capability development. Monitor and enhance business processes through the effective application of technology solutions. Ensure compliance with data protection, cybersecurity, and relevant technology regulations and standards. Manage IT budgets, resources, and procurement to support cost-effective technology operations. Research and evaluate emerging technologies to support innovation and organisational competitiveness. Provide technical direction and resolve complex technology issues to maintain operational continuity.

candidates.title: ICT research manager
candidates.description: ICT research managers plan, manage and monitor research activities and evaluate emerging trends in the information and communication technology field to assess their relevance. They also design and oversee staff training on the use of new technology and recommend ways to implement new products and solutions that will maximise benefits for the organisation.

candidates.title: ICT operations manager
candidates.description: ICT operations managers coordinate ICT services and infrastructure ensuring that the organisation has the required infrastructural resources. They also plan and monitor stages of either a business process or a computer process, negotiate contracts and take mitigation action in case of non-fulfilment of agreements. They oversee the day-to-day tasks involving infrastructure components, ICT systems and software.

candidates.title: chief technology officer
candidates.description: Chief technology officers contribute to a company's technical vision and lead all aspects of technology development, according to its strategic direction and growth objectives. They match technology with business needs.

candidates.title: ICT information and knowledge manager
candidates.description: ICT information and knowledge managers contribute to the definition of organisational information strategy and apply information and knowledge creation, editing, storage, and distribution policies. They manage the maintenance and evolution of structured and unstructured information. They create digital structures to enable exploitation and optimisation of information and knowledge, manage data analysis and enable business intelligence.

candidates.title: ICT product manager
candidates.description: ICT product managers analyse and define current and target status for ICT products, services or solutions. They estimate the cost effectiveness, points of risk, opportunities, strengths and weaknesses of products or services provided. ICT product managers create structured plans and establish time scales and milestones, ensuring optimisation of activities and resources.

candidates.title: ICT project manager
candidates.description: ICT project managers schedule, control and direct the resources, people, funding and facilities to achieve the objectives of ICT projects. They establish budgets and timelines, perform risk analysis and quality management, and complete project closure reports.

candidates.title: ICT environmental manager
candidates.description: ICT environmental managers know the green ICT legal framework, understand the role of the ICT network configurations in the economy and energy resources deployment and evaluate the impact of CO2 footprint of each ICT resource in the organisation's network. They plan and manage the implementation of environmental strategies for ICT networks and systems by conducting applied research, developing organisational policy, and devising strategies to meet sustainability targets. They ensure that the whole organisation uses ICT resources in a way that is as friendly as possible for the environment.

candidates.title: telecommunications manager
candidates.description: Telecommunications managers coordinate telecommunications staff activities for installing, troubleshooting, repairing and maintaining telecommunications equipment and infrastructure. They oversee the research, evaluation and implementation of new technologies and ensure a safe working environment for the employees. They supervise the inventory of supplies as well as user and customer assistance actions.

description: Chief Business Officer oversees the development and execution of overall business strategy to drive organisational performance, growth, and sustainability. The role coordinates key functions such as sales, marketing, product development, operations, and human resources to ensure strategic alignment and effective delivery of business objectives. It involves identifying new market opportunities, supporting long-term planning, and working with senior leadership to strengthen competitiveness and financial outcomes.
tasks: Lead and direct the organisation’s business development strategy to achieve corporate objectives. Develop and implement strategic business plans to drive revenue growth and market expansion. Plan, coordinate, and oversee business operations and service activities to ensure organisational effectiveness. Collaborate with senior leadership to enhance operational efficiency and overall performance. Manage financial planning processes, including budgeting, forecasting, and resource allocation. Identify and evaluate new business opportunities, strategic partnerships, and potential mergers or acquisitions. Plan and coordinate sales and marketing programmes based on market analysis. Provide leadership and oversight to senior business managers to ensure effective team performance. Represent the organisation at industry events, conferences, and business meetings.

candidates.title: chief executive officer
candidates.description: Chief executive officers hold the highest ranking in a pyramidal corporate structure. They are able to hold a complete idea of the functioning of the business, its departments, risks, and stakeholders. They analyse different kinds of information and create links among them for decision-making purposes. They serve as a communication link with the board of directors for reporting and implementation of the overall strategy.

candidates.title: chief marketing officer
candidates.description: Chief marketing officers manage the high level marketing operations in a company. They coordinate all the efforts related to the marketing, promotional, and advertising activities across units or geographical areas. They make sure that different activities aimed at creating awareness of products are profitable for the company. They take decisions and prepare reports on marketing projects and the costs they entail.

candidates.title: chief product officer
candidates.description: Chief Product Officers conduct the product strategy of a company, define the product vision, prioritise customer needs and design the product roadmap. Key drivers of innovation product processes and revenue growth, they are responsible for the entire product development process and product-related activities which involve design, elaboration, product strategy setting, creating multi-functional partnerships, and new products launch. Moreover, they lead the organisation’s product management team and closely work with the marketing department.

candidates.title: chief operating officer
candidates.description: Chief operating officers are the right hand and second in command of a company's chief executive officer. They ensure that the daily operations of the company run smoothly. Chief operating officers also develop company policies, rules and goals.

candidates.title: business manager
candidates.description: Business managers are responsible for setting the objectives of the business unit of a company, creating a plan for the operations, and facilitating the achievement of the objectives and implementation of the plan together with employees of the segment and stakeholders. They keep an overview of the business, understand detailed information of the business unit and support the department, and make decisions based on the information at hand.

candidates.title: chief information officer
candidates.description: Chief information officers define and implement the ICT strategy and governance. They determine necessary resources for the ICT strategy implementation, anticipate ICT market evolutions and company business needs. They contribute to the development of the organisation's strategic plan and ensure that the ICT infrastructure supports the organisation's overall operations and priorities.

candidates.title: chief technology officer
candidates.description: Chief technology officers contribute to a company's technical vision and lead all aspects of technology development, according to its strategic direction and growth objectives. They match technology with business needs.

candidates.title: chief data officer
candidates.description: Chief data officers manage companies' enterprise-wide data administration and data mining functions. They ensure data are used as a strategic business asset at the executive level and implement and support a more collaborative and aligned information management infrastructure for the benefit of the organisation at large.

description: Research and Development Manager plans, directs, and coordinates research and development activities to create or improve products, processes, and technologies. They lead teams of scientists and engineers, ensuring that projects—from formulation and testing to scale-up and commercialization—meet quality, safety, and regulatory standards, including halal requirements where applicable. The manager collaborates with production, quality, marketing, and sales teams to align innovations with market needs, and contributes to strategic decisions on the organisation’s product portfolio and future development.
tasks: Plan, direct, and coordinate research and development activities, ensuring alignment with organisational goals and regulatory standards. Lead and coordinate R&D teams to ensure effective execution of research and development projects. Develop and manage project timelines, budgets, and resource allocation to support R&D activities. Drive innovation to develop new products and enhance existing products. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure product feasibility, compliance, and market relevance. Conduct research, testing, and evaluation to ensure product quality, safety, and compliance with regulatory standards. Coordinate with external stakeholders, including suppliers and regulatory bodies, to support R&D activities and compliance. Analyse market trends and customer feedback to guide R&D priorities and product development strategies. Prepare and present technical reports, documentation, and progress updates to senior management.

candidates.title: product manager
candidates.description: Product managers are responsible for managing the lifecycle of a product. They research and develop new products in addition to managing existing ones through market research and strategic planning. Product managers perform marketing and planning activities to increase profits.

candidates.title: research and development manager
candidates.description: Research and development managers coordinate the efforts of scientists, academical researchers, product developers, and market researchers towards the creation of new products, the improvement of current ones or other research activities, including scientific research. They manage and plan research and development activities of an organisation, specify goals and budget requirements and manage the staff.

candidates.title: product development manager
candidates.description: Product development managers coordinate the development of new products from beginning to end. They receive briefings and start envisioning the new product considering design, technical and cost criteria. They conduct research on market needs and create prototypes of new products for untapped market opportunities. Product development managers also improve and boost technological quality.

candidates.title: research manager
candidates.description: Research managers oversee the research and development functions of a research facility or program or university. They support the executive staff, coordinate work activities, and monitor staff and research projects. They may work in a wide array of sectors, such as the chemical, technical and life sciences sector. Research managers can also advise on research and execute research themselves.

candidates.title: ICT research manager
candidates.description: ICT research managers plan, manage and monitor research activities and evaluate emerging trends in the information and communication technology field to assess their relevance. They also design and oversee staff training on the use of new technology and recommend ways to implement new products and solutions that will maximise benefits for the organisation.

candidates.title: games development manager
candidates.description: Games development managers supervise and coordinate the creation, development, distribution, and selling of games. They communicate with manufacturers to ensure the production of games.

candidates.title: project manager
candidates.description: Project managers oversee the project on a daily basis and are responsible for delivering high-quality results within the identified objectives and constraints, ensuring the effective use of the allocated resources. They are responsible for risk and issue management, project communication and stakeholder management. Project managers perform the activities of planning, organising, securing, monitoring and managing the resources and work necessary to deliver specific project goals and objectives in an effective and efficient way.

candidates.title: clothing development manager
candidates.description: Clothing development managers define product concepts that are consistent with target consumers and overall marketing strategy. They receive scientific findings and specifications in order to lead the briefing and implementation of all relevant seasonal and strategic concepts, including distribution by channel, product, colour introductions, and merchandised assortments. They ensure realisation and execution within budget. They manage and execute the product line and category life cycle from concept determination through sales and distribution, contribution in market research and industry trends to influence category concepts and products.

description: Forestry Manager oversees the management and conservation of forest areas, ensuring sustainable use of forest resources while balancing commercial, environmental, and social objectives. They plan and supervise forestry operations, including timber production, reforestation, pest and disease control, and manage forest inventory, while implementing conservation strategies, monitoring biodiversity, and ensuring compliance with environmental laws and regulations. Their work integrates forest regeneration, sustainable harvesting, and stakeholder engagement to maintain healthy and productive forest ecosystems.
tasks: Develop, implement, and monitor sustainable forest management plans in accordance with national policies and regulations. Plan, supervise, and coordinate forest operations, including harvesting, planting, regeneration, and restoration activities. Monitor forest health through analysis of ecological, biodiversity, and scientific data. Ensure compliance with environmental and forestry laws, regulations, and standards. Lead and manage forestry staff and provide technical guidance to operational teams. Collaborate with government agencies, industry stakeholders, and local communities on forestry and conservation initiatives. Prepare technical reports and analyses to support management decision-making and policy development. Manage budgets, costs, and financial planning for forestry operations and projects. Implement conservation and environmental protection initiatives to support sustainable forest management. Oversee forest fire prevention, pest control, and disease management measures.

candidates.title: forester
candidates.description: Foresters are responsible for monitoring the natural and economic viability of a woodland or forest and for activities related to its management and conservation.

candidates.title: forestry adviser
candidates.description: Forestry advisers provide services and advice on economic and environmental issues related to timber and forestry management in compliance with laws and regulations.

candidates.title: forestry technician
candidates.description: Forestry technicians assist and support the forest manager and implement their decisions. They supervise a team of forestry equipment operators and support and supervise forestry and environmental protection through research and data collection. They also manage resource conservation and harvesting plans.

candidates.title: forestry inspector
candidates.description: Forestry inspectors monitor forestry operations to ensure that workers and their activities comply with proper legislation and standards. They perform inspections to examine operations, wages, costs and health and safety measures. Forestry inspectors also analyse and report on their findings.

candidates.title: forestry equipment operator
candidates.description: Forestry equipment operators carry out operations with specialised equipment in the forest to maintain, harvest, extract and forward wood for the manufacturing of consumer goods and industrial products.

candidates.title: forest worker
candidates.description: Forest workers carry out a variety of jobs to care for and manage trees, woodland areas and forests. Their activities include planting, trimming, thinning and felling trees and protecting them from pests, diseases and damage.

candidates.title: forestry machinery technician
candidates.description: Forestry machinery technicians maintain and transport forestry machinery. As part of the maintenance of forestry machinery, they make use of specialised software and data recording systems and instruments.

candidates.title: wood factory manager
candidates.description: Wood factory managers realise planning, commercial and advisory tasks of wood factory and timber trade. They also manage purchasing, sales, customer service and marketing of wood and wood products.

description: Agricultural Manager directs and coordinates agricultural production across plantations, farms, horticultural projects, and livestock operations. They oversee the growth and health of crops, plants, or animals, manage resources, supervise staff, and implement operational plans to ensure productivity, sustainability, and compliance with environmental, safety, and regulatory standards. Their role also includes budgeting, equipment and supply management, and may involve marketing or coordinating the distribution of agricultural products.
tasks: Plan, coordinate, and oversee activities related to crop production, livestock care, plantations, and horticulture management. Manage human resources, including hiring, training, and supervising staff for agricultural operations. Develop, monitor, and manage budgets, finances, and operational reports for agricultural production. Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental, and halal regulations across agricultural operations. Monitor crop and livestock health and implement measures to optimise growth and prevent disease. Oversee the maintenance, use, and procurement of machinery, equipment, and materials. Implement sustainable farming practices, including soil management, irrigation, and pest control. Coordinate logistics, including the transportation of crops and livestock. Supervise breeding, reproduction, and processing activities for livestock to ensure quality standards.

candidates.title: farm manager
candidates.description: Farm managers plan and organise the daily operations, resourcing and business management of animal and crops producing farms.

candidates.title: agricultural policy officer
candidates.description: Agricultural policy officers analyse and identify agricultural policy issues and develop plans for improvement and new policy implementation. They write reports and presentations in order to communicate and acquire support for the policies from government officials and the public. They also communicate with professionals in agriculture for research and information purposes and perform administrative duties.

candidates.title: horticulture production manager
candidates.description: Horticulture production managers plan the production, manage the enterprise and participate in the horticultural production.

candidates.title: crop production manager
candidates.description: Crop production managers plan the production, manage the enterprise and participate in the production process of crop production facilities.

candidates.title: agricultural engineer
candidates.description: Agricultural engineers intervene in a variety of matters within the agriculture field in combination with engineering concepts. They design and develop machinery and equipment for an efficient and sustainable exploitation of the land. They advise on the use of resources in agricultural sites comprising the usage of water and soil, harvesting methods, and waste management.

candidates.title: food production manager
candidates.description: Food production managers oversee and monitor production and have overall responsibility for staffing and related issues. Hence, they have a detailed knowledge of the manufacturing products and their production processes. On the one hand, they control process parameters and their influence on the product and on the other hand, they ensure that staffing and recruitment levels are adequate.

candidates.title: agricultural inspector
candidates.description: Agricultural inspectors monitor agricultural operations in farms and other agricultural facilities. They inspect activities such as health and safety measures, costs and production processes to ensure that workers and their activities comply with proper legislation and standards. Agricultural inspectors also analyse and report on their findings.

candidates.title: agricultural machinery and equipment distribution manager
candidates.description: Agricultural machinery and equipment distribution managers plan the distribution of agricultural machinery and equipment to various points of sales.
candidates.matched_label: agricultural machinery and equipment logistics manager

description: Veterinary Manager plans, organises, and oversees the operations of livestock farms, veterinary clinics, hospitals, and animal health programs. They lead veterinary teams, manage staff and resources, ensure compliance with regulatory standards, and maintain high-quality care for animals. The role also involves managing budgets, client relations, inventory, and coordination with external suppliers.
tasks: Develop and implement grass and turf maintenance schedules, including watering, mowing, fertilisation, and pest control programmes. Oversee soil condition assessment and the application of fertilisers to maintain turf health. Supervise the installation and maintenance of turf and landscape features. Supervise and coordinate field staff, assign tasks, and ensure safe use of equipment. Monitor turf condition and identify pest, disease, and environmental issues affecting grass health. Plan and manage budgets, including procurement of machinery, equipment, and materials. Ensure compliance with environmental regulations and organisational policies. Coordinate park and field activities, including maintenance and related programmes. Provide training to staff on safety procedures and proper turf management practices.

candidates.title: official veterinarian
candidates.description: Official veterinarians are professionals with a comprehensive scientific education. They have the authority to carry out, in an independent, ethical and personally responsible capacity all veterinary activities with particular focus on the health and welfare of animals and public health in accordance with national and international legislation. They are responsible for national animal disease eradication programmes, the protection of public health and food or animal inspection, animal movements, and import and export of live animals and their products.

candidates.title: veterinary nurse
candidates.description: Veterinary nurses support animals undergoing veterinary treatment and give advice to veterinary clients in the promotion of animal health and disease prevention in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: animal facility manager
candidates.description: Animal facility managers coordinate and plan all activities of a zoo. They formulate policies, manage daily operations, and plan the use of materials and human resources. They are the driving force and public face of their institution. This often involves representing their institution on a national, regional and global scale and taking part in coordinated zoo activities.

candidates.title: specialised veterinarian
candidates.description: Specialised veterinarians are professionals with a comprehensive scientific education. They have the authority to carry out, in an independent, ethical and personally responsible capacity, all aspects of veterinary medicine, in the interest of the health and welfare of animals and public health in accordance with national and international legislation. In addition they need a recognized qualification and/or experience in a specific species and/or veterinary procedure.

candidates.title: veterinary scientist
candidates.description: Veterinary scientist develop and do research in animal models, compare basic biology across animals, and translate research findings to different species, including humans.

candidates.title: equine yard manager
candidates.description: Equine yard managers are responsible for the day to day running of the yard including managing staff, care of the horses, all aspects of health and safety and dealing with clients and owners.

candidates.title: general veterinarian
candidates.description: General veterinarians are professionals with a comprehensive scientific education. They have the authority to carry out, in an independent, ethical and personally responsible capacity, all aspects of veterinary medicine, in the interest of the health and welfare of animals and public health in accordance with national and international legislation. The generalist veterinarian can work with any species, however they may choose to work with a single species or types such as equine, companion or production animals.

candidates.title: veterinary technician
candidates.description: Veterinary technicians provide the technical and administrative support to the veterinarian in accordance with national legislation.

description: Field Manager (Grass) plans, organises, and maintains turf on golf courses, sports fields, parks, and landscaped areas. They oversee the upkeep, repair, and restoration of grassed surfaces, implement pest control measures, and coordinate staff to ensure the areas are safe, healthy, and visually appealing, while ensuring compliance with environmental standards.
tasks: Develop and implement grass and turf maintenance schedules, including watering, mowing, fertilisation, and pest control programmes. Oversee soil condition assessment and the application of fertilisers to maintain turf health. Supervise the installation and maintenance of turf and landscape features. Supervise and coordinate field staff, assign tasks, and ensure safe use of equipment. Monitor turf condition and identify pest, disease, and environmental issues affecting grass health. Plan and manage budgets, including procurement of machinery, equipment, and materials. Ensure compliance with environmental regulations and organisational policies. Coordinate park and field activities, including maintenance and related programmes. Provide training to staff on safety procedures and proper turf management practices.

candidates.title: equine yard manager
candidates.description: Equine yard managers are responsible for the day to day running of the yard including managing staff, care of the horses, all aspects of health and safety and dealing with clients and owners.

candidates.title: farm manager
candidates.description: Farm managers plan and organise the daily operations, resourcing and business management of animal and crops producing farms.

candidates.title: field survey manager
candidates.description: Field survey managers organise and supervise investigations and surveys on the request of a sponsor. They monitor their implementation according to production requirements and lead a team of field investigators.

candidates.title: crop production manager
candidates.description: Crop production managers plan the production, manage the enterprise and participate in the production process of crop production facilities.

candidates.title: recreational facilities manager
candidates.description: Recreational facilities managers direct the operations of facilities that provide recreational services such as gardens, spas, zoos, gambling and lottery facilities. They plan and organise the daily operations of the related staff and facilities and ensure the organisation follows the latest developments in its field. They coordinate the different departments of the facility and manage the correct use of rescources and budgets.

candidates.title: sport facility manager
candidates.description: Sport facility managers lead and manage a sport facility or venue, including its operations, programming, sales, promotion, health and safety, development, and staffing. They ensure it provides excellent customer service whilst achieving business, financial and operational targets.

candidates.title: horticulture production manager
candidates.description: Horticulture production managers plan the production, manage the enterprise and participate in the horticultural production.

candidates.title: camping ground manager
candidates.description: Camping ground managers plan, direct, or coordinate all campsite facilities and manage employees.

description: Aquaculture and Fisheries Production/Operation Manager plans, directs, and coordinates aquaculture and fishery operations, including the breeding, rearing, harvesting, processing, and distribution of fish and other aquatic species. They oversee operational activities to ensure product quality, timely production, regulatory compliance, and environmental sustainability, while managing staff and coordinating across departments such as logistics, quality assurance, and supply chain. The role also involves optimising production processes, controlling costs, and maintaining the health and welfare of aquatic stock.
tasks: Oversee daily aquaculture and fisheries production operations, including hatchery, breeding, farming, and harvesting activities. Manage production schedules, allocate workforce resources, and supervise staff performance and training. Monitor aquatic stock health through water quality assessment, disease prevention, and stock evaluation. Ensure compliance with quality control standards, safety protocols, and environmental regulations. Coordinate supply chain activities, including brood stock sourcing, materials management, inventory, and logistics. Supervise the operation and maintenance of hatchery, breeding, and production facilities and equipment. Manage budgets, expenses, and production costs to achieve operational and financial targets. Develop and implement production plans to maximise efficiency and meet market demand. Provide training and guidance to staff on standard operating procedures and best practices. Maintain accurate records of production data, including growth performance, feed usage, and mortality rates.

candidates.title: aquaculture production manager
candidates.description: Aquaculture production managers plan, direct and coordinate the production of fish, shellfish or other forms of aquatic life such as cash crops, in large-scale aquaculture operations to culture and harvest or for release into fresh, brackish or salt water.

candidates.title: aquaculture harvesting manager
candidates.description: Aquaculture harvesting managers control harvesting operations of aquatic organisms which entails understanding and knowledge of techniques and equipment used in harvesting processes.

candidates.title: aquaculture husbandry manager
candidates.description: Aquaculture husbandry managers specialise in the husbandry of ongrowing aquatic species, especially in the feeding, growth, and stock management processes.

candidates.title: aquaculture mooring manager
candidates.description: Aquaculture mooring managers carry out and supervise the mooring of cages in stable stations, drifting cages or even self-propelled and semi-submerged cages. They safely operate and moor a variety of different types of large-scale cages, manage conditions such as currents, wave climate and seabed profile, in open or semi-open water areas.

candidates.title: aquaculture quality supervisor
candidates.description: Aquaculture quality supervisors establish standards and policies for the quality control of aquatic organisms’ production. They test and inspect the stock according to hazard analysis and critical control points (HACCP) principles and safety regulations.

candidates.title: aquaculture recirculation manager
candidates.description: Aquaculture recirculation managers control the production of aquatic organisms in land-based recirculation systems, manage water re-use processes and supervise complex circulation, aeration and biofilter systems.

candidates.title: aquaculture hatchery manager
candidates.description: Aquaculture hatchery managers plan, direct, and coordinate the production in large-scale aquaculture operations to breed fish and shellfish, developing aquaculture breeding strategies using various types of spawning techniques. They control the reproduction and the early life cycle stages of cultured species. They supervise incubation, early feeding and rearing techniques of the cultured species.

candidates.title: fish production operator
candidates.description: Fish production operators regulate and supervise fish product manufacturing facilities. They keep stock of all required ingredients and equipment for mass manufacturing. They also perform processes such as moulding, breading, frying, freezing, setting the system's temperature and checking speeds.

description: Manufacturing Manager plans, directs, and oversees the production of goods to ensure efficient, safe, and high-quality operations within budget and schedule. They manage production teams, coordinate processes across departments, and ensure compliance with safety and regulatory standards, while optimising resources, improving efficiency, and meeting organisational targets in diverse manufacturing environments, including specialised areas such as design, metal heat treatment, and waste-to-energy operations.
tasks: Organise and supervise manufacturing production to meet output targets and ensure efficient operations. Lead and manage production teams, including resource allocation, workload monitoring, and staff development. Plan, implement, and monitor production strategies, policies, and daily operations. Ensure products meet quality standards through inspections, testing, and corrective actions. Control production costs, optimise processes, and minimise waste to meet budget requirements. Enforce workplace safety procedures and ensure compliance with health, safety, and environmental regulations. Coordinate with suppliers and cross-functional teams, including engineering and logistics, to improve production efficiency. Oversee specialised manufacturing processes to ensure compliance with technical and safety standards. Manage budgets, prepare reports, and monitor operational performance. Identify and implement process improvements, cost-saving measures, and best practices.

candidates.title: manufacturing manager
candidates.description: Manufacturing managers plan, oversee and direct the manufacturing process in an organisation. They ensure products and services are efficiently produced within the timeframe and budget given.

candidates.title: manufacturing facility manager
candidates.description: Manufacturing facility managers foresee the maintenance and routine operational planning of buildings intended to be used for manufacturing activities. They control and manage health and safety procedures, supervise the work of contractors, plan and handle buildings maintenance operations, fire safety and security issues, and oversee buildings' cleaning activities.

candidates.title: industrial production manager
candidates.description: Industrial production managers oversee the operations and the resources needed in industrial plants and manufacturing sites for a smooth running of the operations. They prepare the production schedule by combining the requirements of clients with the resources of the production plant. They organise the journey of incoming raw materials or semi finished products in the plant until a final product is delivered by coordinating inventories, warehouses, distribution, and support activities.

candidates.title: chemical production manager
candidates.description: Chemical production managers are responsible for the technical coordination and control of the chemical production processes. They steer one or more manufacturing units and oversee the implementation of technical and human means, within the framework of objectives of volume, quality and planning. Chemical production managers design and ensure that the production plans and schedules are met. They are responsible for implementation of the processes designed to ensure quality of the manufactured product, good working conditions and environmental practices, and safety of the workplace.

candidates.title: metal production manager
candidates.description: Metal production managers organise and manage the day-to-day and long-term project work in a metal fabrication factory, to process basic metals into fabricated metals. They create and schedule production plans, recruit new staff, enforce safety and company policies, and strive for customer satisfaction through guaranteeing the product's quality.

candidates.title: food production manager
candidates.description: Food production managers oversee and monitor production and have overall responsibility for staffing and related issues. Hence, they have a detailed knowledge of the manufacturing products and their production processes. On the one hand, they control process parameters and their influence on the product and on the other hand, they ensure that staffing and recruitment levels are adequate.

candidates.title: manufacturing engineer
candidates.description: Manufacturing engineers design manufacturing processes for different kinds of production processes. They integrate those specificities and constraints posed by the industry or the product being produced with general and wide-spread manufacturing engineering principles into the design and planification of manufacturing processes.

candidates.title: production supervisor
candidates.description: Production supervisors coordinate, plan and direct manufacturing and production processes. They are responsible for reviewing production schedules or orders as well as dealing with staff in these production areas.

description: Electrical Manager oversees and directs the electrical operations of an organisation, ensuring that electrical systems and components function efficiently and safely. The manager plans, coordinates, and manages maintenance services, designs and implements electrical systems, supervises engineers and technicians, and ensures compliance with safety standards. The manager’s role involves budgeting for electrical projects and collaborating with other departments to integrate electrical systems with broader mechanical and industrial processes.
tasks: Plan, manage, and oversee electrical systems and infrastructure to ensure efficient electricity production. Manage engineering teams, including staff allocation, resource planning, and project scheduling. Provide technical guidance and support for electrical projects and operational planning. Ensure efficient electricity production and optimal utilisation of resources. Ensure compliance with safety standards, regulatory requirements, and operational guidelines. Manage budgets, cost estimates, and procurement of cost-effective materials and resources. Provide training, mentoring, and development for engineers and technical staff.

candidates.title: electrical supervisor
candidates.description: Electrical supervisors monitor the operations involved in installing and servicing electricity cables and other electrical infrastructure. They assign tasks and take quick decisions to resolve problems.

candidates.title: power plant manager
candidates.description: Power plant managers supervise operations in power plants which produce and transport energy. They coordinate the production of energy in the plant, and supervise the construction, operation and maintenance of energy transmission and distribution networks and systems.

candidates.title: electrical engineer
candidates.description: Electrical engineers design and develop electrical systems, electrical equipment, components, motors, and equipment with the feature of energy transmission. They engage in large scale projects such as the design and maintenance of power stations, and the distribution of power to smaller applications such as household appliances.

candidates.title: electrical equipment production supervisor
candidates.description: Electrical equipment production supervisors coordinate, plan and direct the production process of electrical equipment. They manage labourers working on the production line, oversee the quality of the assembled goods, and perform cost and resource management.

candidates.title: electrician
candidates.description: Electricians fit and repair electrical circuits and wiring systems. They also install and maintain electrical equipment and machinery. This work can be performed indoors as well as outdoors, in nearly every type of facility.

candidates.title: industrial electrician
candidates.description: Industrial electricians install and maintain electricity cables and other electrical infrastructure in large industrial and commercial buildings. They perform inspections and repair defective parts of electrical systems to ensure efficiency.

candidates.title: energy manager
candidates.description: Energy managers coordinate the energy use in an organisation, and aim to implement policies for increased sustainability, and minimisation of cost and environmental impact. They monitor the energy demands and use, and develop improvement strategies, as well as researching the most beneficial source of energy for the organisation's needs.

candidates.title: electrical household appliances distribution manager
candidates.description: Electrical household appliances distribution managers plan the distribution of electrical household appliances to various points of sales.

description: Energy Manager is responsible for overseeing and optimising energy usage within an enterprise or public facility. The manager monitors energy consumption, develops and implements strategies to improve efficiency, manages energy audits, and ensures compliance with environmental and regulatory standards. The manager’s role includes coordinating energy-saving projects, promoting best practices, analysing performance data, and supporting organisational sustainability and cost-reduction objectives.
tasks: Conduct energy audits to assess consumption patterns and identify opportunities for improvement. Monitor and manage energy efficiency across organisational facilities and operations. Develop and implement energy management strategies to reduce costs and support sustainable operations. Measure, analyse, and forecast energy consumption to optimise energy usage. Identify and implement energy-efficient technologies and cost-saving initiatives. Promote and implement sustainability programmes, including renewable energy adoption and carbon reduction initiatives. Ensure compliance with energy regulations and environmental requirements. Coordinate with departments to align energy objectives and maintain efficient energy systems. Oversee energy management staff, including training and performance monitoring.

candidates.title: energy manager
candidates.description: Energy managers coordinate the energy use in an organisation, and aim to implement policies for increased sustainability, and minimisation of cost and environmental impact. They monitor the energy demands and use, and develop improvement strategies, as well as researching the most beneficial source of energy for the organisation's needs.

candidates.title: power plant manager
candidates.description: Power plant managers supervise operations in power plants which produce and transport energy. They coordinate the production of energy in the plant, and supervise the construction, operation and maintenance of energy transmission and distribution networks and systems.

candidates.title: energy conservation officer
candidates.description: Energy conservation officers promote the conservation of energy in both residential homes as in businesses. They advise people on ways te reduce their power consumption by enforcing energy efficiency improvements and implementing energy demand management policies.

candidates.title: energy analyst
candidates.description: Energy analysts evaluate the consumption of energy in buidings owned by consumers and businesses. By analysing existing energy systems, they recommend cost-effective alternatives. Energy analysts suggest efficiency improvements, make business analyses and participate in the development of policies concerning the use of traditional fuels, transportation, and other factors relating to energy consumption.

candidates.title: energy consultant
candidates.description: Energy consultants advise clients on the advantages and disadvantages of different energy sources. They help clients to understand energy tariffs and try to reduce their energy consumption and carbon footprint by using energy efficient products and methods.

candidates.title: energy engineer
candidates.description: Energy engineers design new, efficient and clean ways to produce, transform, and distribute energy to improve environmental sustainability and energy efficiency. They deal with the extraction of energy through natural resources, such as oil or gas, or renewable and sustainable sources, such as wind or solar power.

candidates.title: energy systems engineer
candidates.description: Energy systems engineers supervise the energy conversion and distribution processes. They analyse the energy supply and consumption efficiency developing new ways to improve the existing processes, taking into account both the technical and the financial aspects. They also study the environmental impact of energy usage and combine the production of renewable energy in the current power systems.

candidates.title: sustainability manager
candidates.description: Sustainability managers are responsible for ensuring the sustainability of business processes. They provide assistance in the design and implementation of plans and measures to ensure that the manufacturing processes and products comply with given environmental regulations and social responsibility standards and they monitor and report on the implementation of sustainability strategies within the company supply chain and business process. They analyse issues linked to manufacturing processes, use of materials, waste reduction, energy efficiency and products traceability to improve environmental and social impacts and integrate sustainability aspects into the company culture.

description: Production Manager (Manufacturing) plans, directs, and oversees production operations across various manufacturing sectors, including food, halal meat, chemicals, and photovoltaic products. They ensure processes are efficient, safe, and compliant with regulatory and quality standards, while optimising workflows, resources, and equipment. The role includes managing production teams, implementing continuous improvement initiatives, monitoring performance, maintaining workplace safety, and coordinating with other departments to achieve production targets and operational excellence.
tasks: Plan and implement production strategies and policies to meet quality, output, and safety requirements. Oversee daily production operations to ensure efficient and continuous manufacturing processes. Monitor and analyse production processes to optimise efficiency, reduce waste, and support continuous improvement initiatives. Manage and supervise production staff, including training, performance monitoring, and adherence to safety protocols. Ensure compliance with relevant industry regulations, quality standards, and safety requirements. Coordinate with suppliers, logistics, engineering, and other departments to maintain smooth production flow. Schedule equipment maintenance, monitor machinery performance, and address operational issues to minimise downtime. Manage budgets, control production costs, and prepare production reports for senior management. Oversee inventory management, including raw materials and finished goods, to support uninterrupted operations.
