Telecommunications engineers design and oversee the service delivery in all it's phases, supervising the installation and use of telecommunications equipment and facilities, preparing documentation and providing training for company staff once new equipment has been installed.

candidates.title: telecommunications engineering technician
candidates.description: Telecommunications engineering technician deploy, maintain and monitor a telecommunication system that provides interactions between data and voice communications, such as telephone, video conferencing, computer, and voicemail systems. They are also involved in the design, manufacturing, construction, maintenance and repair of telecommunication systems. Telecommunications engineering technicians provide technical assistance in the research and development of telecommunication equipment.

candidates.title: telecommunications technician
candidates.description: Telecommunications technicians install, test, maintain and troubleshoot telecommunications systems. They repair or replace defective devices and equipment and maintain a safe working environment and a complete inventory of supplies. They also provide user or customer assistance.

candidates.title: telecommunications manager
candidates.description: Telecommunications managers coordinate telecommunications staff activities for installing, troubleshooting, repairing and maintaining telecommunications equipment and infrastructure. They oversee the research, evaluation and implementation of new technologies and ensure a safe working environment for the employees. They supervise the inventory of supplies as well as user and customer assistance actions.

candidates.title: telecommunications analyst
candidates.description: Telecommunications analysts review, analyse and evaluate an organisation's telecommunications needs and systems. They provide training on the telecommunications system features and functionalities.

candidates.title: telecommunications equipment maintainer
candidates.description: Telecommunications equipment maintainers repair, install or maintain mobile or stationary radio transmitting, broadcasting, and receiving equipment, and two-way radio communications systems (cellular telecommunications, mobile broadband, ship-to-shore, aircraft-to-ground communications, radio equipment in service and emergency vehicles). They also focus on communication towers, antennas, amplifiers and connectors. They may test and analyse network coverage.

candidates.title: electronics engineer
candidates.description: Electronics engineers research, design, and develop electronic systems such as circuits, semiconductor devices, and equipment that use electricity as a source of power. They work with capacitators, transistors, diodes or resistors to create electronic circuits and applications of use in fields such as telecommunications, acoustics, instruments, and control.

candidates.title: electrical engineer
candidates.description: Electrical engineers design and develop electrical systems, electrical equipment, components, motors, and equipment with the feature of energy transmission. They engage in large scale projects such as the design and maintenance of power stations, and the distribution of power to smaller applications such as household appliances.

description: Network and Systems Engineer is responsible for designing, deploying, configuring, maintaining, and supporting an organisation’s IT infrastructure, including computer networks and systems. The role ensures network performance, reliability, and security through monitoring, fault diagnosis, system upgrades, and optimisation across LAN, WAN, cloud networks, and servers. It also involves analysing requirements, evaluating existing systems, and collaborating with teams to align IT infrastructure with business objectives.
tasks: Design and implement secure and efficient network infrastructures. Configure, maintain, and troubleshoot routers, switches, firewalls, servers, and virtual environments, and resolve network and system faults to minimise downtime. Monitor network performance and implement enhancements to optimise reliability and speed. Ensure compliance with security standards, and implement backup and disaster recovery procedures. Prepare and maintain technical documentation, procedures, and policies. Collaborate with information technology (IT) teams to support network projects and initiatives. Analyse and report on network security incidents and breaches.

candidates.title: ICT network engineer
candidates.description: ICT network engineers implement, maintain and support computer networks. They also perform network modelling, analysis, and planning. They may also design network and computer security measures. They may research and recommend network and data communications hardware and software.

candidates.title: ICT network technician
candidates.description: ICT network technicians install, maintain and troubleshoot networks, data communications equipment and network installed devices such as printers and storage area networks. They also analyse and fix network-related problems reported by users.

candidates.title: telecommunications engineer
candidates.description:
Telecommunications engineers design, build, test and maintain telecommunication systems and networks, including radio and broadcasting equipment.
They analyse customer needs and requirements, ensure that the equipment meets regulations, and prepare and present reports and proposals on telecommunication-related problems. Telecommunications engineers design and oversee the service delivery in all it's phases, supervising the installation and use of telecommunications equipment and facilities, preparing documentation and providing training for company staff once new equipment has been installed.

candidates.title: ICT network architect
candidates.description: ICT network architects design the topology and connectivity of ICT network such as hardware, infrastructure, communication and hardware components.

candidates.title: ICT network administrator
candidates.description: ICT network administrators maintain operation of a reliable, secure, and efficient data communications network, including LAN, WAN, intranet, and internet. They perform network address assignment, management and implementation of routing protocols such as ISIS, OSPF, BGP, routing table configurations and certain implementations of authentication. They perform maintenance and administration of servers (file servers, VPN gateways, intrusion detection systems), desktop computers, printers, routers, switches, firewalls, phones, IP communications, personal digital assistants, smartphones, software deployment, security updates and patches as well as a vast array of additional technologies inclusive of both hardware and software.

candidates.title: embedded systems security engineer
candidates.description: Embedded systems security engineers advise and implement solutions to control access to data and programs in embedded and connected systems. They help ensuring the safe operation of products with embedded systems and connected devices by being responsible for the protection and security of the related systems and design, plan and execute security measures accordingly. Embedded systems security engineers help to keep attackers at bay by implementing safeguards that prevent intrusions and breaches.

candidates.title: computer hardware engineer
candidates.description: Computer hardware engineers design and develop computer hardware systems and components, such as circuit boards, modems, and printers. They draught blueprints and assembly drawings, develop and test the prototypes, and supervise the production process.

candidates.title: ICT system analyst
candidates.description: ICT system analysts specify the system needs to meet the end user requirements. They analyse system functions in order to define their goals or purposes and to discover operations and procedures for accomplishing them most efficiently. They also design new IT solutions to improve business efficiency and productivity, produce outline designs and estimate costs of new systems, specify the operations the system will perform, and the way data will be viewed by the end user. They present the design to the users and work closely with the users to implement the solution.

description: Acoustic Engineer studies and applies the science of sound to design, analyse, and implement solutions for controlling noise, vibrations, and sound quality across various environments. They work on projects ranging from building acoustics and industrial facilities to electronic product development and entertainment venues, ensuring compliance with regulations and achieving optimal auditory performance. The role involves assessing sound, planning and installing systems, and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams to enhance acoustic outcomes and minimise noise impact.
tasks: Evaluate and analyse acoustic environments to design appropriate acoustic and sound system solutions. Select, configure, and calibrate audio and electronic equipment for optimal performance. Perform field measurements and troubleshoot acoustic and audio systems. Conduct noise and vibration impact assessments and propose mitigation solutions. Prepare technical documentation, reports, and compliance records. Provide on-site technical support for the installation, maintenance, and upgrading of acoustic systems. Advise on and ensure adherence to quality, safety, and regulatory standards. Participate in project planning and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams. Contribute to the research and development of acoustic technologies and materials.

candidates.title: acoustical engineer
candidates.description: Acoustical engineers study and apply the science of sound to various applications. They work in a wide range of areas including the consultation of the acoustics and elements affecting the transmission of sound in spaces for performances or recording activities. They can also consult on the levels of noise contamination for those activities that require compliance with standards on that matter.

candidates.title: audio production technician
candidates.description: Audio production technicians set up, prepare, check and maintain equipment in order to provide optimal sound quality for a live performance. They cooperate with road crew to unload, set up and operate sound equipment and instruments.

candidates.title: sound mastering engineer
candidates.description: Sound mastering engineers convert finished recordings to the desired format such as CD, vinyl and digital. They ensure the quality of the sound on all formats.

candidates.title: sound designer
candidates.description: Sound designers develop a sound design concept for a performance and supervise the execution of it. Their work is based on research and artistic vision. Their design is influenced by and influences other designs and must be conform with these designs and the overall artistic vision. Therefore, the designers work closely with artistic directors, operators and the artistic team. Sound designers prepare audio fragments to be used in a performance, which can involve recording, composing, manipulating and editing. Sound designers develop plans, cue lists and other documentation to support the operators and production crew. Sound designers sometimes also work as autonomous artists, creating sound art outside a performance context.

candidates.title: equipment engineer
candidates.description: Equipment engineers design and maintain the machinery and equipment in manufacturing facilities. They design machinery that adjusts to the manufacturing requirements and processes. Moreover, they envision the maintenance of the machines and equipment for uninterrupted functioning.

candidates.title: marine engineer
candidates.description: Marine engineers design, build, maintain and repair the hull, mechanical, electronic equipment and auxiliary systems such as engines, pumps, heating, ventilation, generator sets. They work on all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines.

candidates.title: mechanical engineer
candidates.description: Mechanical engineers research, plan and design mechanical products and systems and supervise the fabrication, operation, application, installation and repair of systems and products. They research and analyse data.

candidates.title: electronics engineer
candidates.description: Electronics engineers research, design, and develop electronic systems such as circuits, semiconductor devices, and equipment that use electricity as a source of power. They work with capacitators, transistors, diodes or resistors to create electronic circuits and applications of use in fields such as telecommunications, acoustics, instruments, and control.

description: Architect is responsible for conceptualising, designing, and overseeing the construction and renovation of buildings and structures across residential, commercial, industrial, and institutional sectors. They create functional, safe, sustainable, and aesthetically appealing designs, develop detailed plans and specifications, and collaborate with clients, engineers, contractors, and other stakeholders throughout all stages of a project. Their work ensures compliance with regulatory standards, building codes, and safety requirements, while monitoring construction, maintenance, and rehabilitation to deliver projects within budget and time constraints.
tasks: Lead and coordinate architectural projects from concept development to completion, covering planning, design, documentation, and implementation. Develop design concepts and prepare detailed architectural drawings, plans, blueprints, and three-dimensional renderings. Consult clients to understand their needs and provide recommendations on style, functionality, materials, and other design aspects. Ensure compliance with building codes, safety standards, and environmental regulations. Conduct site visits and inspections to monitor progress and ensure work aligns with designs. Coordinate with contractors, engineers, project managers, and other stakeholders to achieve project objectives. Monitor project schedules, budgets, and resource requirements to support timely and cost-effective project delivery. Inspect completed work and support handover processes to ensure quality and compliance with approved designs and specifications. Prepare and review project briefs, specifications, and related documentation. Review and refine architectural design approaches and project methods to improve design quality, efficiency, and innovation.

candidates.title: architect
candidates.description: Architects investigate, design, and oversee the construction and development of buildings, urban spaces, infrastructure projects, and social spaces. They design in accordance with the surroundings and regulations applicable in specific geographic areas, taking into account factors that include function, aesthetics, costs, and public health and safety. They are aware of social contexts and environmental factors, which include the relationships between people and buildings, and buildings and the environment. They engage in multidisciplinary projects aimed at developing the social fabric of a geographic area and advancing in social urbanism projects.

candidates.title: interior architect
candidates.description: Interior architects create plans of the interior of a home, building or other structure. They determine the specifications and distribution of the space. Interior architects combine an understanding of space with a sense for aesthetics in order to create a harmonious interior design. They draw architectural drawings using computer-aided equipment and software, or using conventional methods like paper and pen.

candidates.title: software architect
candidates.description: Software architects create the technical design and the functional model of a software system, based on functional specifications. They also design the architecture of the system or different modules and components related to the business' or customer requirements, technical platform, computer language or development environment.

candidates.title: naval architect
candidates.description: Naval architects design, build, maintain and repair all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines. They analyse floating structures and take various features into account for their designs such as the form, structure, stability, resistance, access and propulsion of hulls.

candidates.title: landscape architect
candidates.description: Landscape architects plan and design the construction of gardens and natural spaces. They determine the specifications and distribution of the space. Moreover, landscape architects research and analyse the potential of the landscape at all stages, scales and contexts of the development process, combining, an understanding of the natural space with a sense of aesthetics in order to create a harmonious space.

candidates.title: enterprise architect
candidates.description: Enterprise architects balance technological opportunities with business requirements. They also maintain a holistic view of the organisation's strategy, processes, information and ICT assets and link the business mission, strategy and processes to the ICT strategy.

candidates.title: architectural drafter
candidates.description: Architectural drafters make drawings of the specifications and ideas provided by architects. They draw architectural drawings using computer-aided equipment and software, or using conventional methods like paper and pen.

candidates.title: cloud architect
candidates.description: Cloud architects are responsible for converting the technical features of a project into the architecture to lead to the final product. To develop technical cloud strategy, they have in-depth knowledge of the architectural principles and services, assisting with cloud migration efforts, review workload architectures, and provide guidance on how to address high-risk issues. They typically perform in a pre-sales capacity and are often asked to deliver proof-of-concept projects, topical workshops, and lead implementation projects. They team up with DevOps engineers to build the appropriate technologies.

description: Architect Grade J9/J10 responsible for managing the implementation of government development projects from the planning stage through to project handover. Coordinate the preparation of designs, drawings, tender documents, and project handover. Monitor the physical and financial implementation of projects under construction and ensure that projects are completed with quality, within the planned cost and timeframe, and in accordance with the requirements and expectations of stakeholders.
tasks: Assisting the Project Management Group Leader in managing the implementation of projects under Categories II and III (Minimum Architect Fee Scale). Managing project implementation in accordance with the JKR Quality Management System (MS ISO 9001). Preparing the project Quality Implementation Plan (Q Plan), Amended Quality Plan, and periodic project monitoring reports. Preparing project budget projections in accordance with the prescribed cost ceiling. Coordinating the appointment and payment of consultants, and supervising group officers under their responsibility. Assisting the Director of Architecture in administering and managing the Architecture Unit, and controlling and coordinating the work of the unit staff. Providing architectural advisory services, including construction site assessment, planning, design, materials, services, and standards, and ensuring that works are completed on schedule and to high quality. Preparing Architectural Consultant appointment documents as approved by the Treasury for relevant projects. Ensuring that the latest directives and circulars are complied with by staff under their supervision.

candidates.description: Cloud architects are responsible for converting the technical features of a project into the architecture to lead to the final product. To develop technical cloud strategy, they have in-depth knowledge of the architectural principles and services, assisting with cloud migration efforts, review workload architectures, and provide guidance on how to address high-risk issues. They typically perform in a pre-sales capacity and are often asked to deliver proof-of-concept projects, topical workshops, and lead implementation projects. They team up with DevOps engineers to build the appropriate technologies.

description: Landscape Architect plans, designs, and oversees the development of gardens, natural spaces, and landscapes, ensuring projects are both functional and aesthetically appealing. They manage the full design process from conception to completion, coordinate with architects, engineers, contractors, and other stakeholders to maintain design integrity, comply with regulations, and meet quality, budget, and schedule requirements. They also conduct site visits, resolve issues during construction, and integrate sustainable practices while keeping abreast of current design trends.
tasks: Plan and design landscape development projects, including parks, streetscapes, recreational areas, gardens, and natural spaces. Prepare detailed landscape drawings, project documentation, and submissions for approvals, tenders, and contracts. Coordinate with clients, consultants, contractors, and other stakeholders to resolve project and technical issues and maintain design integrity. Conduct site evaluations and inspections to monitor progress and ensure compliance with designs. Consult with clients to determine landscape design style, type, and specifications. Ensure projects comply with regulatory requirements and project specifications. Present design changes, material selections, and cost estimates to clients and other relevant stakeholders. Manage project progress and oversight to maintain quality standards, budgets, and schedules.

candidates.title: landscape architect
candidates.description: Landscape architects plan and design the construction of gardens and natural spaces. They determine the specifications and distribution of the space. Moreover, landscape architects research and analyse the potential of the landscape at all stages, scales and contexts of the development process, combining, an understanding of the natural space with a sense of aesthetics in order to create a harmonious space.

candidates.title: landscape designer
candidates.description: Landscape designers design and create outdoor public areas, landmarks, structures, parks, gardens and private gardens to achieve environmental, social-behavioral, or aesthetic outcomes.

candidates.title: architect
candidates.description: Architects investigate, design, and oversee the construction and development of buildings, urban spaces, infrastructure projects, and social spaces. They design in accordance with the surroundings and regulations applicable in specific geographic areas, taking into account factors that include function, aesthetics, costs, and public health and safety. They are aware of social contexts and environmental factors, which include the relationships between people and buildings, and buildings and the environment. They engage in multidisciplinary projects aimed at developing the social fabric of a geographic area and advancing in social urbanism projects.

candidates.title: landscape gardener
candidates.description: Landscape gardeners plan, construct, renovate and maintain parks, gardens and public green spaces.

candidates.title: interior landscaper
candidates.description: Interior landscapers design, install, manage and maintain indoor green spaces to customer requirements.

candidates.title: interior architect
candidates.description: Interior architects create plans of the interior of a home, building or other structure. They determine the specifications and distribution of the space. Interior architects combine an understanding of space with a sense for aesthetics in order to create a harmonious interior design. They draw architectural drawings using computer-aided equipment and software, or using conventional methods like paper and pen.

candidates.title: land planner
candidates.description: Land planners visit sites in order to create projects and plans for land usage and development. They collect and analyse data about the land. Land planners provide advice on the efficiency and safety of development plans.

candidates.title: land surveyor
candidates.description: Land surveyors determine, by means of specialised equipment, the distances and positions of points at the surface of sites for construction purposes. They use measurements of the specific aspects of construction sites, such as electricity, distance measurements, and metal structure volumes to create architectural drawings and develop construction projects.

description: Landscape Architect Grade J9 planning, preparing, coordinating, and implementing public parks and recreational facilities as well as landscapes nationwide, and ensuring that they are well designed and constructed, practical, and safe. Formulating policies, Acts, guidelines, and information related to landscape planning, construction, and management. Coordinating the planning of landscape development programmes through the use of appropriate information system support services and computerisation with accessible information. Ensuring that landscape development complies with prescribed standards, guidelines, and specifications. Providing professional landscape development planning and technical advisory services. Providing advisory services and efficient landscape maintenance manuals for each landscape development project implemented. Preparing plans to develop and update landscape conservation programmes aimed at conserving, preserving, and enriching the nation’s landscape resources.
tasks: Studying and preparing the Department’s development programmes within the Five-Year Malaysia Plan (MP) and prepares policies, guidelines, acts, and legislation related to landscape development. Preparing the Landscape Master Plan (10-year planning) for nationwide landscape development. Studying and planning research requirements in landscape and related fields for landscape conservation. Executing and coordinating landscape research programmes in line with design and industry requirements. Planning and coordinating the development of landscape and public park maintenance programmes nationwide. Identifying potential applications of information technology and promotes the adoption of suitable current IT to support planning, development, and landscape management activities undertaken by all divisions/units within the department. Planning and coordinating the implementation of landscape promotion programmes through landscape competitions, exhibitions, celebratory events such as National Landscape Day, mass media programmes, publications, and other related activities. Preparing monitoring, planning, and evaluation works for the development needs of public parks and recreational facilities nationwide. Identifying spatial planning issues and development project requirements in landscape projects. Providing technical advisory services to all government sectors on planning, design preparation, and landscape construction aspects. Assisting in preparing cost estimates, reviewing construction costs, and preparing cost planning for construction and development projects.

description: Commercial Products Designer is responsible for conceptualising, designing, and developing consumer products. They create designs for mass, batch, or bespoke production, preparing specifications and prototypes while considering materials, manufacturing methods, cost efficiency, and quality standards. The role involves collaboration with marketing, engineering, manufacturing, and design professionals to ensure the product meets market trends, client requirements, and practical usability.
tasks: Research consumer behaviour, market trends, and design forecasts to inform product development. Develop design concepts for commercial products based on client requirements, market trends, and practical usability. Produce sketches, detailed drawings, and three-dimensional models using specialised software. Create prototypes, conduct user testing, and refine designs based on feedback and technical constraints. Specify materials, finishes, and production methods, and ensure designs are manufacturable and meet quality standards. Prepare technical documentation, specifications, and production information to support manufacturing. Collaborate with engineers, suppliers, production teams, clients, and other stakeholders throughout the design process. Coordinate design timelines, cost considerations, and compliance with regulatory and company standards. Review sample production and product quality, and support presentation of design concepts where required.

candidates.title: industrial designer
candidates.description: Industrial designers work out ideas and develop them into designs and concepts for a wide variety of manufactured products. They integrate creativity, aesthetics, production feasibility, and market relevance in the design of new products.

candidates.title: production designer
candidates.description: Production designers are responsible for the complete look (style, colouring and locations) of television programmes, series, motion pictures and commercials. They create the visual concept for the entire production such as set design, lighting, costumes and camera angles. Production designers work together with the director, designers and oversee the art department. They also create sketches, drawings, do colouring and location research and advise props and stage settings to the director.

candidates.title: textile product developer
candidates.description: Textile product developers innovate and perform product design of apparel textiles, home textiles, and technical textiles (e.g. agriculture, safety, construction, medicine, mobile tech, environmental protection, sports, etc.). They apply scientific and technical principles to develop innovative textile products.

candidates.title: footwear product developer
candidates.description: Footwear product developers provide interface between design and production. They engineer the footwear prototypes previously created by designers. They select, design or re-design lasts and footwear components, make patterns for uppers, linings and bottom components, and produce technical drawings for a various range of tools, e.g. cutting dies, mould, etc. They also produce and evaluate footwear prototypes, grade and produce sizing samples, perform required tests for samples and confirm the customer’s qualitative and pricing constraints.

candidates.title: clothing fashion designer
candidates.description: Clothing fashion designers create concepts and make sketches of their creative ideas by hand or by using software. They analyse and interpret fashion trends in order to propose new ideas with high aesthetical value. They perform forecasting and market research to put together collections. They build collection lines by operating mood or concept boards, colour palettes, materials, drawings and sketches considering among others ergonomical criteria, etc.

candidates.title: leather goods product developer
candidates.description: Leather goods product developers perform and interface between design and actual production. They analyse and study designer’s specifications and transform them into technical requirements, updating concepts to manufacturing lines, selecting or even designing components and selecting materials. Leather goods product developers also perform the pattern engineering, namely they make patterns manually and produce technical drawings for various range of tools, especially cutting. They evaluate prototypes, performing required tests for samples and confirming the customer’s quality requirements and pricing constrains.

candidates.title: automotive designer
candidates.description: Automotive designers create model designs in 2D or 3D and prepare isometric drawings and graphics. They work closely with computer hardware engineers to develop hardware designs for the next generation of automotive applications including advanced driver-assistance and vehicle-to-everything systems. They re-evaluate vehicle design, materials and manufacturing technologies, anticipating changes to vehicle architecture and power management, vehicle features and seating functionality and safety.

candidates.title: product development manager
candidates.description: Product development managers coordinate the development of new products from beginning to end. They receive briefings and start envisioning the new product considering design, technical and cost criteria. They conduct research on market needs and create prototypes of new products for untapped market opportunities. Product development managers also improve and boost technological quality.

description: Green Technology Design Professional plans, designs, and implements sustainable energy and infrastructure solutions that incorporate environmentally friendly and energy-efficient technologies. They work across solar, biomass, hydro, and other green systems, advising organisations on strategies to optimise performance, meet environmental objectives, and comply with regulatory standards. They collaborate with engineers, architects, and project stakeholders to develop innovative designs for buildings, industrial facilities, and infrastructure projects, ensuring cost-effective, sustainable outcomes aligned with national green policies and global best practices.
tasks: Conduct site inspections and feasibility and sustainability assessments to inform green technology design solutions. Design energy-efficient systems for solar thermal, biomass, hydro, and other renewable technology applications using specialised software and modelling tools. Prepare technical drawings, diagrams, plans, and reports for design proposals, approvals, and green certification applications. Specify and recommend sustainable materials, components, and production methods to ensure system efficiency, durability, and environmental compliance. Collaborate with engineers, project managers, and stakeholders to integrate designs and refine technical specifications. Ensure all designs comply with safety, environmental, and regulatory standards. Support installation, commissioning, and testing activities to verify system performance. Monitor operational systems and evaluate performance, efficiency, and environmental impact for continuous improvement. Advise clients and project teams on sustainability practices, carbon reduction strategies, and regulatory compliance. Develop project proposals and conduct cost and risk assessments for green technology projects.

candidates.title: green ICT consultant
candidates.description: Green ICT consultants advise organisations on their green ICT strategy and its implementation in the most effective and efficient manner to allow the organisation to reach their short, mid, and long term ICT environmental objectives.

candidates.title: renewable energy engineer
candidates.description: Renewable energy engineers research alternative sources of energy in order to design systems for renewable energy production. They strive to optimise energy production from renewable sources, and reduce production expenses and environmental strain. They design systems which focus on energy sustainability and efficiency.

candidates.title: environmental engineer
candidates.description: Environmental engineers integrate environmental and sustainable measures in the development of projects of various natures. They seek to preserve natural resources and natural sites. They work together with engineers from other fields to envision all the implications that projects might have in order to design ways to conserve natural reserves, prevent pollution, and deploy sanitary measures.

candidates.title: solar energy engineer
candidates.description: Solar energy engineers design systems which generate electrical energy from sunlight, such as photovoltaic systems. They design and construct systems which optimise the energy output from solar power, and the sustainability of the production process of solar systems.

candidates.title: environmental expert
candidates.description: Environmental experts search for technological solutions to tackle environmental problems. They detect and analyse environmental issues and develop new technological production processes to counter these problematic issues. They research the effect of their technological innovations and present their findings in scientific reports.

candidates.title: ICT environmental manager
candidates.description: ICT environmental managers know the green ICT legal framework, understand the role of the ICT network configurations in the economy and energy resources deployment and evaluate the impact of CO2 footprint of each ICT resource in the organisation's network. They plan and manage the implementation of environmental strategies for ICT networks and systems by conducting applied research, developing organisational policy, and devising strategies to meet sustainability targets. They ensure that the whole organisation uses ICT resources in a way that is as friendly as possible for the environment.

candidates.title: energy engineer
candidates.description: Energy engineers design new, efficient and clean ways to produce, transform, and distribute energy to improve environmental sustainability and energy efficiency. They deal with the extraction of energy through natural resources, such as oil or gas, or renewable and sustainable sources, such as wind or solar power.

candidates.title: energy systems engineer
candidates.description: Energy systems engineers supervise the energy conversion and distribution processes. They analyse the energy supply and consumption efficiency developing new ways to improve the existing processes, taking into account both the technical and the financial aspects. They also study the environmental impact of energy usage and combine the production of renewable energy in the current power systems.

description: Town Planner develops, assesses, and manages land use plans, policies, and regulations to guide the sustainable physical development of towns, cities, and regions. They analyse community and regional needs, evaluate environmental, social, and economic factors, and prepare detailed reports and layouts to propose practical development solutions. Working closely with authorities, developers, and stakeholders, they ensure urban growth aligns with legal requirements, infrastructure efficiency, and environmental sustainability.
tasks: Conduct site assessments to evaluate land suitability, zoning, and environmental, social, and economic factors. Prepare detailed development and land use plans, proposals, and technical documentation in compliance with national and local planning guidelines. Conduct feasibility studies and review environmental and social planning considerations for proposed developments. Coordinate with government agencies, municipal councils, planning committees, and stakeholders to secure permits and approvals. Engage in public consultations, gather community feedback, and incorporate sustainable planning principles into planning strategies. Compile, analyse, and present site, community, and project data through reports, maps, and visual documentation for stakeholders. Inspect development sites and implementation progress to ensure compliance with approved plans and planning requirements. Monitor ongoing development projects to ensure alignment with approved plans and long-term strategic goals. Advise on planning, layout designs, and development recommendations to support decision-making.

candidates.title: land planner
candidates.description: Land planners visit sites in order to create projects and plans for land usage and development. They collect and analyse data about the land. Land planners provide advice on the efficiency and safety of development plans.

candidates.title: urban planner
candidates.description: Urban planners create development plans for towns, urban areas, cities, and regions. They research the needs of the community or the region (economic, social, transport) and evaluate other parameters such as sustainability in order to present solid programs aimed at the improvement of the site.

candidates.title: interior planner
candidates.description: Interior planners help clients in planning their interiors for commercial and private use.

candidates.title: transport planner
candidates.description: Transport planners develop and implement policies in order to improve transport systems, taking into account the social, environmental and economic factors. They collect and analyse traffic data using statistical modelling tools.

candidates.title: purchase planner
candidates.description: Purchase planners organise the continuous supply with goods out of existing contracts.

candidates.title: smart city consultant
candidates.description: Smart city consultants advise on sustainability solutions for the implementation of smart city initiatives. They execute environmental projects based on smart services, advanced technology, and digital transformation in urban areas. In addition, Smart city consultants develop business plans to attract investment resources, identify challenges and sustainable business opportunities, as well as synergies between public and private stakeholders or clients.

candidates.title: wedding planner
candidates.description: Wedding planners assist with all logistical details required concerning their client's wedding ceremony. Based on their client's requirements, they make arrangements for floral decorations, wedding venue and catering, guest invitations, etc., coordinating activities both before and during the wedding.

candidates.title: food production planner
candidates.description: Food production planners prepare production plans, evaluate all the variables in the process and strive to ensure that production objectives be achieved.

description: Traffic Engineer plans, designs, and manages transportation systems to ensure the safe, efficient, and sustainable movement of people and goods. They analyse current traffic conditions, forecast future travel demands, and develop solutions to reduce congestion, improve road safety, and enhance public transport efficiency. Working with government agencies, developers, and engineering teams, they implement traffic control measures, optimise road layouts and signalling, and contribute to integrated transport strategies that support regional and national development goals.
tasks: Conduct traffic and transportation studies, including traffic impact assessments, traffic volume and road capacity analysis, travel pattern assessment, and modelling of future traffic conditions using specialised software. Carry out site visits and inspections to assess road conditions and verify that traffic-related works comply with approved plans, specifications, and quality standards. Design and optimise traffic signal systems, road networks, and transport infrastructure improvements to improve safety and traffic flow. Develop and recommend traffic management strategies and traffic calming measures to reduce congestion and enhance road safety. Assess the transport-related environmental implications of transportation and urban development projects in support of sustainable planning. Prepare technical reports, layout plans, and presentations to communicate traffic findings and recommendations to stakeholders. Coordinate with city councils, transport authorities, and public agencies to obtain approvals and support the implementation of traffic plans. Ensure compliance with national transportation regulations, local authority requirements, and urban planning guidelines. Advise on development planning by integrating traffic and transportation considerations into layout plans and related proposals.

candidates.title: transport planner
candidates.description: Transport planners develop and implement policies in order to improve transport systems, taking into account the social, environmental and economic factors. They collect and analyse traffic data using statistical modelling tools.

candidates.title: transport engineer
candidates.description: Transport engineers design and set the engineering specifications for the construction and development of roadways and transport infrastructure. They apply engineering concepts and knowledge for developing sustainable and efficient modes of transportation ranging from roads to canals, railways, and airports.

candidates.title: automotive engineer
candidates.description: Automotive engineers design and oversee the manufacturing process and operation of motor vehicles such as motorcycles, cars, trucks, buses and their respective engineering systems. They design new vehicles or mechanical parts, supervise modifications and resolve technical problems. They make sure the designs comply with cost specifications and other constraints. They also conduct research studying environmental, energy and safety aspects.

candidates.title: air traffic manager
candidates.description: Air traffic managers coordinate the planning of ground control, the maintenance of the aircrafts, and the handling of customers. They strive for the most efficient use of resources in directing the aircraft. They manage safety, quality, and risks in everyday work. They also plan and compare performance with other air navigation service providers.

candidates.title: civil engineer
candidates.description: Civil engineers design, plan, and develop technical and engineering specifications for infrastructure and construction projects. They apply engineering knowledge in a vast array of projects, from the construction of infrastructure for transportation, housing projects, and luxury buildings, to the construction of natural sites. They design plans that seek to optimise materials and integrate specifications and resource allocation within the time constraints.

candidates.title: road operations manager
candidates.description: Road operations managers oversee day-to-day road transportation processes, managing processes, and strive to meet customer expectations.

candidates.title: health and safety engineer
candidates.description: Health and safety engineers design objects and programs by combining engineering principles and health and safety requirements. They envision the protection and well-being of the people using designed objects or performing work under designed health and safety programs. They assess facilities and the risks that they might pose (e.g. contaminant materials, ergonomics, handling of dangerous substances, etc.) in order to design and improve health and safety measures.

candidates.title: air traffic safety technician
candidates.description: Air traffic safety technicians provide technical support regarding the safety of air traffic control and navigation systems. They design, maintain, install and operate these systems both in the airport and on board the aeroplane according to regulations.

description: Urban and Regional Planner is responsible for developing and implementing land use strategies and policies for urban, suburban, and rural areas to promote sustainable and efficient development. They conduct research, analyse data, and engage with public and private stakeholders to plan new communities, revitalise infrastructure, and guide the design of residential, recreational, institutional, and landscape areas. Their work addresses social, environmental, and economic considerations, ensures compliance with regulatory frameworks, and contributes to improving quality of life while managing challenges such as urban sprawl, traffic, and climate resilience.
tasks: Conduct site assessments and research on land use patterns, population growth, and environmental conditions to assess development feasibility. Prepare development and land use plans, zoning regulations, and planning policies to support sustainable urban and regional growth. Evaluate planning and development proposals for compliance with zoning laws, planning requirements, building regulations, and environmental regulations. Collaborate with architects, engineers, environmental scientists, government officials, and other stakeholders to support planning decisions. Prepare reports, technical documents, and visual presentations to support planning analysis and decision-making. Monitor development implementation and site progress to ensure compliance with approved plans and planning requirements. Participate in long-term strategic planning initiatives, including transport, housing, infrastructure, and green development projects. Advise on planning proposals, layout plans, and development strategies for urban and regional areas. Coordinate and oversee the implementation and integration of urban and regional development projects.

candidates.title: urban planner

They research the needs of the community or the region (economic, social, transport) and evaluate other parameters such as sustainability in order to present solid programs aimed at the improvement of the site.

candidates.title: regional development policy officer
candidates.description: Regional development policy officers research, analyse and develop regional development policies. They implement policies that aim at reducing regional disparities by fostering economic activities in a region and structural changes such as supporting multi-level governance, rural development and improvement of infrastructure. They work closely with partners, external organisations or other stakeholders and provide them with regular updates.

candidates.title: interior planner
candidates.description: Interior planners help clients in planning their interiors for commercial and private use.

candidates.title: government planning inspector
candidates.description: Government planning inspectors monitor the development and implementation of government plans and policies, as well as processing planning and policy proposals, and performing inspections of planning procedures.

candidates.title: purchase planner
candidates.description: Purchase planners organise the continuous supply with goods out of existing contracts.

candidates.title: food production planner
candidates.description: Food production planners prepare production plans, evaluate all the variables in the process and strive to ensure that production objectives be achieved.

role_title: Urban and Rural Planning Officer Grade J9
description: Urban and Rural Planning Officer Grade J9 coordinating the Urban Structure Plan Study, Safe City Study, Kajian Petunjuk Bandar Sejahtera (MURNInet), research, and other planning studies, implementing e-Pemajuan of the Urban Planning Division, developing a GIS database for planning data, as well as collecting information on planning progress and urban development, controlling development to ensure uniformity, comfort, and safety in land use activities, layout preparation, and design of quality and effective public facilities, and creating a comfortable environment for the community.
tasks: Assisting to coordinate studies related to Urban Planning, such as the Safe City Implementation Study in Putrajaya. Assisting to coordinate planning studies and review preparation of policy papers related to urban planning aspects. Assisting to coordinate preparation of the Urban Structure Plan Study. Assisting to coordinate collection of development planning information and data, and coordinate planning of public facility development in line with population growth. Assisting to coordinate public complaints through CRM (Controller) for the Urban Planning Division. Assisting to coordinate updating of information in the local Corporation Community Portal. Preparing improvements to the Departmental Manual Prosedur Kerja (MPK) and update the Client Charter Unit. Preparing the ISO Development Plan for the Urban Planning Department. Providing planning reviews on studies conducted by Putrajaya Corporation and studies carried out by external agencies such as JPBD Peninsular Malaysia and other local authorities. Managing the Department Resource Centre and assist to update the unit Annual Work Targets (SKT) for officers. Updating individual Desk File (FM).

candidates.title: urban planner
candidates.description: Urban planners create development plans for towns, urban areas, cities, and regions. They research the needs of the community or the region (economic, social, transport) and evaluate other parameters such as sustainability in order to present solid programs aimed at the improvement of the site.

candidates.title: land planner
candidates.description: Land planners visit sites in order to create projects and plans for land usage and development. They collect and analyse data about the land. Land planners provide advice on the efficiency and safety of development plans.

candidates.title: regional development policy officer
candidates.description: Regional development policy officers research, analyse and develop regional development policies. They implement policies that aim at reducing regional disparities by fostering economic activities in a region and structural changes such as supporting multi-level governance, rural development and improvement of infrastructure. They work closely with partners, external organisations or other stakeholders and provide them with regular updates.

candidates.title: community development officer
candidates.description: Community development officers develop plans to improve quality of life in local communities. They investigate and assess the community's issues and needs, manage resources, and develop implementation strategies. They communicate with the community for investigation purposes, and to inform the community on development plans.

candidates.title: agricultural policy officer
candidates.description: Agricultural policy officers analyse and identify agricultural policy issues and develop plans for improvement and new policy implementation. They write reports and presentations in order to communicate and acquire support for the policies from government officials and the public. They also communicate with professionals in agriculture for research and information purposes and perform administrative duties.

candidates.title: government planning inspector
candidates.description: Government planning inspectors monitor the development and implementation of government plans and policies, as well as processing planning and policy proposals, and performing inspections of planning procedures.

candidates.title: strategic planning manager
candidates.description: Strategic planning managers create, together with a team of managers, the strategic plans of the company as a whole, and provide coordination in the implementation per department. They help to interpret the overall plan and create a detailed plan for each one of the departments and branches. They ensure consistency in the implementation.

candidates.title: housing policy officer
candidates.description: Housing policy officers research, analyse and develop housing policies which enable affordable and adequate housing for all. They implement these policies to improve the housing situation of the population by measures such as building affordable housing, supporting people to buy real estate and improving conditions in existing housing. Housing policy officers work closely with partners, external organisations or other stakeholders and provide them with regular updates.

description: Cartographer applies scientific, technological, and artistic methods to collect, analyse, and interpret spatial data, producing accurate and visually informative maps. Their work supports urban planning, transportation, environmental monitoring, and disaster management, using both traditional techniques and modern Geographic Information Systems (GIS). They determine the position of natural and constructed features, boundaries, and other spatial elements, creating and updating maps and charts for government, private, and research applications.
tasks: Collect and compile geographic and spatial data from surveys, satellite imagery, aerial photographs, and other relevant sources. Interpret and analyse spatial data using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and mapping software to identify geographic patterns and trends. Produce accurate and visually informative topographic, thematic, and other maps in digital or print formats. Maintain and update mapping databases, maps, and charts to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compliance with standards. Collaborate with urban planners, engineers, and environmental consultants to support mapping and spatial planning requirements. Apply photogrammetry and survey measurement techniques in the preparation and refinement of maps and spatial data outputs. Ensure maps and related outputs comply with mapping standards and legal requirements.

candidates.title: cartographer
candidates.description: Cartographers create maps by combining various scientific informations depending of the purpose of the map (e.g. topographic, urban, or political maps). They combine the interpretation of mathematical notes and measurements with the aesthetics and visual depiction of the site for developing the maps. They may also work on developing and improving geographic information systems and may perform scientific research within cartography.

candidates.title: geographer
candidates.description: Geographers are scholars who study human and physical geography. Depending on their specialisation, they study political, economical and cultural aspects of humanity contained within human geography. Moreover, they study land formations, soils, natural frontiers, and water flows contained in physical geography.

candidates.title: geographic information systems specialist
candidates.description: Geographic information systems specialists use specialised computer systems, engineering measures, and geological concepts to process land, geographic, and geospatial information into visually detailed digital maps and geomodels of a reservoir. They convert technical information like soil density and properties into digital representations to be used by engineers, governments and interested stakeholders.

candidates.title: hydrographic surveyor
candidates.description: Hydrographic surveyors measure and map, by means of specialised equipment, marine environments. They collect scientific data in order to study the underwater topography and morphology of bodies of water.

candidates.title: oceanographer
candidates.description: Oceanographers study and perform research on matters related to the sea and oceans. Oceanographers divide their expertise in different branches of research which are physical oceanographers whose research focus on waves and tides, chemical oceanographers whose study address the chemical constitution of sea waters, and geological oceanographer whose research refers to the bottom of seas and their plaques.

candidates.title: hydrographic surveying technician
candidates.description: Hydrographic surveying technicians perform oceanographic and surveying operations in marine environments. They assist hydrographic surveyors, using specialised equipment to map and study underwater topography and morphology of bodies of water. They assist in the installation and deployment of hydrographic and surveying equipment and report about their work.

candidates.title: radiographer
candidates.description: Radiographers use a range of technologies to examine, treat and care for patients. They work in the fields of Medical Imaging, Radiotherapy and Nuclear Medicine and apply ionising radiation, ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and radioactive sources.

candidates.title: demographer
candidates.description: Demographers study a variety of parameters related with population. They develop, based on their observations, statistical analyses on the evolutions and changes of births, elderly, marriage and divorce, employment, mortality, immigration and related matters.

description: Surveyor is responsible for measuring, mapping, and analysing land and site data to support planning, design, construction, and operational activities. They establish control points, boundaries, alignments, and levels, verify the accuracy of measurements and drawings, and resolve dimensional discrepancies. Their work includes liaising with consultants and site teams, preparing survey records, conducting as-built surveys, and using advanced instruments and technology to ensure precise and reliable data across diverse environments.
tasks: Conduct field surveys to establish property boundaries, land features, control points, alignments, and levels, ensuring accuracy. Prepare and maintain maps, sketches, survey records, and reports based on survey findings for clients and stakeholders. Analyse survey data and verify measurements and drawings for accuracy and compliance with standards. Use advanced technology such as Global Positioning System (GPS), total stations, and Geographic Information System (GIS) software to enhance survey precision. Coordinate with architects, engineers, consultants, site teams, and government authorities to integrate survey data into planning and construction documents. Supervise field teams and ensure proper calibration and maintenance of survey instruments. Assess and describe land surfaces, and conduct as-built surveys for property, construction, and development purposes.

candidates.title: land surveyor
candidates.description: Land surveyors determine, by means of specialised equipment, the distances and positions of points at the surface of sites for construction purposes. They use measurements of the specific aspects of construction sites, such as electricity, distance measurements, and metal structure volumes to create architectural drawings and develop construction projects.

candidates.title: soil surveying technician
candidates.description: Soil surveying technicians analyse soil by carrying out technical surveying tasks, using soil surveying techniques. They focus on the process of classifying soil types and other soil properties. Soil surveying technicians operate surveying equipment and utilise programs to retrieve and interpret relevant data, and perform computations as required.

candidates.title: surveying technician
candidates.description: Surveying technicians carry out technical surveying tasks. They assist surveyors, architects or engineers in surveying related technical tasks such as mapping land, creating construction drawings and operating precise measuring equipment.

candidates.title: mine surveyor
candidates.description: Mine surveyors prepare and maintain mining plans in line with statutory and management requirements. They keep records of the physical progress of mining operations and of ore or mineral production.

candidates.title: real estate surveyor
candidates.description: Real estate surveyors undertake research in order to assess the value of property for tax purposes. They investigate multiple properties at once, using accurate appraisal techniques. They provide their services usually to local and governmental bodies for taxation reasons.

candidates.title: hydrographic surveyor
candidates.description: Hydrographic surveyors measure and map, by means of specialised equipment, marine environments. They collect scientific data in order to study the underwater topography and morphology of bodies of water.

candidates.title: marine surveyor
candidates.description: Marine surveyors inspect vessels intended for operations in maritime or open sea waters. They ensure that vessels and equipment follow the regulations laid down by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO). They may also act as third parties for the review of offshore facilities and construction projects.

candidates.title: quantity surveyor
candidates.description: Quantity surveyors have under their helm complete management of the cost involved in building and construction projects from the inception of the project until the delivery. They strive for an efficient use of the resources whilst keeping an eye on quality, quality standards, and client's requirements.

description: Geospatialist Grade J9 responsible for the preparation of electronic map designs, thematic maps as well as limited and unrestricted topographic maps required by the government and the public for the purposes of defense, national development, resource management, education and administration.
tasks: Leading units within the State Survey and Mapping Section/Department that manage the Geospatial Database. Collecting, processing, managing, and analysing geographic, spatial, and attribute data on a regular basis. Designing menus and integrating spatial and attribute data to facilitate system user operations. Establishing a systematic, effective, and efficient management and updating system for attribute databases to facilitate data retrieval, control data redundancy, and ensure data validity. Executing data entry and management to enhance data provision, security, consistency, and storage reliability. Preparing presentation displays and editing information in complete and visually appealing formats. Reviewing and ensuring the accuracy of GIS information data, and managing the security of digital GIS files. Performing digital GIS data backups and ensuring compliance with ICAO requirements in GIS data usage. Planning, preparing technical and financial proposals, and managing the implementation of service improvements and system/equipment upgrades in the Cartography Laboratory. Managing the budget for service delivery, production of MACRES mapping products and publications, and upgrading of systems and equipment in the Cartography Laboratory. Evaluating current technologies for MACRES mapping product and publication production, and subsequently preparing technical and financial proposals for the adoption of appropriate technologies at MACRES. Preparing scopes and specifications, and managing the procurement of supplies/services related to the cartography laboratory through direct purchase, quotations, or tenders. Responsible for the maintenance and procurement of cartographic systems/equipment and shared-use equipment under the management of the cartography laboratory. Certifying the specifications of MACRES outputs for adoption by other branches. Managing safety procedures, quality control, copyright, and restricted material usage for MACRES mapping outputs and publications.

candidates.title: geographic information systems specialist
candidates.description: Geographic information systems specialists use specialised computer systems, engineering measures, and geological concepts to process land, geographic, and geospatial information into visually detailed digital maps and geomodels of a reservoir. They convert technical information like soil density and properties into digital representations to be used by engineers, governments and interested stakeholders.

candidates.title: geographer
candidates.description: Geographers are scholars who study human and physical geography. Depending on their specialisation, they study political, economical and cultural aspects of humanity contained within human geography. Moreover, they study land formations, soils, natural frontiers, and water flows contained in physical geography.

candidates.title: geophysicist
candidates.description: Geophysicists study the physical characteristics of the earth and apply physical measurements to geological situations. Geophysicists use the principles of gravity, seismicity and electromagnetics to identify the structure and composition of the earth.

candidates.title: geotechnician
candidates.description: Geotechnicians collect and process rock and soil samples for geomechanical testing. They also describe the quality of rock mass, including structure, discontinuities, colour and weathering. Mine geotechnicians may measure the size of underground openings. They report the collected information to geologists and engineers as required.

candidates.title: geochemist
candidates.description: Geochemists study the characteristics and chemical elements in minerals, rocks and soils, and how they interact with hydrological systems. They coordinate the collection of samples and indicate the suite of metals to be analysed.

candidates.title: cartographer
candidates.description: Cartographers create maps by combining various scientific informations depending of the purpose of the map (e.g. topographic, urban, or political maps). They combine the interpretation of mathematical notes and measurements with the aesthetics and visual depiction of the site for developing the maps. They may also work on developing and improving geographic information systems and may perform scientific research within cartography.

candidates.title: geologist
candidates.description: Geologists research the materials that form the earth. Their observations depend on the purpose of the research. Depending on their specialisation, geologists study how the Earth has been shaped over time, its geological layers, the quality of minerals for mining purposes, earthquakes and volcanic activity for private services, and similar phenomena.

candidates.title: geography teacher secondary school
candidates.description: Geography teachers at secondary schools provide education to students, commonly children and young adults, in a secondary school setting. They are usually subject teachers, specialised and instructing in their own field of study, geography. They prepare lesson plans and materials, monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate the students' knowledge and performance on the subject of geography through assignments, tests and examinations.

description: Surveyor Grade J9 responsible for carrying out survey works in the fields of topographic mapping, geodetic, utility mapping, and cadastral, covering standard control cross-section measurements, control measurements, double wall measurements, land acquisition measurements, urban and rural area measurements, sports courts, high accuracy investigation measurements, and state and international boundaries. Providing training, preparing reports and work statements for the work team, and other administrative tasks related to the department.
tasks: Coordinating section administrative work, activity planning, and staff task allocation, and ensuring that tasks are executed in accordance with departmental policies. Planning, implementing projects, and coordinating the collection and processing of surveying, mapping, and cadastre data. Conducting reviews, analyses, and quality control of all surveying, mapping, and cadastre data processing work. Preparing branch/unit annual budget estimates and requirements. Responsible for the security of all surveying, mapping, and cadastre data documents and records. Conducting surprise inspections, scheduled visits, supervisory visits, and fieldwork testing visits from time to time. Representing the section in providing explanations and technical advisory services to relevant parties regarding section activities. Managing and administering the Quantity Surveying Unit, supervising subordinate officers, and managing the secretariat for designated meetings. Reviewing tender, quotation, and project contract documents prepared by Quantity Surveyors. Preparing monthly and annual reports on unit/branch activities and progress, as well as staff performance reports.
