candidates.title: marine surveyor
candidates.description: Marine surveyors inspect vessels intended for operations in maritime or open sea waters. They ensure that vessels and equipment follow the regulations laid down by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO). They may also act as third parties for the review of offshore facilities and construction projects.

description: Poster Designer creates and produces visually compelling posters for marketing, educational, informational, or artistic purposes. They develop designs that effectively communicate messages to target audiences, supporting branding and promotional efforts. The role involves combining creative design with communication objectives, collaborating with marketing teams, art directors, and clients, and overseeing production to ensure quality and consistency.
tasks: Develop design concepts and layouts for posters based on client briefs and marketing objectives. Consult with clients to determine design requirements, messaging, and target audience. Select colours, images, typography, and visual elements to achieve the intended design impact. Create and edit poster designs using graphic design software for print and digital distribution. Ensure designs comply with brand guidelines and campaign objectives. Revise and refine designs based on client or stakeholder feedback. Prepare final artwork and files to ensure high-quality output for print or digital use. Coordinate with printers, production teams, and digital marketing teams to ensure accurate production and delivery. Research design trends and visual styles to maintain relevant and effective poster designs. Produce mock-ups or sample designs for review and approval prior to final production.

candidates.title: costume designer
candidates.description: Costume designers develop a costume design concept for events, a performance, a movie or a television program. They supervise the execution of it. Their work is based on research and artistic vision. Their design is influenced by and influences other designs and must be conform with these designs and the overall artistic vision. Therefore, the designers work closely with artistic directors, operators and the artistic team. Costume designers develop sketches, design drawings, patterns or other documentation to support the workshop and performance crew.

candidates.title: fashion designer
candidates.description: Fashion designers work on designs for the haute couture and/or ready-to-wear, high street fashion markets, and more generally on items of clothing and fashion ranges. Fashion designers can operate in a specialised area, such as sportswear, childrenswear, footwear or accessories.

candidates.title: production designer
candidates.description: Production designers are responsible for the complete look (style, colouring and locations) of television programmes, series, motion pictures and commercials. They create the visual concept for the entire production such as set design, lighting, costumes and camera angles. Production designers work together with the director, designers and oversee the art department. They also create sketches, drawings, do colouring and location research and advise props and stage settings to the director.

candidates.title: graphic designer
candidates.description: Graphic designers create text and images to communicate ideas. They make visual concepts by hand or using computer software, intended for publishing in paper or online media such as advertisements, websites, and magazines.

candidates.title: industrial designer
candidates.description: Industrial designers work out ideas and develop them into designs and concepts for a wide variety of manufactured products. They integrate creativity, aesthetics, production feasibility, and market relevance in the design of new products.

candidates.title: decorative painter
candidates.description: Decorative painters design and create visual art on different kinds of surfaces such as pottery, casings, glass and fabric. They use diverse materials and a variety of techniques to produce decorative illustrations ranging from stenciling to free-hand drawing.

candidates.title: clothing fashion designer
candidates.description: Clothing fashion designers create concepts and make sketches of their creative ideas by hand or by using software. They analyse and interpret fashion trends in order to propose new ideas with high aesthetical value. They perform forecasting and market research to put together collections. They build collection lines by operating mood or concept boards, colour palettes, materials, drawings and sketches considering among others ergonomical criteria, etc.

candidates.title: footwear designer
candidates.description: Footwear designers perform fashion trends analysis, forecasting and market research, create footwear concepts and build collection lines by operating mood or concept boards, colour palettes, materials, drawings and sketches etc. They conduct the sampling process, make footwear prototypes and samples for presentations aimed to promoting the footwear concepts and collections. They identify the range of materials and components, define the design specifications by collaborating with the technical team and review the footwear samples, prototypes, and collections.

description: Designer Grade B9 responsible for graphic and multimedia design works, exhibitions, and outdoor publicity for government campaigns in visual and display formats for arts-related works, in an effort to market government information and policies to the public. Responsible for creating designs for presentation and production props. Coordinate, plan, and prepare design of publication materials and FINAS trophies. Responsible for ensuring presentation stages, preparation of guest reception ceremonies, and coordinating promotional materials to states, in magazines, on radio, and at Media Conferences.
tasks: Managing and administers the unit, including leading and supervising unit members under their charge. Preparing financial requirements for the unit’s annual budget to fund strategies, programmes, and activities. Managing unit expenditures and procurement, ensuring payments are made accurately, promptly, and in accordance with regulations and circulars. Planning and implementing government campaign strategies through effective visual communication. Preparing monthly and annual activity reports, as well as various unit working papers. Conducting studies and identifies the latest methods and technologies in visual communication/design. Supervising projects to ensure divisional objectives are achieved, and makes decisions as a reference expert. Assisting in managing the production of multimedia/publicity materials to support campaigns, programmes, and activities. Responsible for executing integrated/graphic/multimedia exhibitions in accordance with planned concepts. Providing guidance, coaching, and training to subordinate staff to enhance the quality of innovative and creative work outputs.

candidates.title: art director
candidates.description: Art directors shape the visual layout of a concept. They create innovative designs, develop artistic projects and manage the cooperation between all aspects involved. Art directors may perform creative work in theatre, marketing, advertising, video and motion picture, fashion or online companies. They ensure that the work performed is visually appealing to audiences.

candidates.title: production designer
candidates.description: Production designers are responsible for the complete look (style, colouring and locations) of television programmes, series, motion pictures and commercials. They create the visual concept for the entire production such as set design, lighting, costumes and camera angles. Production designers work together with the director, designers and oversee the art department. They also create sketches, drawings, do colouring and location research and advise props and stage settings to the director.

Fashion designers can operate in a specialised area, such as sportswear, childrenswear, footwear or accessories.

candidates.title: textile designer
candidates.description: Textile designers conceptualise textile products considering visual communication and functional performance.

candidates.title: clothing fashion designer
candidates.description: Clothing fashion designers create concepts and make sketches of their creative ideas by hand or by using software. They analyse and interpret fashion trends in order to propose new ideas with high aesthetical value. They perform forecasting and market research to put together collections. They build collection lines by operating mood or concept boards, colour palettes, materials, drawings and sketches considering among others ergonomical criteria, etc.

description: Marine Engineer is responsible for the design, operation, maintenance, and repair of mechanical, electrical, and electronic systems on ships and marine vessels. This includes propulsion systems, auxiliary machinery, power generation units, and other critical onboard equipment. They ensure that all systems function safely, efficiently, and in compliance with maritime regulations, oversee technical operations, manage engineering crews, and perform emergency repairs to maintain the seaworthiness of the vessel and the safety of its crew and cargo.
tasks: Design, install, inspect, diagnose, and maintain propulsion, auxiliary, and other ship machinery and onboard mechanical, electrical, and electronic systems. Supervise and manage the engineering team to ensure efficient and safe ship operations. Ensure compliance with maritime regulations, safety standards, and environmental conventions. Manage fuel consumption, bunkering operations, and onboard energy efficiency. Coordinate repairs, refits, technical tests, and emergency responses for ship machinery and systems. Maintain accurate operational records, logs, and engineering documentation. Provide technical advice during vessel construction, modifications, and dry docking activities. Collaborate with naval architects, shipyards, and other professionals on vessel operations and maintenance.

candidates.title: marine engineer
candidates.description: Marine engineers design, build, maintain and repair the hull, mechanical, electronic equipment and auxiliary systems such as engines, pumps, heating, ventilation, generator sets. They work on all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines.

candidates.title: marine chief engineer
candidates.description: Marine chief engineers are responsible for the entire technical operations of the vessel including engineering, electrical, and mechanical divisions. They are the head of the entire engine department aboard the ship and have overall responsibility for all technical operations and equipment on-board the ship. Marine chief engineers collaborate on security, survival and health care on board and observe the national and international standards of application.

candidates.title: marine engineering technician
candidates.description: Marine engineering technicians carry out technical functions to help marine engineers with the design, development, manufacturing and testing processes, installation and maintenance of all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines. They also conduct experiments, collect and analyse data and report their findings.

candidates.title: marine mechanic
candidates.description: Marine mechanics are in charge of the engines and mechanical parts of the vessel and replace defective equipment and parts. They communicate with other crew members on the operational level. Marine mechanics maintain and repair the engines and other machinery of vessels such as boilers, generators and electrical equipment.

candidates.title: marine electronics technician
candidates.description: Marine electronics technicians lay out, install and repair electronic systems and equipment in vessels. They assemble electronic components and wiring according to blueprints and assembly drawings.

candidates.title: ship duty engineer
candidates.description: Ship duty engineers share responsibility for most of the content of the ship's hull. They ensure operation of the main engines, steering mechanism, electrical generation and other major subsystems. They communicate with the ship chief engineer to perform technical operations.

candidates.title: marine electrician
candidates.description: Marine electricians install, maintain and repair electrical and electronic systems in vessels such as air conditioning systems, lamps, radios, heating systems, batteries, electrical wiring and alternators. They use diagnostic testing equipment to inspect vessels and find faults. To do repair work, they use hand tools and specialised electrical instruments and machines.

candidates.title: ship assistant engineer
candidates.description: Ship assistant engineers assist the ship chief engineer and the ship duty engineer in the operations of the ship's hull. They support the operation of the main engines, steering mechanism, electrical generation and other major subsystems. They communicate with maritime engineers about the performance of technical operations. They also ensure appropriate safety and regulatory standards compliance and are able to take on higher level positions if needed.

description: Naval Architect is responsible for designing, constructing, maintaining, and repairing marine vessels and structures, including ships, submarines, yachts, ferries, and offshore platforms. They apply engineering principles to ensure vessels are safe, efficient, stable, and environmentally sustainable, considering hull form, structure, stability, resistance, and propulsion. Their work integrates mechanical, electrical, and structural systems, often collaborating with marine engineers and other specialists throughout the vessel’s lifecycle.
tasks: Develop detailed designs and plans for marine vessels and structures in compliance with technical, safety, and regulatory standards. Conduct hydrostatic, hydrodynamic, and structural calculations to assess vessel stability, resistance, propulsion, and overall performance. Simulate and evaluate vessel behaviour using Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and engineering software to support design validation. Collaborate with construction teams and other specialists to ensure vessel designs are accurately implemented during construction. Provide technical advice on vessel performance, safety, stability, and design efficiency throughout the vessel lifecycle. Oversee vessel modifications and retrofits to ensure continued compliance, safety, and performance improvement. Ensure vessel and marine structure designs comply with international maritime standards and classification requirements.

candidates.title: naval architect
candidates.description: Naval architects design, build, maintain and repair all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines. They analyse floating structures and take various features into account for their designs such as the form, structure, stability, resistance, access and propulsion of hulls.

candidates.title: marine engineer
candidates.description: Marine engineers design, build, maintain and repair the hull, mechanical, electronic equipment and auxiliary systems such as engines, pumps, heating, ventilation, generator sets. They work on all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines.

candidates.title: architect
candidates.description: Architects investigate, design, and oversee the construction and development of buildings, urban spaces, infrastructure projects, and social spaces. They design in accordance with the surroundings and regulations applicable in specific geographic areas, taking into account factors that include function, aesthetics, costs, and public health and safety. They are aware of social contexts and environmental factors, which include the relationships between people and buildings, and buildings and the environment. They engage in multidisciplinary projects aimed at developing the social fabric of a geographic area and advancing in social urbanism projects.

candidates.title: marine engineering drafter
candidates.description: Marine engineering drafters convert the marine engineers’ designs into technical drawings usually using software. Their drawings detail dimensions, fastening and assembling methods and other specifications used in the manufacture of all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines.

candidates.title: marine painter
candidates.description: Marine painters work in the shipbuilding industry and are responsible for completing the blasting, painting, hull washing and cleaning, scraping and protection jobs of all varieties as assigned by supervisors. They follow set guidelines, processes and procedures to ensure successful completion of work.

candidates.title: shipwright
candidates.description: Shipwrights build and repair small type of water vessels from pleasure craft to naval vessels. They prepare preliminary sketches and create templates. They use hand and power tools to construct smaller boat themselves or supervise a team of shipbuilders. They also construct cradles and slipways for the ship’s construction, transportation, launching and slipping. Depending on the vessels, they might work with different materials such as metal, wood, fibreglass, aluminium etc.

candidates.title: ship assistant engineer
candidates.description: Ship assistant engineers assist the ship chief engineer and the ship duty engineer in the operations of the ship's hull. They support the operation of the main engines, steering mechanism, electrical generation and other major subsystems. They communicate with maritime engineers about the performance of technical operations. They also ensure appropriate safety and regulatory standards compliance and are able to take on higher level positions if needed.

candidates.title: interior architect
candidates.description: Interior architects create plans of the interior of a home, building or other structure. They determine the specifications and distribution of the space. Interior architects combine an understanding of space with a sense for aesthetics in order to create a harmonious interior design. They draw architectural drawings using computer-aided equipment and software, or using conventional methods like paper and pen.

description: Hovercraft Pilot is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of hovercrafts over water, land, ice, and mud. They navigate varying terrains and weather conditions, ensure the safety of passengers or cargo, monitor and operate onboard systems, and maintain communication with control stations, making real-time decisions to ensure secure operations. They may also oversee vessel navigation and related duties while in port.
tasks: Conduct pre-departure inspections of the hovercraft, including basic checks of structural condition and onboard systems, to ensure operational readiness. Navigate and command the hovercraft safely along assigned routes. Maintain communication with relevant control stations to support safe and efficient operations. Oversee the safe loading of passengers or cargo and confirm readiness for transit. Carry out safety procedures and respond to emergencies in accordance with operational requirements. Record operational activities, incidents and voyage details accurately for reporting and review. Identify mechanical or system issues during operation and report them to the maintenance team for follow-up action. Ensure compliance with registration, safety and navigation requirements during hovercraft operations.

candidates.title: aircraft pilot
candidates.description: Aircraft pilots control and navigate aircraft. They operate the mechanical and electrical systems of the aircraft and transport people, mail and freight.

candidates.title: helicopter pilot
candidates.description: Helicopter pilots fly helicopters in order to transport passengers and cargo from one place to another. They plan flights using aeronautical charts and navigation instruments. Prior to departure, they inspect helicopters following checklists to detect leaking hydraulic fluid, inoperative control, low fuel level, or other unsafe conditions.

candidates.title: commercial pilot
candidates.description: Commercial pilots navigate flight of fixed-wing and multi-engine aircrafts for the transport of passengers and cargo.

candidates.title: maritime pilot
candidates.description: Maritime pilots are mariners who guide ships through dangerous or congested waters, such as harbours or river mouths. They are expert ship handlers who possess detailed knowledge of local waterways.

candidates.title: co-pilot
candidates.description: Co-pilots are responsible for assisting captains by monitoring the flight instruments, handling radio communications, watching for air traffic, and taking over for the pilot as needed. They adhere to the pilot's commands, flight plans, and regulations and procedures of aviation national authorities, companies, and airports.

candidates.title: air force pilot
candidates.description: Air force pilots operate aircrafts in combat missions, patrol missions, or search and rescue missions. They ensure aircraft maintenance, and communicate with air force bases and other vessels to ensure safety and efficiency in operations.

candidates.title: drone pilot
candidates.description: Drone pilots remotely operate unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). They navigate the drone as well as activate other equipment as cameras, sensors as LIDARS to calculate distances, or any other instrumentation.

candidates.title: airline transport pilot
candidates.description: Airline transport pilots fly large aircrafts with a maximum take-off weight of more than 5700 kilograms, to transport passengers, mail, or freight on long or short-haul flights for leisure, business or commercial purposes. They have the overall responsibility for the safe and efficient operation of aircrafts and the safety of crew and passengers.

description: Port Captain is responsible for supervising and coordinating vessel operations at ports or terminals, ensuring compliance with national and international regulations. The role oversees cargo handling, port logistics, and operational efficiency while maintaining safety standards, acting as a key liaison between shipping companies, port authorities, and vessel crews to ensure the safe and timely arrival, departure, and handling of ships.
tasks: Coordinate vessel arrival and departure activities to ensure safe and timely port operations. Ensure compliance with maritime safety and environmental regulations, and oversee safety inspections. Oversee the safe and efficient loading and unloading of cargo. Monitor crew operational activities to ensure adherence to safety protocols and regulations. Liaise with port and maritime authorities for vessel clearance, documentation, and operational coordination. Manage emergency situations, including oil spills or accidents, and implement corrective actions. Maintain vessel operational, safety, and compliance records. Perform administrative duties, including documentation and operational reporting.

candidates.title: ship captain
candidates.description: Ship captains are in charge of a vessel for the transportation of goods and passengers, operating in offshore and coastal waters. The size of the vessel can range from a small vessel to a cruise liner depending on the tonnage that they are certified to sail. Ship captains have vast experience with ships and their operation, and are likely to have worked their way through the ranks of other ship-related positions.

candidates.title: skipper
candidates.description: Skippers are the highest authority on-board or on inland waterways, they are in charge of the vessel and are held responsible for the safety and well being of the clients and crew. They are licensed by the responsible authority and will determine the operations of the vessel at any time. They are the ultimate instance responsible for the crew, the ship, the cargo and/or passengers, and the voyage.

candidates.title: port coordinator
candidates.description: Port coordinators manage operations of traffic division for port authorities. They enforce rules and regulations, such as the berthing of ships, handling and storing of cargo, and the use of port facilities. They direct policing and cleaning activities of the harbour department land, streets, buildings, and water areas. Port coordinators also ensure that activities concerning revenue are documented and submitted to the accounting division. They advise port authorities on rates and revisions of port tariff, and solicit steamship companies to use port facilities. They direct activities concerned with compiling daily and annual ship and cargo statistics.

candidates.title: army captain
candidates.description: Army captains aid in the supervision of large units of soldiers, as well as perform planning and strategic duties in tactical operations. They also ensure equipment maintenance and provide support in logistic matters as well as support during operations.

candidates.title: fleet commander
candidates.description: Fleet commanders ensure that naval vessels are ready for inclusion in operations, and are maintained in compliance with rules and regulations. They also supervise naval personnel and are responsible for the operations of the naval service.

candidates.title: fisheries boatmaster
candidates.description: Fisheries boatmasters operate fishing vessels in coastal waters performing operations at the deck and engine. They control the navigation as well as capture and conservation of fish within the established boundaries in compliance with national and international regulations.

candidates.title: sailor
candidates.description: Sailors assist the ship captain and any crew higher in hierarchy to operate ships. They dust and wax furniture and polish wood trim, sweep floors and decks, and polish brass and other metal parts. They inspect, repair, and maintain sails and rigging, and paint or varnish surfaces. They make emergency repairs to the auxiliary engine. Sailors may stow supplies and equipment and record data in log, such as weather conditions and distance travelled.

candidates.title: deck officer
candidates.description: Deck officers or mates perform the watch duties on board of vessels like determining the course and speed, manoeuvring to avoid hazards, and continuously monitoring the vessels position using charts and navigational aids. They maintain logs and other records tracking the ship's movements. They ensure that the proper procedures and safety practices are followed, check that equipment is in good working order, and oversee the loading and discharging of cargo or passengers. They supervise crew members engaged in maintenance and the primary upkeep of the vessel.

description: Ship Navigator is responsible for safely directing vessels from one location to another, ensuring compliance with maritime laws and port regulations. The role involves planning routes, interpreting weather conditions, operating navigational equipment, and supervising crew to maintain the vessel’s operational integrity. The position focuses on safe passage, hazard avoidance, and the accurate documentation of voyages.
tasks: Prepare detailed voyage plans using navigational charts and instruments. Supervise and adjust the ship’s course and speed according to the passage plan, weather conditions, tides, and ocean currents. Monitor radar, Global Positioning System (GPS), and other navigational systems to ensure positional accuracy. Operate and ensure the readiness of navigation and communication equipment. Coordinate with port authorities for berthing, docking, and related operations. Lead and supervise deck crew in navigation-related tasks. Ensure navigational safety and compliance with maritime laws and port regulations. Maintain accurate navigational records and voyage documentation.

candidates.title: ship captain
candidates.description: Ship captains are in charge of a vessel for the transportation of goods and passengers, operating in offshore and coastal waters. The size of the vessel can range from a small vessel to a cruise liner depending on the tonnage that they are certified to sail. Ship captains have vast experience with ships and their operation, and are likely to have worked their way through the ranks of other ship-related positions.

candidates.title: maritime pilot
candidates.description: Maritime pilots are mariners who guide ships through dangerous or congested waters, such as harbours or river mouths. They are expert ship handlers who possess detailed knowledge of local waterways.

candidates.title: fleet commander
candidates.description: Fleet commanders ensure that naval vessels are ready for inclusion in operations, and are maintained in compliance with rules and regulations. They also supervise naval personnel and are responsible for the operations of the naval service.

candidates.title: skipper
candidates.description: Skippers are the highest authority on-board or on inland waterways, they are in charge of the vessel and are held responsible for the safety and well being of the clients and crew. They are licensed by the responsible authority and will determine the operations of the vessel at any time. They are the ultimate instance responsible for the crew, the ship, the cargo and/or passengers, and the voyage.

candidates.title: ship planner
candidates.description: Ship planners manage the performance of a vessel. They ensure the safety of the vessel and its cargo, its operationality and link available vessels to available cargos in order to maximise the profitability of the voyages. They ensure that each container ship is loaded to its optimal capacity, while keeping berth times and handling costs to a minimum. They also plan the maintenance and overhaul of the ship, as well as the crew needed.

candidates.title: ship duty engineer
candidates.description: Ship duty engineers share responsibility for most of the content of the ship's hull. They ensure operation of the main engines, steering mechanism, electrical generation and other major subsystems. They communicate with the ship chief engineer to perform technical operations.

candidates.title: ship assistant engineer
candidates.description: Ship assistant engineers assist the ship chief engineer and the ship duty engineer in the operations of the ship's hull. They support the operation of the main engines, steering mechanism, electrical generation and other major subsystems. They communicate with maritime engineers about the performance of technical operations. They also ensure appropriate safety and regulatory standards compliance and are able to take on higher level positions if needed.

candidates.title: ship pilot dispatcher
candidates.description: Ship pilot dispatchers coordinate ships entering or leaving port. They write orders showing name of ship, berth, tugboat company, and time of arrival or departure, and notify the maritime pilot of assignment. They obtain receipts of pilotage from the pilot upon return from ship. Ship pilot dispatchers also record charges on receipt, using tariff book as guide, compile reports of activities, such as number of ships piloted and charges made, and keep records of ships entering port, showing owner, name of ship, displacement tonnage, agent, and country of registration.

description: Marine Superintendent (Deck) oversees and manages marine operations for a fleet of vessels, ensuring safe, efficient, and regulation-compliant operations. The role includes conducting inspections and audits, maintaining vessel performance and seaworthiness, managing safety and operational protocols, and ensuring adherence to schedules and cost efficiency. They also serve as the primary link between shipboard personnel and shore-based management to facilitate smooth communication and operations.
tasks: Ensure vessels comply with international and local maritime regulations and are prepared for inspections and audits. Liaise with ship captains to enforce company policies and safety procedures. Oversee navigational safety and vessel operations to ensure safe and efficient fleet performance. Review and update safety management systems to ensure compliance with operational standards. Monitor crew readiness and certification compliance, and support training coordination as required. Coordinate dry-docking, repairs, and maintenance to maintain vessel seaworthiness and operational readiness. Investigate incidents and implement corrective actions as required. Evaluate vessel performance and recommend improvements to enhance operational efficiency. Maintain accurate vessel records and statutory documentation for compliance, inspections, and audits. Coordinate ship safety, operational matters, and communication between vessels and shore-based management to ensure smooth operations.

candidates.title: marine chief engineer
candidates.description: Marine chief engineers are responsible for the entire technical operations of the vessel including engineering, electrical, and mechanical divisions. They are the head of the entire engine department aboard the ship and have overall responsibility for all technical operations and equipment on-board the ship. Marine chief engineers collaborate on security, survival and health care on board and observe the national and international standards of application.

candidates.title: fisheries boatmaster
candidates.description: Fisheries boatmasters operate fishing vessels in coastal waters performing operations at the deck and engine. They control the navigation as well as capture and conservation of fish within the established boundaries in compliance with national and international regulations.

candidates.title: stevedore superintendent
candidates.description: Stevedore superintendents supervise and monitor the freight handling and longshore labor in a dockyard to maximise productivity. They manage the loading and unloading of cargo and monitor the safety of the work area. Stevedore superintendents may also investigate incidents and prepare accident reports.

candidates.title: marine mechanic
candidates.description: Marine mechanics are in charge of the engines and mechanical parts of the vessel and replace defective equipment and parts. They communicate with other crew members on the operational level. Marine mechanics maintain and repair the engines and other machinery of vessels such as boilers, generators and electrical equipment.

candidates.title: vessel operations coordinator
candidates.description: Vessel operations coordinators manage chartered vessels' transit and performance optimizing the schedulers but also assessing the capabilities and the risks for vessels according to the different types of cargo such as crude oil or other chemical cargos. They make sure all necessary certifications are according to the regulations and all employees have up-to-date passports and licenses. Vessel operations coordinators schedule and maintain records of vessels' maintenance. At the operational level they have contact with the customers, following up customer complains, identifying new opportunities and providing customers with solutions.

candidates.title: marine electrician
candidates.description: Marine electricians install, maintain and repair electrical and electronic systems in vessels such as air conditioning systems, lamps, radios, heating systems, batteries, electrical wiring and alternators. They use diagnostic testing equipment to inspect vessels and find faults. To do repair work, they use hand tools and specialised electrical instruments and machines.

candidates.title: maritime instructor
candidates.description: Maritime instructors teach all those occupationally piloting a boat or a ship, such as skippers and ship captains, how to operate their inland water boats or maritime ships according to regulations. They teach their students theory and techniques on how to optimally pilot, steer and navigate, and maintain their specific boat or ship, observe and evaluate the students' practice. They also focus on non-steering related subjects such as customer service (in case of person transportation) and safety measure regulations.

description: Shipping Executive is responsible for managing and coordinating the full shipping and logistics processes, ensuring the timely dispatch and delivery of goods while maintaining accurate documentation for local and international shipments. They liaise with freight forwarders and logistics providers, ensure compliance with customs and regulatory requirements, and resolve delivery or scheduling issues. The role also involves optimising shipment workflows, maintaining shipping records, and coordinating with internal departments, while representing the ship owner in foreign ports to oversee necessary formalities.
tasks: Coordinate and schedule shipments with internal departments, freight forwarders, and logistics providers to ensure timely dispatch and delivery. Prepare, verify, and manage shipping documents, including invoices, packing lists, bills of lading, and customs declarations. Arrange transportation and book freight services for local and international shipments. Track shipments and provide timely status updates to relevant stakeholders. Ensure compliance with import and export regulations, and coordinate customs clearance requirements. Maintain accurate shipping records and transaction documentation for auditing and compliance purposes. Resolve shipment delays, discrepancies, and scheduling issues promptly. Negotiate shipping rates with freight carriers and recommend cost-effective shipping arrangements. Evaluate freight carrier performance and recommend improvements to shipping and logistics processes. Represent the ship owner in foreign ports and oversee insurance, licensing, and other required formalities.

candidates.title: shipping agent
candidates.description: Shipping agents represent the ship owner in a foreign port. They make sure customs is cleared in a timely manner so that the cargo doesn't have to stay too long in the port. Shipping agents also ensure that insurance, licences and other formalities are in order.

candidates.title: freight transport dispatcher
candidates.description: Freight transport dispatchers receive and transmit reliable messages, track vehicles and equipment, and record other important information. They oversee the planning operations of dispatching by coordinating different modes of transport. Freight transport dispatchers structure routes or services and determine the appropriate mode of transport. They are also responsible for equipment and vehicle maintenance and workers dispatching. The freight transport dispatchers provide the legal and contractual documentation for the transporting parties.

candidates.description: Logistics and distribution managers take decisions on logistic services, operations and provisions. They take internal and external variables into consideration for effective and successful organisational logistic services. They give appropriate support to all the activities of the supply chain from the beginning to the end. These professionals organise the storage and distribution of goods and ensure that the right products are delivered to the right location on time and at a good cost.

description: Marine Officer Grade AL9 responsible for managing ship registration, ship safety, maritime security, seafarers and port affairs, maritime technical training, development projects as well as conducting studies and evaluations of international conventions and maritime legislation, managing the implementation of training, research and statistical data management, particularly in relation to the shipping and sea transportation industry.
tasks: Implementing the registration, licensing, and ownership of ships and boats in Malaysia, as well as the prescribed auditing and verification activities. Conducting ship inspections, safety and security management audits, and ensuring compliance with international conventions such as the International Maritime Organization (IMO), SOLAS, and MARPOL 73/78. Conducting marine casualty investigations and inquiries for the purpose of prosecution in court. Managing and implementing maritime traffic management, and monitors navigational traffic compliance through the Vessel Traffic System (VTS). Managing and implementing the prevention, control, and response actions against marine pollution from ships in Malaysian waters in accordance with international and national legislation. Implementing hydrographic surveys, data processing, QA/QC, and the production and maintenance of a hydrographic database for the safety of navigation channels. Managing the issuance of competency certificates, recognition certificates, safe manning documents, medical practitioner certificates, modular certificates, and navigator licenses. Managing port operations, the gazettement of port limits, vessel arrivals and departures, as well as ship-to-ship transfer activities. Preparing budget proposals and manages annual expenditure. Examining and evaluating international technical requirements by representing the nation at international meetings for the purpose of compliance with international conventions of importance to the country.

candidates.title: navy officer
candidates.description: Navy officers command missions during conflict and peace times, and supervise training and development of their teams. They supervise combat operations of their team, as well as aid missions, and patrolling missions to ensure peace-keeping. Often they collaborate on a regular basis with the HR department of the HQCS for the best planning of the future needs.

candidates.title: marine cargo inspector
candidates.description: Marine cargo inspectors investigate all baggage and freight listed on the ship's manifest. They are responsible for checking the condition of the cargo and verifying the cargo's documentation and compliance with rules and regulations. Marine cargo inspectors analyse the vessels' capabilities, the fuel compartments, the safety equipment and the specific licenses required.

candidates.title: marine firefighter
candidates.description: Marine firefighters are responsible for emergency response in case of a fire outbreak or other hazardous situations in marine environments. They actively respond to contain fires and the outbreak of other hazardous on vessels, docks and other marine facilities. They ensure the marine installation complies with health and safety regulations. They also regulate the clean-up of the scene and assess the damage.

Marine chief engineers collaborate on security, survival and health care on board and observe the national and international standards of application.

candidates.title: marine engineer
candidates.description: Marine engineers design, build, maintain and repair the hull, mechanical, electronic equipment and auxiliary systems such as engines, pumps, heating, ventilation, generator sets. They work on all types of boats from pleasure crafts to naval vessels, including submarines.

candidates.title: marine electronics technician
candidates.description: Marine electronics technicians lay out, install and repair electronic systems and equipment in vessels. They assemble electronic components and wiring according to blueprints and assembly drawings.

description: Pilot operates an aeroplane, helicopter, or other aircraft to transport passengers, cargo, or provide specialised aerial services. They plan and manage flight routes, conduct thorough pre-flight inspections, and control the aircraft during all phases of flight while maintaining communication with air traffic control to ensure safety and compliance with aviation regulations. The role also involves responding effectively to in-flight emergencies, keeping accurate flight records, and staying updated on safety procedures and regulatory changes.
tasks: Fly and navigate aeroplanes, helicopters, and other aircraft to transport passengers, cargo, or provide specialised aerial services. Conduct pre-flight safety checks, review weather conditions, and prepare flight plans. Monitor and manage aircraft systems, adjusting flight paths for weather and traffic conditions. Communicate with air traffic control during take-off, flight, and landing. Handle in-flight emergencies calmly and efficiently. Inspect aircraft before flight and verify maintenance records to ensure operational readiness and safety. Coordinate with maintenance crews to report and address mechanical issues affecting flight operations. Maintain accurate flight records and complete required operational documentation. Complete post-flight documentation and report operational or safety-related issues. Ensure the safety of passengers, crew, and equipment throughout the flight.

candidates.title: aircraft pilot
candidates.description: Aircraft pilots control and navigate aircraft. They operate the mechanical and electrical systems of the aircraft and transport people, mail and freight.

candidates.title: co-pilot
candidates.description: Co-pilots are responsible for assisting captains by monitoring the flight instruments, handling radio communications, watching for air traffic, and taking over for the pilot as needed. They adhere to the pilot's commands, flight plans, and regulations and procedures of aviation national authorities, companies, and airports.

candidates.title: air force pilot
candidates.description: Air force pilots operate aircrafts in combat missions, patrol missions, or search and rescue missions. They ensure aircraft maintenance, and communicate with air force bases and other vessels to ensure safety and efficiency in operations.

candidates.title: commercial pilot
candidates.description: Commercial pilots navigate flight of fixed-wing and multi-engine aircrafts for the transport of passengers and cargo.

candidates.title: helicopter pilot
candidates.description: Helicopter pilots fly helicopters in order to transport passengers and cargo from one place to another. They plan flights using aeronautical charts and navigation instruments. Prior to departure, they inspect helicopters following checklists to detect leaking hydraulic fluid, inoperative control, low fuel level, or other unsafe conditions.

candidates.title: maritime pilot
candidates.description: Maritime pilots are mariners who guide ships through dangerous or congested waters, such as harbours or river mouths. They are expert ship handlers who possess detailed knowledge of local waterways.

candidates.title: private pilot
candidates.description: Private pilots operate non-commercial airplanes for leisure with a limited amount of seats and engine horsepower. They also provide private transport for people.

candidates.title: drone pilot
candidates.description: Drone pilots remotely operate unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). They navigate the drone as well as activate other equipment as cameras, sensors as LIDARS to calculate distances, or any other instrumentation.

description: Flight Instructor is responsible for training new and experienced pilots to obtain licences and enhance their flying skills. They provide instruction on aviation theory, flight planning, navigation, regulations, and conduct both simulator and in-flight practical sessions, ensuring students develop the competence to operate aircraft safely. The role requires monitoring student progress, providing feedback, and complying with standards set by the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia and other aviation regulatory bodies.
tasks: Prepare and deliver classroom lessons on aviation theory, flight planning, navigation, and aviation regulations. Conduct simulator sessions to teach aircraft handling and emergency procedures. Perform instructional flights with student pilots, ensuring safe and effective learning. Evaluate student performance and provide feedback on training progress. Maintain and update student training records and instructional materials. Develop and update training curricula and programmes in line with regulatory and industry standards. Ensure compliance with aviation regulations and safety protocols throughout training activities. Coordinate with other instructors and administrative personnel to support smooth training operations. Make instructional flight decisions to ensure the safety of students, crew, and equipment.

candidates.title: flight instructor
candidates.description: Flight instructors train both new and experienced pilots seeking to gain licences or experience in flying new aircraft, how to properly operate an aircraft according to regulations. They teach their students both the theory and practice of how to optimally fly and maintain an airplane, and they observe and evaluate student technique. They also focus on the regulations relating to operational and safety procedures specific to different (commercial) airline aircraft.

candidates.title: air traffic instructor
candidates.description: Air traffic instructors train people in all the matters regarding with the operations in air navigation services such as the management of flight traffic and the communication for navigation in aerodromes. They teach all the directives issued by air traffic control for the purpose of passing to trainees the sense of safety and expeditious flow of air traffic.

candidates.title: cabin crew instructor
candidates.description: Cabin crew instructors teach trainees all the matters regarding the operations in aircraft cabins. They teach, depending on the type of airplane, the operation carried out in the aircraft, the pre and post flight checks, the safety procedures, the service equipment, and client service procedures and formalities.

candidates.title: maritime instructor
candidates.description: Maritime instructors teach all those occupationally piloting a boat or a ship, such as skippers and ship captains, how to operate their inland water boats or maritime ships according to regulations. They teach their students theory and techniques on how to optimally pilot, steer and navigate, and maintain their specific boat or ship, observe and evaluate the students' practice. They also focus on non-steering related subjects such as customer service (in case of person transportation) and safety measure regulations.

candidates.title: flight operations officer
candidates.description: Flight operations officers compile flight information to expedite movement of aircraft between and through airports. They compile aircraft dispatch data such as scheduled arrival and departure times at checkpoints and scheduled stops, amount of fuel needed for flight, and maximum allowable gross take-off and landing weight.

candidates.title: aircraft pilot
candidates.description: Aircraft pilots control and navigate aircraft. They operate the mechanical and electrical systems of the aircraft and transport people, mail and freight.

candidates.title: flight attendant
candidates.description: Flight attendants perform a variety of personal services conducive to the safety and comfort of airline passengers during flight. They greet passengers, verify tickets, and direct passengers to assigned seats. They prepare reports after landing describing how the flight went in terms of operations, procedures, and anomalies.

candidates.title: aviation safety officer
candidates.description: Aviation safety officers plan and develop safety procedures for aviation companies. They study safety regulations and restrictions relative to aviation company operations. Hence, they direct activities of personnel in order to safeguard the application of safety measures in compliance with regulations.

description: Aircraft Design Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, and evaluating aircraft structures, systems, and components to ensure safety, performance, and efficiency. They conduct research, develop design specifications, perform simulations and tests, and collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to transform concepts into functional aircraft, missiles, or spacecraft, while ensuring compliance with aerospace industry standards and regulations.
tasks: Develop detailed designs for aircraft structures, systems, and components using specialised Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software. Conduct simulations and engineering analyses to evaluate aerodynamics, material strength, structural integrity, performance, and efficiency. Ensure aircraft designs comply with aviation safety regulations, aerospace industry standards, and relevant environmental requirements. Analyse engineering proposals and technical data to assess design feasibility, production requirements, and implementation constraints. Collaborate with manufacturing and multidisciplinary engineering teams to ensure designs are practical, functional, and efficient for production. Plan and conduct experimental, prototype, and stress tests to validate aircraft designs and support design improvements. Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including design specifications, engineering reports, test records, manuals, and technical bulletins. Coordinate design, testing, and modification activities with engineering and technical personnel. Develop conceptual aircraft designs based on technical requirements and transform them into functional design solutions.

candidates.title: aerospace engineer
candidates.description: Aerospace engineers develop, test and oversee the manufacture of flight vehicles such as aircrafts, missiles, and spacecrafts. The field of engineering they are active in, can be divided into two branches: aeronautical engineering and astronautical engineering.

candidates.title: flight test engineer
candidates.description: Flight test engineers work with other systems engineers to plan the tests in detail and to make sure that the recording systems are installed for the required data parameters. They analyse the data collected during test flights and produce reports for individual test phases and for the final flight test. They are also responsible for the safety of the test operations.

candidates.title: design engineer
candidates.description: Design engineers develop new conceptual and detailed designs. They create the look for these concepts or products and the systems used to make them. Design engineers work with engineers and marketers to enhance the functioning and efficiency of existing devices.

candidates.title: aircraft maintenance engineer
candidates.description: Aircraft maintenance engineers make preflight and postflight inspections, adjustments, and minor repairs to ensure safe and sound performance of aircrafts. They inspect aircraft prior to takeoff to detect malfunctions such as oil leaks, electrical or hydraulic problems. They verify passenger and cargo distribution and amount of fuel to ensure that weight and balance specifications are met.

candidates.title: aerodynamics engineer
candidates.description: Aerodynamics engineers perform aerodynamics analysis to make sure the designs of transport equipment meet aerodynamics and performance requirements. They contribute to designing engine and engine components, and issue technical reports for the engineering staff and customers. They coordinate with other engineering departments to check that designs perform as specified. Aerodynamics engineers conduct research to assess adaptability of equipment and materials. They also analyse proposals to evaluate production time and feasibility.

candidates.title: aviation ground systems engineer
candidates.description: Aviation ground systems engineers are in charge of supervising the maintenance of the equipment of the airport, for example, the visual aids, airport electrical systems, luggage systems, security systems, pavements, drainage, maintenance of unpaved areas and equipment and vehicles.

candidates.title: industrial tool design engineer
candidates.description: Industrial tool design engineers design various industrial tools in accordance with customer needs, manufacturing requirements, and building specifications. They test the designs, look for solutions to any problems, and oversee production.

candidates.title: aerospace engineering technician
candidates.description: Aerospace engineering technicians work with aerospace engineers to operate, maintain and test equipment used on aircraft and spacecraft. They review blueprints and instructions to determine test specifications and procedures. They use software to make sure that parts of a spacecraft or aircraft are functioning properly. They record test procedures and results, and make recommendations for changes.

They coordinate aircraft maintenance, flight missions, and operational activities aboard vessels, ensuring aviation equipment is ready and flight safety protocols are upheld. The role includes leading personnel, managing logistics, conducting training, and liaising with other naval and aviation units to maintain operational readiness and effective execution of aviation strategies.

Oversee the inspection, repair, and maintenance of aviation equipment. Ensure aircraft and aviation equipment are operational and mission-ready. Train and mentor aircrew and ground personnel in aviation procedures. Coordinate rescue, reconnaissance, and other maritime aviation support missions. Implement air safety protocols and conduct risk assessments. Liaise with logistics units to ensure the timely supply of parts and fuel. Maintain detailed records of flight operations and aircraft performance. Participate in joint operations with other naval, aviation, or relevant operational units.

Marine mechanics maintain and repair the engines and other machinery of vessels such as boilers, generators and electrical equipment.

candidates.title: marine electronics technician
candidates.description: Marine electronics technicians lay out, install and repair electronic systems and equipment in vessels. They assemble electronic components and wiring according to blueprints and assembly drawings.

candidates.title: maritime pilot
candidates.description: Maritime pilots are mariners who guide ships through dangerous or congested waters, such as harbours or river mouths. They are expert ship handlers who possess detailed knowledge of local waterways.

candidates.title: marine firefighter

They actively respond to contain fires and the outbreak of other hazardous on vessels, docks and other marine facilities. They ensure the marine installation complies with health and safety regulations. They also regulate the clean-up of the scene and assess the damage.

tasks: Evaluating and approving applications for the issuance of licences and/ or ratings, as appropriate. candidates.description: Aircraft assembly inspectors use measuring and testing equipment to inspect and monitor aircraft assemblies to ensure conformity to engineering specifications and to safety standards and regulations. candidates.title: aircraft engine inspector
candidates.description: Aircraft engine inspectors inspect all types of engines used for aircrafts in factories to ensure compliance with safety standards and regulations. They conduct routine, post-overhaul, pre-availability and post-casualty inspections. They provide documentation for repair activities and technical support to maintenance and repair centres. They review administrative records, analyse the operating performance of engines and report their findings.

candidates.title: aviation safety officer
candidates.description: Aviation safety officers plan and develop safety procedures for aviation companies. They study safety regulations and restrictions relative to aviation company operations. candidates.title: aircraft pilot

candidates.description: Avionics inspectors inspect instruments, electrical, mechanical and electronic systems of aircrafts to ensure their compliance with performance and safety standards. candidates.title: air force pilot

candidates.title: co-pilot

candidates.description: Aircraft interior technicians manufacture, assemble and repair interior components for aircrafts such as seats, carpeting, door panels, ceiling, lighting, etc. They also replace entertainment equipment such as video systems. candidates.description: Aircraft engine specialists advise on maintaining procedures to engines of aircrafts and helicopters. They perform operability tests to components and parts of aircrafts to diagnose suitability for usage and possible operations to improve performance. They interpret and provide support to understand the technical specifications given by manufacturers for application at the airport's premises.

Responsible for ensuring that airline operations in the country comply with the regulations set out in MCAR 1996. Responsible for ensuring the standard and level of aircraft flight tests and flight examinations are conducted according to established regulations. Ensuring that policies, legislation, procedures, and operational standards of airlines in the country always comply with ICAO requirements and other international bodies to maintain recognition and international landing rights. Ensuring that the operations of international airlines operating in the country comply with national legislation and ICAO requirements. Managing and administering the Flight Operations Division, including planning financial requirements and staff training. Overseeing investigations and providing advisory services regarding aviation incident reports for prevention and control purposes. candidates.description: Flight test engineers work with other systems engineers to plan the tests in detail and to make sure that the recording systems are installed for the required data parameters. They analyse the data collected during test flights and produce reports for individual test phases and for the final flight test. They are also responsible for the safety of the test operations.

description: Air Traffic Controller is responsible for managing the safe and orderly movement of aircraft in the air and on the ground. They monitor aircraft positions, coordinate flight paths, issue clearances and instructions to pilots, and oversee air cargo operations while ensuring compliance with aviation and customs regulations. Working in control towers, area control, or en route centres, they maintain high levels of concentration to prevent collisions, manage emergencies, and ensure the timely and efficient flow of both passenger and cargo flights.
tasks: Direct aircraft during all phases of flight, ensuring safe separation and orderly flow in controlled airspace. Monitor radar screens, flight data, and position reports to coordinate take-offs, landings, and in-flight movements. Communicate essential information to pilots, including weather conditions, flight plans, runway status, and operational updates. Authorise changes to flight levels, altitudes, routing, and sequencing as necessary to maintain safe and efficient traffic flow. Direct aircraft movements on the ground, including taxiing, take-offs, and landings, using radar or non-radar procedures. Coordinate air cargo receiving, dispatch, tracking, documentation, and compliance requirements to support safe and timely operations. Liaise with airlines, freight forwarders, handling agents, customs, and emergency services to support safe and timely airport and cargo operations. Respond to emergencies, coordinating search and rescue or other critical interventions. Maintain accurate operational records, reports, and documentation in compliance with aviation regulations and standards.

candidates.title: air traffic controller
candidates.description: Air traffic controllers assist pilots by providing information concerning the height, speed and course. They assist pilots in order to facilitate a safe take off and landing of aircrafts. They are responsible for maintaining a secure and orderly movement of aircraft along major air routes up in the sky and around airports. They control air traffic in and within vicinity of airports according to established procedures and policies to prevent collisions and to minimise delays arising from traffic congestion.

candidates.title: air traffic manager
candidates.description: Air traffic managers coordinate the planning of ground control, the maintenance of the aircrafts, and the handling of customers. They strive for the most efficient use of resources in directing the aircraft. They manage safety, quality, and risks in everyday work. They also plan and compare performance with other air navigation service providers.

candidates.title: air traffic instructor
candidates.description: Air traffic instructors train people in all the matters regarding with the operations in air navigation services such as the management of flight traffic and the communication for navigation in aerodromes. They teach all the directives issued by air traffic control for the purpose of passing to trainees the sense of safety and expeditious flow of air traffic.

candidates.title: air traffic safety technician
candidates.description: Air traffic safety technicians provide technical support regarding the safety of air traffic control and navigation systems. They design, maintain, install and operate these systems both in the airport and on board the aeroplane according to regulations.

candidates.title: rail traffic controller
candidates.description: Rail traffic controllers operate signals and points that help make sure trains run safely and on time. They operate from a signal box in order to control the order and movement of trains and ensure safety at all times. They are responsible for maintaining safety standards when trains are running normally and also in degraded or emergency operational situations.

candidates.title: airspace manager
candidates.description: Airspace managers control activities aimed at developing the European airspace into a continuum that is flexible and reactive to changes of users’ needs in airspace. They aim to optimise the network capacity and improve the performance.

candidates.title: taxi controller
candidates.description: Taxi controllers take bookings, dispatch vehicles, and are responsible for coordinating drivers while maintaining customer liaison.

candidates.title: passenger fare controller
candidates.description: Passenger fare controllers collect tickets, fares, and passes from passengers. They answer questions from passengers concerning transport rules, station, and timetable information.

description: Operation Centre Controller is responsible for overseeing the centralised management of an organisation’s operational activities within an operations center. They monitor systems, coordinate with technical and operational teams, and ensure smooth, continuous operations across departments. The role includes responding to operational anomalies, mitigating risks, and ensuring compliance with policies and regulatory standards, often providing round-the-clock support to maintain efficiency and service continuity.
tasks: Monitor system, network, and operational performance to detect issues and support continuous operations. Communicate operational status, system conditions, and service updates to relevant technical and operational teams. Coordinate emergency response and incident escalation during operational disruptions to reduce risk and restore normal operations. Coordinate internal communications during service disruptions to minimise downtime and operational risk. Document incidents and prepare reports to support performance reviews and operational improvement. Supervise technical and operational teams to ensure compliance with standard operating procedures. Review and update operational protocols to improve efficiency, safety, and service continuity.

candidates.title: data centre operator
candidates.description: Data centre operators maintain computer operations within the data centre. They manage daily activities within the centre to solve problems, maintain the system availability, and evaluate the system's performance.

candidates.title: operations manager
candidates.description: Operations managers plan, oversee and coordinate the daily operations of production of goods and provision of services. They also formulate and implement company policies and plan the use of human resources and materials.

candidates.description: ICT operations managers coordinate ICT services and infrastructure ensuring that the organisation has the required infrastructural resources. They also plan and monitor stages of either a business process or a computer process, negotiate contracts and take mitigation action in case of non-fulfilment of agreements. They oversee the day-to-day tasks involving infrastructure components, ICT systems and software.

candidates.title: financial controller
candidates.description: Financial controllers handle all tasks related to the budgeting and accounting aspects of a company or organisation. They implement and ensure compliance with internal financial and accounting procedures, and prepare documentation for external audits. They collect information related to financial statements such as assets, liabilities, equity, and cash flow in order to assess the company's financial position to prepare annual budgets and forecasts.

candidates.title: rescue centre manager
candidates.description: Rescue centre managers supervise operations of a rescue centre, performing administrative duties and supervision of staff. They ensure that the centre operates according to policies and staff perform rescue missions in a safe, efficient and compliant manner.

candidates.title: contact centre manager
candidates.description: Contact centre managers coordinate and plan the daily operations of contact centres. They ensure that customer inquiries are satisfied efficiently and according to policies. They manage employees, resources and procedures to improve best practices and achieve high levels of customer satisfaction.

candidates.title: call centre manager
candidates.description: Call centre managers set the objectives of the service per month, week, and day. They perform micromanagement of the results obtained in the centre in order to proactively react with plans, trainings, or motivational plans depending on the problems faced by the service. They strive for achievement of KPIs such as minimum operating time, sales per day, and compliance with quality parameters.

description: Air Traffic Control Officer Grade A9 responsible for designing and implementing the tasks of providing air traffic services to Malaysian airspace users (FIR Kuala Lumpur and FIR Kota Kinabalu) in accordance with the rules set by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) and in accordance with the powers given in the Aviation Act Malaysian Civil Aviation (MCAA 1969) and Malaysian Civil Aviation Regulations (MCAR 1996) to always be in a safe and smooth condition.
tasks: Performing duties in providing and ensuring the availability of communication system and equipment requirements within Malaysian airspace to deliver satisfactory air traffic services. Identifying and ensuring the provision of requirements for air traffic services such as surveillance systems and air traffic control systems. Planning and coordinating ATC and non-ATC courses for PKTU/PPKTU and Assistant KTU. Conducting evaluations of project planning and the preparation of contract documentation. Responsible for managing Malaysian airspace, including airway planning, airspace classification, and allocation of airspace for air force training and air shows. Providing air traffic control services within Air Traffic Control Centre sectors by issuing clearances, instructions, advice, and information to aircraft preparing for or conducting flights in order to prevent collisions and minimise delays. Issuing ATC clearances and SIDs to aircraft intending to depart. Ensuring that all ATC equipment under control, such as the Data Processing Surveillance Display (DPSD), Flight Data Processing System (FDPS), Voice Switching Communication System (VSCS), and Airfield Ground Lighting (AGL), are in good working condition at all times. Supervising the implementation of Aerodrome and Surface Movement Control services for all aircraft movements in and out of the airport in accordance with established regulations. Teaching the courses offered, namely Basic ATC Course, Aerodrome Course, Procedural ATC Course, Surveillance ATC Course, Search and Rescue (SAR) Course, and Non-ATC courses.
