candidates.description: Kinesiologists study and research the movement of the body; its muscles and parts. They analyse and use scientific data and methods to improve body motion, generally in humans, through an understanding of such areas as physiology, kinetics, neurology, and biology. They recognise the effects that some factors, such as body condition, have on motion and develop solutions to improve overall mechanics and mobility.

candidates.title: maternity support worker
candidates.description: Maternity support workers work together in a team with midwives and health professionals within the occupational fields of nursing and midwifery. They assist midwives and women in childbirth by providing the necessary support, care and advice during pregnancy, labour and the postpartum period, assist births and assist in providing care for the new-born.

description: Surgeon diagnoses and treats a condition, injury, or deformity that requires surgical intervention, performing an operation to restore function, correct abnormalities, or manage disease. They provide comprehensive care before, during, and after surgery, including assessing risks, planning the procedure, and collaborating with a multidisciplinary team. Specialisations may focus on a specific patient group, such as children, or on areas like reconstructive, aesthetic, or vascular surgery, requiring expertise in anatomy, physiology, and advanced surgical techniques.
tasks: Examine and assess patients using medical history, physical examinations, and diagnostic tests to determine surgical needs. Plan and explain surgical procedures, including risks, recovery, and follow-up care, according to patient condition and surgical requirements. Perform surgical operations using appropriate techniques and instruments for elective and specialised procedures. Maintain sterile conditions and adhere to infection control protocols to ensure patient safety during surgery. Lead and coordinate the surgical team across pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative stages. Monitor post-operative recovery, prescribe medications, and manage follow-up care to optimise patient outcomes. Collaborate with healthcare professionals to provide integrated multidisciplinary patient care. Provide counselling and information to patients and families on surgical options, risks, and expected outcomes.

candidates.title: doctors' surgery assistant
candidates.description: Doctors' surgery assistants support doctors of medicine in medical measures, in performing simple support activities during medical procedures, standardised diagnostic programmes and standardised point-of-care tests, ensuring surgery hygiene, cleaning, disinfecting, sterilising and maintaining medical devices and performing the organisational and administrative tasks required for operating a doctor`s surgery under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: tree surgeon
candidates.description: Tree surgeons maintain trees. They use heavy machinery to prune and cut trees. Tree surgeons are often required to climb the trees to perform maintenance.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: specialist dentist
candidates.description: Specialist dentists prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues specialised in oral surgery or orthodontics.

candidates.title: surgical instrument maker
candidates.description: Surgical instrument makers create, repair and design surgical instruments, such as clamps, graspers, mechanical cutters, scopes, probes and other surgical instruments.

candidates.title: anaesthetic technician
candidates.description: Anaesthetic technicians assist specialised doctors in anaesthetics. They prepare operating theatres and other specialised clinics for anaesthetic procedures, prepare the equipment needed for anaesthesia, and assist with inducing and maintaining adequate anaesthesia and post-anaesthesia procedures. They do so under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: specialist biomedical scientist
candidates.description: Specialist biomedical scientists lead a department or specialist area, undertaking clinical research projects and working as a diagnostic partner within the health care team (investigating and diagnosing patient illnesses like, cancer, diabetes, haematological disorders and coagulation, in the areas of molecular biology or genomics, among others) using several methods, digital tools, and bioinformatics.

candidates.title: specialist nurse
candidates.description: Specialist nurses promote and restore people's health, and diagnose and care within a specific branch of the nursing field. Examples of such specialist nursing jobs include but are not restricted to; ambulatory care nurse, advanced practice nurse, cardiac nurse, dental nurse, community health nurse, forensic nurse, gastroenterology nurse, hospice and palliative care nurse, paediatric nurse, public health nurse, rehabilitation nurse, renal nurse and school nurse. Specialist nurses are general care nurses prepared beyond the level of a nurse generalist and authorised to practice as specialists with specific expertise in a branch of the nursing field.

description: Dermatologist diagnoses and treats medical and cosmetic conditions affecting the skin, hair, nails, and mucous membranes. They manage a disorder such as eczema, psoriasis, acne, fungal infections, or skin cancer, and perform relevant procedures including minor surgery, laser therapy, chemical peels, and cryotherapy. Their work involves patient assessment, treatment planning, and promoting skin health through education and preventive care in clinical and hospital settings.
tasks: Evaluate and diagnose disorders affecting the skin, hair, nails, and mucous membranes through clinical examinations and diagnostic tests. Prescribe and manage treatments, including topical, oral, and biologic medications. Perform dermatological procedures, including minor surgery, biopsies, laser therapy, chemical peels, and cryotherapy. Explain treatment plans, procedures, recovery requirements, and follow-up care to patients. Monitor patient progress and adjust treatments based on clinical response. Provide patient counselling on preventive skincare and long-term management of dermatological conditions. Collaborate with other healthcare specialists to support integrated patient care.

candidates.title: toxicologist
candidates.description: Toxicologists study the effects that chemical substances or biological and physical agents have in living organisms, more specifically, on the environment and on the animal and human health. They determine doses of the exposure to substances for arising toxic effects in environments, people, and living organisms, and also perform experiments on animals and cell cultures.

candidates.title: immunologist
candidates.description: Immunologists research the immune system of living organisms (e.g. human body) and the way it reacts to external infections or invasive harmful agents (e.g. virus, bacteria, parasites). They focus their study on those diseases that affect the immunology of living organisms in order to classify them for treatment.

candidates.title: metrologist
candidates.description: Metrologists study and practice the science of measurement. They develop quantity systems, units of measurement and measuring methods to be used in science. Metrologists establish new methods and tools to quantify and better understand information.

candidates.title: epidemiologist
candidates.description: Epidemiologists centre their research on origin and causes for illness eruption in humans. They determine the way in which diseases are spread out and propose risk preventive measures to health policy organisms.

candidates.title: microbiologist
candidates.description: Microbiologists study and research the life forms, characteristics, and processes of microscopic organisms. They study microorganisms such as bacteria, protozoa, fungi, etc. in order to diagnose and counteract the effects that these microorganisms might have in animals, in the environment, in the food industry, or in the health care industry.

candidates.title: climatologist
candidates.description: Climatologists study the average change in weather and climate from a long-term perspective. They research and analyse historic weather conditions in order to forecast climatic conditions trends such as changes in temperature, global warming, or regional evolutive weather conditions. They use these findings for advising on environmental policy, construction, agricultural projects, and societal matters.

candidates.title: hair removal technician
candidates.description: Hair removal technicians provide cosmetic services to their clients by removing unwanted hair on various body parts. They can use different techniques for temporary hair removal, such as epilation and depilation techniques, or permanent hair removal methods, such as electrolysis or intense pulsed light.

candidates.title: graphologist
candidates.description: Graphologists analyse written or printed materials in order to draw conclusions and evidence about traits, personality, abilities and authorship of the writer. They interpret letter forms, the fashion of writing, and patterns in the writing.

description: Orthopaedist specialises in diagnosing, treating, preventing, and rehabilitating a condition of the musculoskeletal system, including bones, joints, muscles, ligaments, and tendons. They provide both surgical and non-surgical care to restore function, relieve pain, and improve mobility, often collaborating with a physiotherapist and other healthcare professionals. Their practice may adopt a holistic approach, considering the interaction of the musculoskeletal system with overall health to support natural healing and wellbeing.
tasks: Consult with patients to assess musculoskeletal conditions and review their medical history. Diagnose fractures, joint disorders, deformities, and other musculoskeletal conditions through physical examinations and diagnostic imaging. Develop and discuss individualised surgical and non-surgical treatment plans to relieve pain, restore function, and improve mobility. Perform orthopaedic surgical procedures such as joint replacement, arthroscopy, and corrective surgery. Prescribe and oversee physiotherapy, rehabilitation, and exercise programmes in coordination with physiotherapists and other healthcare professionals. Manage pre-operative and post-operative care, monitor recovery, and adjust treatment as needed. Advise patients on posture, lifestyle modifications, and preventive measures to maintain musculoskeletal health and reduce injury risk. Coordinate with other healthcare professionals to provide integrated patient care.

candidates.title: prosthetist-orthotist
candidates.description: Prosthetist-orthotists design and custom fit prostheses and orthoses for individuals who are missing a limb from accident, disease or congenital conditions or for individuals who have impairments, deficiences or weaknesses due to injury, pathology or congenital malformation. They mix patient care with the design and fabrication of these devices to address their patients' needs.

candidates.title: osteopath
candidates.description: Osteopaths provide therapeutic treatment of disorders in the musculoskeletal system to patients with physical issues such as back pain, joint pain and digestive disorders. They mainly use manipulation of the body tissues, touch, stretching and massage techniques to relieve the patients` pain and promote a healthy lifestyle.

candidates.title: orthoptist
candidates.description: Orthoptists diagnose and treat anomalies of binocular vision. They examine, assess and treat vision impairments, squint, amblyopia and eye motility disorders. Orthoptists apply these methods in particular in the fields of paediatrics, neurology, neuro-ophthalmology, ophthalmology, orthoptics, optometry, pleoptics and strabology assessing functional diseases of the eye for improving functional disorders of the visual system. They also provide counselling, preventive measures and training activities and may refract and prescribe glasses, such as prism corrective glasses.

candidates.title: orthopaedic footwear technician
candidates.description: Orthopaedic footwear technicians design footwear and make patterns, using manufacturing technology. They compensate and accommodate foot and ankle fitting problems and design and manufacture footwear and its orthopaedic components, including orthoses, insoles, soles and others.

candidates.title: physiotherapist
candidates.description: Physiotherapists are autonomous health professionals who are responsible for developing, maintaining or restoring motor function and movement throughout the lifespan using evidence-based practice. They relieve pain and treat or prevent physical conditions associated with injury, disease or other impairments. Physiotherapists empower patients and their carers to manage the condition outside clinical settings. They work within their scope of practice and their professional Code of Conduct.

candidates.title: orthopaedic supplies specialised seller
candidates.description: Orthopaedic supplies specialised sellers sell orthopaedic goods in specialised shops.

candidates.title: prosthetic-orthotics technician
candidates.description: Prosthetic-orthotics technicians design, create, fit and repair supportive devices, such as braces, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.

candidates.title: chiropractor
candidates.description: Chiropractors are responsible for the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disorders related to the neuromusculoskeletal system and the effects of these disorders on general health. They are independent primary health care professionals.

description: Paediatrician specialises in the medical care of an infant, child, or adolescent, focusing on promoting overall health, development, and wellbeing. They diagnose, treat, and prevent illnesses and medical conditions, manage acute and chronic diseases, monitor growth and developmental milestones, and administer vaccinations. They also provide guidance on nutrition, health, and emotional support to the patient and their caregiver from birth through young adulthood.
tasks: Conduct paediatric medical assessments and diagnostic tests to evaluate the health of infants, children, and adolescents. Diagnose and manage childhood illnesses, infections, and developmental disorders, including acute and chronic conditions. Prescribe age-appropriate treatments and medications based on diagnosis. Administer vaccinations and monitor children’s immunisation schedules. Provide health education and preventive care guidance to parents or guardians on nutrition, health, and child wellbeing. Offer guidance and counselling on children’s behavioural, emotional, and developmental issues. Refer patients to medical specialists for advanced care when required.

candidates.title: child care coordinator
candidates.description: Child care coordinators organise child care services, activities and events after the school hours and during school hoildays. They assist in the development of children by implementing care programmes. Child care coordinators also entertain children and maintain a safe environment for the children.

candidates.title: doctors' surgery assistant
candidates.description: Doctors' surgery assistants support doctors of medicine in medical measures, in performing simple support activities during medical procedures, standardised diagnostic programmes and standardised point-of-care tests, ensuring surgery hygiene, cleaning, disinfecting, sterilising and maintaining medical devices and performing the organisational and administrative tasks required for operating a doctor`s surgery under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: child care worker
candidates.description: Child care workers provide care for children when the parents or family members are unavailable. They look after the children's basic needs and help or supervise them during play. Child care workers can work for preschools, daycare centres, childcare agencies or individual families.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: specialist nurse
candidates.description: Specialist nurses promote and restore people's health, and diagnose and care within a specific branch of the nursing field. Examples of such specialist nursing jobs include but are not restricted to; ambulatory care nurse, advanced practice nurse, cardiac nurse, dental nurse, community health nurse, forensic nurse, gastroenterology nurse, hospice and palliative care nurse, paediatric nurse, public health nurse, rehabilitation nurse, renal nurse and school nurse. Specialist nurses are general care nurses prepared beyond the level of a nurse generalist and authorised to practice as specialists with specific expertise in a branch of the nursing field.

candidates.title: nursery school head teacher
candidates.description: Nursery school head teachers manage the day-to-day activities of a kindergarten or nursery school. They manage staff, make decisions concerning admissions and are responsible for meeting curriculum standards, which are age-appropriate for kindergarten students and facilitate social and behavioural development education. They also ensure the school meets the national education requirements set by law.

candidates.title: dietitian
candidates.description: Dietitians assess specific nutritional requirements of populations or individuals throughout their lives and translate this into advice which will maintain, reduce risk to, or restore people’s health. Using evidence-based approaches, dietitians work to empower individuals, families and groups to provide or select food which is nutritionally adequate, safe, tasty and sustainable. Beyond healthcare, dietitians improve the nutritional environment for all through governments, industry, academia and research.

candidates.title: child day care centre manager
candidates.description: Child day care centre managers provide social services to children and their families. They supervise and support child care workers and manage the childcare facilities. Child day care centre managers have the responsibility for strategic and operational leadership and management of staff teams and resources within and or across child care services.

description: Physician diagnoses, treats, and prevents an illness or injury, providing comprehensive medical care through an examination, medical history, treatment, and health advice. They collaborate with other healthcare professionals and refer the patient to a specialist when necessary, supporting the overall health and wellbeing of the individual and the community across a hospital, clinic, or private practice.
tasks: Conduct consultations, take medical histories, and perform physical examinations to assess patient health. Diagnose illnesses, injuries, and other medical conditions based on clinical findings. Prescribe appropriate medications and therapies according to patient needs. Order and interpret diagnostic tests. Perform minor clinical procedures when necessary. Advise patients on preventive health measures and lifestyle changes. Refer complex or specialised cases to appropriate medical specialists. Follow clinical policies, safety procedures, and universal precautions to protect patients and staff.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: doctors' surgery assistant
candidates.description: Doctors' surgery assistants support doctors of medicine in medical measures, in performing simple support activities during medical procedures, standardised diagnostic programmes and standardised point-of-care tests, ensuring surgery hygiene, cleaning, disinfecting, sterilising and maintaining medical devices and performing the organisational and administrative tasks required for operating a doctor`s surgery under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: physiologist
candidates.description: Physiologists study and exert research on the functioning of different living organisms, the parts they are composed of, and their interactions. They understand the fashion in which living systems react to factors such as diseases, physical activity, and stress, and use that information to develop methods and solutions to even out the effect that those stimuli have in living bodies.

candidates.title: specialist pharmacist
candidates.description: Specialist pharmacists provide specialist services for companies in the pharmacy industry and in hospital pharmacies. The role of the specialist pharmacist varies throughout Europe, subject to national rules and training.

candidates.title: medical practice manager
candidates.description: Medical practice managers manage the day-to-day operations of a medical practice. They oversee the staff and business side of the practice.

candidates.title: pharmacist
candidates.description: Pharmacists prepare, dispense, and provide prescriptions for, over the counter medication. They offer clinical information on medicines, report suspected adverse reactions, and provide personalised support to patients. Pharmacists formulate and test medications in laboratories, and store, preserve, and distribute them.

candidates.title: hospital pharmacist
candidates.description: Hospital pharmacists prepare, dispense and provide medication to patients in hospitals. They collaborate with healthcare personnel such as doctors and nurses to treat patients and also offer advice and information on medications.

candidates.title: healthcare specialist lecturer
candidates.description: Healthcare specialist lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of healthcare, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of specialist healthcare, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

description: Radiologist specialises in diagnosing and treating a disease or injury using medical imaging and image-guided techniques. They interpret X-rays, CT scans, MRIs, ultrasounds, nuclear medicine, and PET scans to identify abnormalities, support treatment planning, and guide minimally invasive procedures. They may also develop and oversee radiotherapy for cancer, collaborate with a multidisciplinary team, monitor patient progress, and contribute to research and teaching within their specialty.
tasks: Assess and interpret medical images to diagnose medical conditions. Determine and plan appropriate imaging or interventional procedures based on clinical indications. Administer contrast media or radiopharmaceuticals in accordance with safety protocols and radiation regulations. Perform image-guided interventional procedures, including biopsies, drainages, and minimally invasive treatments. Provide input on radiotherapy planning and monitoring where applicable, in collaboration with relevant specialists. Collaborate with referring physicians and multidisciplinary teams to support diagnosis, treatment planning, and patient management. Explain imaging procedures, associated risks, and follow-up care to patients and their families. Supervise and coordinate radiology staff, technologists, and support personnel.

candidates.title: diagnostic radiographer
candidates.description: Diagnostic radiographers plan, prepare and perform diagnostic imaging examinations and post processing, with a wide range of equipment and techniques using X-rays, strong magnetic fields or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and high frequency sound (Ultrasound).

candidates.title: radiographer
candidates.description: Radiographers use a range of technologies to examine, treat and care for patients. They work in the fields of Medical Imaging, Radiotherapy and Nuclear Medicine and apply ionising radiation, ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and radioactive sources.

candidates.title: nuclear medicine radiographer
candidates.description: Nuclear medicine radiographers plan, prepare and perform nuclear medicine examinations, post-processing and treatment with a wide range of equipment and techniques using X-rays, magnetic resonance imaging and radiopharmaceuticals.

candidates.title: radiation therapist
candidates.description: Radiation therapists are responsible for the accurate delivery of radiotherapy to cancer patients and, as part of the multidisciplinary team, for elements of treatment preparation and patient care. This encompasses the safe and accurate delivery of the radiation dose prescribed and the clinical care and support of the patient throughout the treatment preparation, treatment delivery and immediate post treatment phases.

candidates.title: radio technician
candidates.description: Radio technicians install, adjust, test, maintain, and repair mobile or stationary radio transmitting and receiving equipment and two-way radio communications systems. They also monitor their performance and determine causes of faults.

candidates.title: audiologist
candidates.description: Audiologists assess, diagnose and treat patients ( children or adults) with audiological and vestibular disorders caused by infectious, genetic, traumatic or degenerative conditions, such as hearing loss, tinnitus, dizziness, imbalance, hyperacusis and auditory processing difficulties. They can prescribe a hearing aid and have a role in assessing and managing patients who may benefit from cochlear implants.

candidates.title: radiation protection technician
candidates.description: Radiation protection technicians monitor radiation levels in buildings and facilities to ensure compliance with health and safety standards, and to prevent dangerous elevations in the radiation level. They take measures to minimise radiation emissions, and to prevent further contamination in the event of radiation pollution, by developing radiation protection plans, in particular for nuclear plants and facilities.

candidates.title: metrologist
candidates.description: Metrologists study and practice the science of measurement. They develop quantity systems, units of measurement and measuring methods to be used in science. Metrologists establish new methods and tools to quantify and better understand information.

description: Urologist specialises in diagnosing, treating, and managing a disorder of the urinary tract and male reproductive system. They assess the patient’s health through an examination, diagnostic tests, and imaging, and provide both surgical and non-surgical treatments. They also manage ongoing care and coordinate with other healthcare professionals to ensure effective patient outcomes.
tasks: Assess patients by reviewing symptoms, medical history, and conducting physical examinations. Order and interpret diagnostic tests. Diagnose urological conditions such as kidney stones, bladder disorders, prostate enlargement, and urinary tract cancers. Plan and perform surgical procedures. Explain procedures, treatment, recovery, and follow-up care to patients. Prescribe medications and non-surgical therapies for urological conditions. Manage chronic urological conditions, including incontinence and erectile dysfunction, and provide ongoing care. Coordinate with surgical teams and other healthcare professionals during treatment and operations, ensuring adherence to clinical protocols. Provide preventive care advice and patient education related to urological health.

candidates.title: sophrologist
candidates.description: Sophrologists aim to reduce their clients` stress and produce optimal health and well-being by applying a dynamic relaxation method which consists of a specific set of physical and mental exercises on a doctor's order.

candidates.title: microbiologist
candidates.description: Microbiologists study and research the life forms, characteristics, and processes of microscopic organisms. They study microorganisms such as bacteria, protozoa, fungi, etc. in order to diagnose and counteract the effects that these microorganisms might have in animals, in the environment, in the food industry, or in the health care industry.

candidates.title: immunologist
candidates.description: Immunologists research the immune system of living organisms (e.g. human body) and the way it reacts to external infections or invasive harmful agents (e.g. virus, bacteria, parasites). They focus their study on those diseases that affect the immunology of living organisms in order to classify them for treatment.

candidates.title: physiologist
candidates.description: Physiologists study and exert research on the functioning of different living organisms, the parts they are composed of, and their interactions. They understand the fashion in which living systems react to factors such as diseases, physical activity, and stress, and use that information to develop methods and solutions to even out the effect that those stimuli have in living bodies.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: hydrologist
candidates.description: Hydrologists research and study the quality, current challenges, and distribution of water in the Earth. They study water supply from rivers, streams, and springs to determine their adequate and sustainable use. Together with a cross functional team of professionals, they plan and develop how water can be supplied to cities and urban areas while ensuring efficiency and resource conservation.

candidates.title: toxicologist
candidates.description: Toxicologists study the effects that chemical substances or biological and physical agents have in living organisms, more specifically, on the environment and on the animal and human health. They determine doses of the exposure to substances for arising toxic effects in environments, people, and living organisms, and also perform experiments on animals and cell cultures.

candidates.title: hydrogeologist
candidates.description: Hydrogeologists study the distribution, quality and flow of water in order to keep mine workings free of nuisance water and to ensure an adequate supply of process water. They supply and evaluate information which will protect ground and surface water from contamination.

description: Venereologists diagnose, treat, and prevent sexually transmitted infections and related reproductive health conditions. They assess patient health, perform diagnostic tests, prescribe appropriate treatments, and provide guidance on safe sexual practices and disease prevention, maintaining confidentiality and professional standards in clinical settings.
tasks: Assess patients’ sexual and reproductive health through detailed medical histories and physical examinations. Order and interpret diagnostic tests to identify sexually transmitted infections and related reproductive health conditions. Diagnose and treat sexually transmitted infections and related reproductive health conditions. Prescribe appropriate medications and therapies for sexually transmitted infections and related conditions. Perform minor clinical procedures related to the treatment of sexually transmitted infections when necessary. Explain treatment plans, procedures, and follow-up care to patients. Provide preventive education on safe sexual practices and disease prevention.

candidates.title: oenologist
candidates.description: Oenologists track the wine manufacturing process in its entirety and supervise the workers in wineries. They supervise and coordinate production to ensure the quality of the wine and also give advice by determining the value and classification of wines being produced.

candidates.title: ecologist
candidates.description: Ecologists carry out assessments of the health and distribution of organisms, namely people, plants, and animals, and the relationship between organisms and their environment. Ecologists usually have a specialisation area, e.g. freshwater, marine, terrestrial, fauna, and flora about which they conduct research and perform related tasks.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: epidemiologist
candidates.description: Epidemiologists centre their research on origin and causes for illness eruption in humans. They determine the way in which diseases are spread out and propose risk preventive measures to health policy organisms.

candidates.title: seismologist
candidates.description: Seismologists study the movement of tectonic plaques in the Earth which causes the propagation of seismic waves and earthquakes. They study and observe the various sources causing earthquakes such as volcanic activity, atmospheric phenomena, or the behaviour of oceans. They provide their scientific observations to prevent dangers in construction and infrastructure.

candidates.title: microbiologist
candidates.description: Microbiologists study and research the life forms, characteristics, and processes of microscopic organisms. They study microorganisms such as bacteria, protozoa, fungi, etc. in order to diagnose and counteract the effects that these microorganisms might have in animals, in the environment, in the food industry, or in the health care industry.

candidates.title: hydrologist
candidates.description: Hydrologists research and study the quality, current challenges, and distribution of water in the Earth. They study water supply from rivers, streams, and springs to determine their adequate and sustainable use. Together with a cross functional team of professionals, they plan and develop how water can be supplied to cities and urban areas while ensuring efficiency and resource conservation.

candidates.title: hydrogeologist

description: Occupational Therapist helps an individual across all ages who faces physical, mental, or social challenges to live more independent and fulfilling lives. They assess patients’ abilities and develop personalised intervention plans to support daily activities, work, and leisure, addressing difficulties arising from illness, injury, disability, developmental conditions, or ageing. Their work aims to enhance overall quality of life and functional independence.
tasks: Assess clients’ physical, cognitive, and emotional abilities to identify functional limitations affecting daily activities. Develop and implement individualised treatment and rehabilitation plans to improve functional abilities and independence. Train and support patients in performing activities of daily living, including mobility and personal care. Recommend, provide training on, and monitor the use of assistive and adaptive equipment. Educate and support patients and caregivers on rehabilitation strategies, prevention of complications, and ongoing care. Conduct home and workplace assessments to enhance safety and support independent living. Collaborate with multidisciplinary healthcare teams to coordinate integrated patient care. Document treatment plans, interventions, and patient progress accurately.

candidates.title: physiotherapist
candidates.description: Physiotherapists are autonomous health professionals who are responsible for developing, maintaining or restoring motor function and movement throughout the lifespan using evidence-based practice. They relieve pain and treat or prevent physical conditions associated with injury, disease or other impairments. Physiotherapists empower patients and their carers to manage the condition outside clinical settings. They work within their scope of practice and their professional Code of Conduct.

candidates.title: occupational therapist
candidates.description: Occupational therapists assist individuals or groups who have occupational limitations due to diseases, physical disorders, and temporary or permanent mental disabilities, in regaining their ability to perform daily activities. They provide treatment and rehabilitation to enable them to actively participate in society, to live their lives according to their wishes and to perform those activities that are meaningful to them. Occupational therapists work in public health and social care services, but can also be involved in supporting asylum seekers, refugees and/or homeless people.

candidates.title: occupational therapy assistant
candidates.description: Occupational therapy assistants support occupational therapists by working with people and communities to enhance their ability to engage in the occupations they want to, need to, or are expected to do, or by modifying the occupation or the environment to better support their occupational engagement. They work under the supervision of an occupational therapist.

candidates.title: recreational therapist
candidates.description: Recreational therapists offer treatment to persons who have behavioural disorders or conditions. They use techniques and interventions such as art, music, animals and dance to promote, maintain and restore the development and health of the patient.

candidates.title: rehabilitation support worker
candidates.description: Rehabilitation support workers provide counselling to individuals dealing with birth defects or with major consequences caused by diseases, accidents, and burnouts. They help them to cope with personal, social and vocational issues. They assess the personal needs of clients, develop rehabilitation plans, get involved in the training, and help people undergoing a rehabilitation plan with job placement.

candidates.title: occupational analyst
candidates.description: Occupational analysts collect and analyse occupational information within one field or company in order to make recommendations for reducing costs and general business improvements. They provide technical assistance to employers in dealing with problematic staff recruitment and development and with staff restructuring. Occupational analysts study and write job descriptions and prepare occupational classification systems.

candidates.title: sport therapist
candidates.description: Sport therapists program and supervise rehabilitation exercises for individuals and groups. They work with individuals that have chronic health conditions or are at high risk of developing them. They communicate with medical and healthcare professionals about participants' conditions using correct medical terminology, and with an understanding of the standard treatment options for an individual’s condition. Sport therapists take a holistic approach to the wellness of their clients that includes advising on lifestyle, food or time management. They do not have a medical background and do not require medical qualifications.

candidates.title: art therapist
candidates.description: Art therapists help patients overcome psychological and emotional difficulties through an artistic process which reflects emotions and feelings, focusing on patients who suffer a variety of problems such as mental, psychological, and behavioural disorders in order to facilitate self-understanding and awareness.

description: Professional Nurse provides care, support, and treatment for an individual experiencing illness, injury, ageing, or other health-related conditions. They assess patient needs, develop and implement a nursing care plan, administer medications and treatments, and work collaboratively with other healthcare professionals. Their role also includes educating the patient and family and delivering patient-centred care across hospitals, clinics, and community health settings.
tasks: Provide patient-centred nursing care, support, treatment, and advice to patients who are ill, injured, ageing, or disabled. Conduct patient assessments and physical examinations to evaluate health status and identify care needs. Develop, implement, and review nursing care plans according to patient needs and prescribed treatment. Administer medications and prescribed treatments safely and effectively. Monitor patients, document progress, and maintain accurate nursing and patient records. Assist physicians and other healthcare professionals in surgical, diagnostic, and therapeutic procedures. Educate patients and families on health management, disease prevention, and post-treatment care. Adhere to safety, hygiene, and infection prevention and control protocols.

candidates.title: specialist nurse
candidates.description: Specialist nurses promote and restore people's health, and diagnose and care within a specific branch of the nursing field. Examples of such specialist nursing jobs include but are not restricted to; ambulatory care nurse, advanced practice nurse, cardiac nurse, dental nurse, community health nurse, forensic nurse, gastroenterology nurse, hospice and palliative care nurse, paediatric nurse, public health nurse, rehabilitation nurse, renal nurse and school nurse. Specialist nurses are general care nurses prepared beyond the level of a nurse generalist and authorised to practice as specialists with specific expertise in a branch of the nursing field.

candidates.title: advanced nurse practitioner
candidates.description: Advanced nurse practitioners are in charge of promoting and restoring patients` health, provide diagnosis and care in advanced settings, coordinating care within areas of chronic disease management, providing integrated care, and supervising assigned team members. Advanced nurse practitioners are general care nurses who have acquired an expert knowledge base, complex decision making skills and clinical competencies for expanded clinical practice on advanced level.

candidates.title: nurse assistant
candidates.description: Nurse assistants provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. They perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, move patients or change linens and may transfer or transport patients.

candidates.title: nurse responsible for general care
candidates.description: Nurses responsible for general care are in charge of promoting and restoring patients` health by providing physical and psychological support to patients, friends, and families. They also supervise assigned team members.

candidates.title: nursing lecturer
candidates.description: Nursing lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, nursing, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of nursing, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: veterinary nurse
candidates.description: Veterinary nurses support animals undergoing veterinary treatment and give advice to veterinary clients in the promotion of animal health and disease prevention in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: midwife
candidates.description: Midwives assist women in childbirth by providing the necessary support, care and advice during pregnancy, labour and the postpartum period, conduct births and provide care for the new-born. They advise on health, preventive measures, preparation for parenthood, detection of complications in mother and child, accessing of medical care, promoting normal birth and carrying out emergency measures.

description: Specialist Nurse promotes and restores health by providing expert care within a specific nursing field. They possess advanced training beyond general nursing, enabling them to assess a patient’s needs, diagnose conditions, initiate treatments, and monitor responses independently. Working collaboratively with healthcare teams, they deliver specialised clinical care, contribute to health education, clinical leadership, research, and inform policies to enhance outcomes in areas such as intensive care, cardiology, oncology, or emergency medicine.
tasks: Provide specialised nursing care, treatment, and advice to patients with complex or acute health conditions. Conduct advanced patient assessments and physical examinations to determine health status and disease conditions. Develop and implement nursing care plans tailored to patient needs. Administer medications and prescribed treatments safely and accurately. Monitor patient progress and responses to treatment using clinical observation and diagnostic tools. Educate patients and families on disease management, treatment plans, and care practices. Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to coordinate patient care. Lead quality improvement activities and mentor junior nursing staff. Prepare clinical reports and contribute to the development of protocols and guidelines.

candidates.title: specialist biomedical scientist
candidates.description: Specialist biomedical scientists lead a department or specialist area, undertaking clinical research projects and working as a diagnostic partner within the health care team (investigating and diagnosing patient illnesses like, cancer, diabetes, haematological disorders and coagulation, in the areas of molecular biology or genomics, among others) using several methods, digital tools, and bioinformatics.

description: Nurse Instructor guides the education and professional development of a nurse by teaching, mentoring, and supervising a student in academic and clinical settings. They deliver theoretical instruction, oversee practical skill application, assess student progress, and contribute to curriculum development, ensuring graduates acquire the competencies necessary for high-quality patient care.
tasks: Plan and coordinate nursing courses and practical training for students and staff. Ensure students’ clinical practice follows Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and clinical guidelines. Supervise, mentor, and support students during clinical practice. Develop and implement lesson plans, teaching materials, and practical simulations. Deliver lectures, demonstrations, and hands-on training sessions. Evaluate student performance through assessments, tests, and feedback. Coordinate with hospital staff to facilitate clinical placements and align training objectives. Conduct supervisory visits to monitor adherence to nursing standards in clinical training. Contribute to curriculum development and prepare reports related to teaching and training activities. Participate in professional development, seminars, and training programmes.

candidates.title: first aid instructor
candidates.description: First aid instructors teach students immediate lifesaving emergency measures, such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the recovery position, and injury care. They provided practice materials such as a specialised manikin.

candidates.title: specialist nurse
candidates.description: Specialist nurses promote and restore people's health, and diagnose and care within a specific branch of the nursing field. Examples of such specialist nursing jobs include but are not restricted to; ambulatory care nurse, advanced practice nurse, cardiac nurse, dental nurse, community health nurse, forensic nurse, gastroenterology nurse, hospice and palliative care nurse, paediatric nurse, public health nurse, rehabilitation nurse, renal nurse and school nurse. Specialist nurses are general care nurses prepared beyond the level of a nurse generalist and authorised to practice as specialists with specific expertise in a branch of the nursing field.

candidates.title: sports instructor
candidates.description: Sports instructors introduce people to a sport and teach them the skills required for the performance of sport. They have a strong grip on one or more sports, which are often adventure sports, and know how to motivate others and share with them the enjoyment of the activity.

candidates.title: firefighter instructor
candidates.description: Firefighter instructors train probationary, new academy recruits, or cadets, on the theory and practice necessary to become a firefighter. They conduct theoretical lectures on academic subjects such as law, basic chemistry, safety regulations, risk management, fire prevention, reading blueprints etc. Fire academy instructors also provide more hands-on, practical instruction regarding the usage of assistive equipment and rescue tools such as a fire hose, fire axe, smoke mask etc., but also heavy physical training, breathing techniques, first aid, self defense tactics and vehicle operations. They also prepare and develop lesson plans and new training programmes as new public service-related regulations and issues arise. The instructors monitor the students' progress, evaluate them individually and prepare performance evaluation reports.

candidates.title: survival instructor
candidates.description: Survival instructors guide groups into vast, natural areas, and assist them in a self-directed instruction of basic survival needs without any comfort facilities or modern gear to fall back on. They coach the participants into mastering survival skills such as fire making, producing primitive equipment, shelter construction and procurement of water and nourishment. They ensure the participants are aware of certain safety measures without diminishing the level of adventure, of environment protection and of risk management. They encourage efforts of leadership from the group and mentor the participants individually so as to push their limits responsibly and help overcome potential fears.

candidates.title: advanced nurse practitioner
candidates.description: Advanced nurse practitioners are in charge of promoting and restoring patients` health, provide diagnosis and care in advanced settings, coordinating care within areas of chronic disease management, providing integrated care, and supervising assigned team members. Advanced nurse practitioners are general care nurses who have acquired an expert knowledge base, complex decision making skills and clinical competencies for expanded clinical practice on advanced level.

description: Nurse Grade U9 responsible for implementing patient care and treatment, health education and promotion, patient monitoring and safety, equipment and medications used, as well as management, planning, training, and research duties to enhance and maintain the quality of nursing services.
tasks: Nursing supervision. Regulating patient care by conducting scheduled ward/clinic/unit rounds to monitor the effectiveness of care, equipment, and patient safety. Conducting monitoring of nursing practice services at the hospital level and determine Nursing projections. Strengthening nursing practices, medical programmes, and training. Planning nursing and care services in line with the advancements in science and technology, as well as current concepts. Supervising the formation and career development of nursing personnel through in-service training, courses, research, and development. Planning supervisory visits to ensure nursing practices are conducted according to standards. Coordinating Quality Assurance programmes at the hospital level, identifying areas of weakness in service quality and implementing corrective actions, as well as prepare reports. Infection control – ensuring all nursing personnel receive training in infection control and monitors and evaluates the effectiveness of infection control in the hospital. Planning and coordinating training courses required for nursing personnel at the hospital level.

candidates.title: nurse assistant
candidates.description: Nurse assistants provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. They perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, move patients or change linens and may transfer or transport patients.

candidates.title: specialist nurse
candidates.description: Specialist nurses promote and restore people's health, and diagnose and care within a specific branch of the nursing field. Examples of such specialist nursing jobs include but are not restricted to; ambulatory care nurse, advanced practice nurse, cardiac nurse, dental nurse, community health nurse, forensic nurse, gastroenterology nurse, hospice and palliative care nurse, paediatric nurse, public health nurse, rehabilitation nurse, renal nurse and school nurse. Specialist nurses are general care nurses prepared beyond the level of a nurse generalist and authorised to practice as specialists with specific expertise in a branch of the nursing field.

candidates.title: nurse responsible for general care
candidates.description: Nurses responsible for general care are in charge of promoting and restoring patients` health by providing physical and psychological support to patients, friends, and families. They also supervise assigned team members.

candidates.title: nursing lecturer
candidates.description: Nursing lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, nursing, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of nursing, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: veterinary nurse
candidates.description: Veterinary nurses support animals undergoing veterinary treatment and give advice to veterinary clients in the promotion of animal health and disease prevention in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: advanced nurse practitioner
candidates.description: Advanced nurse practitioners are in charge of promoting and restoring patients` health, provide diagnosis and care in advanced settings, coordinating care within areas of chronic disease management, providing integrated care, and supervising assigned team members. Advanced nurse practitioners are general care nurses who have acquired an expert knowledge base, complex decision making skills and clinical competencies for expanded clinical practice on advanced level.

candidates.title: midwife
candidates.description: Midwives assist women in childbirth by providing the necessary support, care and advice during pregnancy, labour and the postpartum period, conduct births and provide care for the new-born. They advise on health, preventive measures, preparation for parenthood, detection of complications in mother and child, accessing of medical care, promoting normal birth and carrying out emergency measures.

candidates.title: nanny
candidates.description: Nannies provide qualified care services to children on the premises of the employer. They organise play activities and entertain children with games and other cultural and educative activities according to their respective age, prepare meals, give them bathes, transport them from and to school and assist them with homework on a punctual basis.

description: Professional Midwife provides comprehensive care to a woman throughout pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period. They manage normal deliveries, conduct routine antenatal and postnatal check-ups, support the mother emotionally and physically during labour, and advise on infant care and breastfeeding. They work collaboratively with a doctor and other health professionals to ensure the health of both mother and newborn, and refer high-risk cases as needed.
tasks: Perform routine antenatal examinations to monitor maternal and fetal health. Advise expectant mothers on diet, exercise, pregnancy care, and preparation for childbirth. Manage labour and normal deliveries, assisting doctors when required. Monitor vital signs and labour progress during childbirth. Conduct routine postnatal evaluations and identify complications for referral when required. Provide guidance on breastfeeding and infant care. Monitor newborn health and identify complications requiring further medical attention.

candidates.title: midwife
candidates.description: Midwives assist women in childbirth by providing the necessary support, care and advice during pregnancy, labour and the postpartum period, conduct births and provide care for the new-born. They advise on health, preventive measures, preparation for parenthood, detection of complications in mother and child, accessing of medical care, promoting normal birth and carrying out emergency measures.

candidates.title: maternity support worker
candidates.description: Maternity support workers work together in a team with midwives and health professionals within the occupational fields of nursing and midwifery. They assist midwives and women in childbirth by providing the necessary support, care and advice during pregnancy, labour and the postpartum period, assist births and assist in providing care for the new-born.

candidates.title: auxiliary nursing and midwifery vocational teacher
candidates.description: Auxiliary nursing and midwifery vocational teachers instruct students in their specialised field of study, auxiliary nursing and midwifery, which is predominantly practical in nature. They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques the students must subsequently master. Auxiliary nursing and midwifery vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of auxiliary nursing and midwifery through assignments, tests and examinations.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: child care worker
candidates.description: Child care workers provide care for children when the parents or family members are unavailable. They look after the children's basic needs and help or supervise them during play. Child care workers can work for preschools, daycare centres, childcare agencies or individual families.

candidates.title: home care aide
candidates.description: Home care aides provide personal assistance and promote autonomy, on a daily basis to individuals who are unable to take care of themselves due to illness, ageing or disability. They assist them with personal hygiene, feeding, communication or medication according to the health care professional's instructions.

description: Paramedic provides urgent medical care and support to an individual experiencing illness, injury, or other health impairments. They respond to an emergency call, assess the patient on-site, administer life-saving interventions such as CPR and medications, and transport the patient safely to a healthcare facility. Operating primarily outside hospital settings, the paramedic serves as the first point of contact in emergencies, ensuring timely and effective medical response.
tasks: Respond promptly to emergency calls and assess patient conditions on site. Perform emergency procedures. Administer authorised emergency medications as required. Provide emergency treatment to stabilise patients and preserve life before and during transport. Transport patients safely to hospitals while continuing medical care en route. Accurately document patient assessments, treatments, and relevant observations. Maintain and clean ambulances and emergency medical equipment to ensure operational readiness. Coordinate with hospital staff to ensure smooth handover and continuity of care.

candidates.title: paramedic in emergency responses
candidates.description: Paramedics in emergency responses provide emergency care to sick, injured, and vulnerable persons in emergency medical situations, before and during transport to a medical facility. They implement and oversee the transfer of the patient in connection with transport. They provide assistance in acute situations, implement life-saving emergency measures, and monitor the performance of the transportation process. As allowed by national law they may also provide oxygen, certain drugs, the puncture of peripheral veins and infusion of crystalloid solutions and perform endotracheal intubation if needed for the immediate prevention of threats for the life or health of an emergency patient.

candidates.title: emergency ambulance driver
candidates.description: Emergency ambulance drivers use emergency vehicles to respond to medical emergencies and support the work of paramedics, move patients safely, take note of changes in the patient's vital signs and report to the paramedics in charge, ensuring the medical equipment is well stored, transported and functional, under supervision and on order of a doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: emergency medical dispatcher
candidates.description: Emergency medical dispatchers respond to urgent calls made to the control center, take information about the emergency situation, the address and other details and dispatch the nearest ambulance or paramedic helicopter.

candidates.title: emergency response worker
candidates.description: Emergency response workers work in missions to aid in emergency and disaster situations, such as natural disasters or oil spills. They clean up the debris or waste caused by the event, ensure the people involved are brought to safety, prevent further damage, and transport goods such as food and medical supplies.

candidates.title: firefighter
candidates.description: Firefighters are responsible for emergency response in case of a fire outbreak or other hazardous situations. They oversee the evacuation of the endangered premises and ensure victims are rescued and taken care of by the appropriate professionals. Once the premises are clear of victims, they ensure the fire is extinguished, compliant with health and safety regulations. They also regulate the clean-up of the scene and assess the damage.

candidates.title: emergency response coordinator
candidates.description: Emergency response coordinators analyse potential risks such as disasters and emergencies for a community or institution and develop a strategy for reacting to these risks. They outline guidelines for the response to an emergency in order to decrease the effects. They educate the parties at risk on these guidelines. They also test response plans and ensure that the necessary supplies and equipments are in place in compliance with health and safety regulations.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: first aid instructor
candidates.description: First aid instructors teach students immediate lifesaving emergency measures, such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the recovery position, and injury care. They provided practice materials such as a specialised manikin.

description: Veterinarian diagnoses, treats, and prevents diseases, disorders, and injuries in an animal, providing care for pets, livestock, and wildlife. They conduct a physical examination, perform surgical procedures, prescribe medications, and advise an owner, farmer, or handler on animal health, nutrition, vaccination, and disease prevention. Their work may also include research, disease surveillance, laboratory testing, regulatory inspections, and contributions to public health, animal welfare, and the development of medicines and strategies for controlling animal diseases.
tasks: Conduct physical and clinical examinations to assess the health of animals. Diagnose animal diseases and develop appropriate treatment and prevention plans. Administer medical and surgical treatments, including vaccinations, emergency care and obstetric procedures. Collect, analyse and interpret tissue, fluid and laboratory samples to detect disease. Perform necropsies to determine the causes of disease or death. Advise animal owners, handlers and farmers on nutrition, hygiene, breeding, general care and disease prevention. Monitor and improve animal and livestock health, including epidemiological surveillance and outbreak investigation. Inspect livestock, farm operations and food products of animal origin to ensure safety, quality and compliance with regulations. Train, supervise and collaborate with veterinary technicians, assistants and interdisciplinary teams on animal health and disease control.

candidates.title: official veterinarian
candidates.description: Official veterinarians are professionals with a comprehensive scientific education. They have the authority to carry out, in an independent, ethical and personally responsible capacity all veterinary activities with particular focus on the health and welfare of animals and public health in accordance with national and international legislation. They are responsible for national animal disease eradication programmes, the protection of public health and food or animal inspection, animal movements, and import and export of live animals and their products.

candidates.title: veterinary nurse
candidates.description: Veterinary nurses support animals undergoing veterinary treatment and give advice to veterinary clients in the promotion of animal health and disease prevention in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: specialised veterinarian
candidates.description: Specialised veterinarians are professionals with a comprehensive scientific education. They have the authority to carry out, in an independent, ethical and personally responsible capacity, all aspects of veterinary medicine, in the interest of the health and welfare of animals and public health in accordance with national and international legislation. In addition they need a recognized qualification and/or experience in a specific species and/or veterinary procedure.

candidates.title: general veterinarian
candidates.description: General veterinarians are professionals with a comprehensive scientific education. They have the authority to carry out, in an independent, ethical and personally responsible capacity, all aspects of veterinary medicine, in the interest of the health and welfare of animals and public health in accordance with national and international legislation. The generalist veterinarian can work with any species, however they may choose to work with a single species or types such as equine, companion or production animals.

candidates.title: veterinary technician
candidates.description: Veterinary technicians provide the technical and administrative support to the veterinarian in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: veterinary scientist
candidates.description: Veterinary scientist develop and do research in animal models, compare basic biology across animals, and translate research findings to different species, including humans.

candidates.title: veterinary medicine lecturer
candidates.description: Veterinary medicine lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, veterinary medicine, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of veterinary medicine, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: veterinary receptionist
candidates.description: Veterinary receptionists provide reception and office/administrative support in a veterinary practice, scheduling appointments and receiving clients, sale and advice on animal related products, in accordance with national legislation.

description: Veterinary Officer Grade GV9 responsible for controlling animal and zoonotic diseases and providing clinical treatment, ensuring that animal-based protein foods are disease-free and safe for entry into the human food chain, planning and implementing development, maintenance, and improvement of livestock quality, enforcing import and export laws on animal and livestock products in accordance with international regulations (WOAH, WTO, FAO, etc.), preparing technical and general reports on the department’s development and annual progress, and performing other departmental administrative duties in accordance with the specific requirements and guidelines of the World Organization for Animal Health (WOAH-formerly known as OIE) for Good Veterinary Governance and Quality Veterinary Services.
tasks: Conducting health examinations, disease investigations, tentative and differential diagnoses in animals based on clinical signs and post-mortem findings. Providing clinical treatment (e.g., administration of veterinary medicines, clinical procedures, and issuance of prescriptions), performing minor elective surgeries, and assisting in major surgeries (assistant surgeon). Implementing control and prevention measures (metaphylaxis and prophylaxis) to prevent disease spread, including disinfection, vaccination, treatment, culling, disposal, and livestock movement control. Performing bacteriological, virological, parasitological, pathological, and other diagnostic tests on animal disease samples. Reviewing and certifying Veterinary Health Certificates for the movement of live animals. Conducting document and field inspections on animal health, premises (slaughterhouses and processing plants), livestock products (domestic and international), and animal feed to ensure quality and safety under departmental certification programmes (GAHP, MyGAP, MYOrganik, VHM, GMP, GVHP, and other relevant certifications). Inspecting the use of veterinary medicines and biologics to ensure compliance with prescriptions and usage instructions. Conducting breeding soundness examinations and livestock suitability assessments for breeding purposes, including pregnancy diagnosis. Providing advisory services covering technical advice on animal health and welfare, veterinary public health, regulatory, legal, and livestock industry development aspects. Preparing training modules and course schedules.

candidates.title: animal facility manager
candidates.description: Animal facility managers coordinate and plan all activities of a zoo. They formulate policies, manage daily operations, and plan the use of materials and human resources. They are the driving force and public face of their institution. This often involves representing their institution on a national, regional and global scale and taking part in coordinated zoo activities.

description: Dentist diagnoses, treats, and prevents diseases, injuries, and abnormalities of the teeth, mouth, jaws, and related tissues, applying modern dentistry principles and procedures. They perform clinical treatments including preventive care, restorations, extractions, root canal therapy, prosthetic fittings, and may carry out surgical interventions for functional or aesthetic purposes. Their work also involves creating a treatment plan, consulting with a patient, educating on oral hygiene. In specialised roles, examining oral tissues and collaborating with other health professionals to ensure accurate diagnosis and comprehensive care.
tasks: Provide dental care, including examinations, cleaning, fillings, extractions, crowns, bridges, and root canal treatments. Conduct patient consultations to diagnose oral diseases and advise on appropriate treatment. Perform dental surgical procedures, including the management of impacted teeth, when required. Administer local anaesthesia and prescribe medications as required. Perform clinical assessments of oral lesions and interpret relevant pathology findings when applicable. Provide post-operative care, follow-up, and patient management guidance.

candidates.title: dental practitioner
candidates.description: Dental practitioners prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues.

candidates.title: specialist dentist
candidates.description: Specialist dentists prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues specialised in oral surgery or orthodontics.

candidates.title: dental hygienist
candidates.description: Dental hygienists work in cleaning and polishing teeth, supra- and sub-gingival scaling of the teeth, application of prophylactic materials to the teeth, collecting data, administering comprehensive advice on oral hygiene and the care of the mouth, according to patients` needs under the supervision of dental practitioners following her/his directions.

candidates.title: dentistry lecturer
candidates.description: Dentistry lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, dentistry, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of dentistry, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: dental technician
candidates.description: Dental technicians manufacture dental custom-made devices like bridges, crowns, dentures and appliances under the supervision of dental practitioners following their directions and specifications.

candidates.title: equine dental technician
candidates.description: Equine dental technicians provide routine equine dental care, using appropriate equipment in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: dental chairside assistant
candidates.description: Dental chairside assistants support dental practitioners in clinical treatments, as preparation and helping in practical execution and follow-up, and administrative tasks under supervision and following the orders of the dental practitioner.

candidates.title: enameller
candidates.description: Enamellers embellish metals such as gold, silver, copper, steel, cast iron or platinum by painting it. The enamel they apply, consists of coloured powdered glass.

description: Dental Officer Grade UG9 responsible for enhancing the standard of health and quality of life of the community through dental treatment and preventive oral health activities.
tasks: Responsible to the Senior Assistant Director for the implementation of all clinical activities and dental health promotion in accordance with the policies and objectives of the Ministry of Health Malaysia. Implementing and ensuring that patients receive quality dental services in accordance with established service policies. Conducting oral health education activities, including delivering dental talks and organising exhibitions for health promotion. Performing emergency (on-call) duties after office hours. Assisting senior dental officers in the implementation, supervision, and evaluation of dental service programmes. Participating in quality improvement initiatives conducted for clinic dental services, including ISO implementation, innovation projects, and KMK. Participating in studies related to dental health conducted at the clinic. Referring complex cases to Dental Specialists for cases requiring specialist treatment.

candidates.title: specialist dentist
candidates.description: Specialist dentists prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues specialised in oral surgery or orthodontics.

candidates.title: dental chairside assistant
candidates.description: Dental chairside assistants support dental practitioners in clinical treatments, as preparation and helping in practical execution and follow-up, and administrative tasks under supervision and following the orders of the dental practitioner.
