Furthermore health physics is applied at facilities where people are exposed to ionizing radiation such as nuclear power plants and research institutions.

candidates.title: medical administrative assistant
candidates.description: Medical administrative assistants work very closely with health professionals. They provide office support such as correspondence, fixing appointments and answering queries of patients.

candidates.title: physiotherapy assistant
candidates.description: Physiotherapy assistants work under supervision, within defined contexts using agreed treatment protocols and procedures such as collecting client data and maintaining the equipment required in physiotherapy interventions. The overall responsibility is retained by the delegating professional.

candidates.title: occupational therapist
candidates.description: Occupational therapists assist individuals or groups who have occupational limitations due to diseases, physical disorders, and temporary or permanent mental disabilities, in regaining their ability to perform daily activities. They provide treatment and rehabilitation to enable them to actively participate in society, to live their lives according to their wishes and to perform those activities that are meaningful to them. Occupational therapists work in public health and social care services, but can also be involved in supporting asylum seekers, refugees and/or homeless people.

candidates.title: healthcare institution manager
candidates.description: Healthcare institution managers supervise the operations of healthcare institutions, such as hospitals, rehabilitation facilities, home care services and elderly care institutions to ensure the organisation meets requirements, the patients and residents are cared for, the organisation is maintained and the necessary equipment present. They also supervise the staff and ensure record maintenance.

candidates.title: recreation policy officer
candidates.description: Recreation policy officers research, analyse and develop policies in the sports and recreation sector and implement these policies in order to improve the sport and recreation system and improve the health of the population. They strive to increase the participation in sports, support athletes, enhance the performance of athletes in national and international competitions, improve social inclusion and community development. They work closely with partners, external organisations or other stakeholders and provide them with regular updates.

description: Dietitian plans, implements, and supervises diet for an individual or group, addressing nutritional needs to manage or prevent health conditions. They assess dietary requirements, develop a personalised nutrition plan, and monitor outcomes, while providing guidance on healthy eating and promoting nutrition education in communities, schools, and healthcare settings. Their work supports overall health, wellness, and public health objectives.
tasks: Conduct nutritional assessments and interpret relevant health and biochemical data to determine dietary requirements. Plan and implement personalised meal plans based on medical conditions and lifestyle goals. Provide dietary counselling, nutrition education, and guidance on healthy eating to individuals and groups. Monitor patient or client progress and adjust nutrition interventions as needed. Supervise food preparation and meal service to ensure dietary accuracy, quality, and compliance with prescribed requirements. Manage and monitor dietetic services in clinical, community, or institutional settings. Develop and implement nutrition programmes and wellness initiatives for institutions or communities. Provide guidance on therapeutic diets and clinical nutrition standards.

candidates.title: dietitian
candidates.description: Dietitians assess specific nutritional requirements of populations or individuals throughout their lives and translate this into advice which will maintain, reduce risk to, or restore people’s health. Using evidence-based approaches, dietitians work to empower individuals, families and groups to provide or select food which is nutritionally adequate, safe, tasty and sustainable. Beyond healthcare, dietitians improve the nutritional environment for all through governments, industry, academia and research.

candidates.title: dietetic technician
candidates.description: Dietetic technicians assist dietitians in planning nutritional programmes and in planning menus for patients as part of an overall treatment plan under supervision of a dietitian. Under supervision of a dietitian, dietetic technicians assist dietitians in patient reviews, enteral feeding discharge planning, and clinical auditing which includes nutritional screening.

candidates.title: prepared meals nutritionist
candidates.description: Prepared meals nutritionists value ingredients, manufacturing processes, and foodstuffs in order to assure nutritional quality and suitability of prepared meals and dishes. They study nutritional value of foodstuffs and dishes and advise on the composition of different meals or dishes for human feed, allergenic items and macro and micronutrients.

candidates.title: diet cook
candidates.description: Diet cooks prepare and present meals according to special dietary or nutrition needs.

candidates.title: weight loss consultant
candidates.description: Weight loss consultants assist clients in obtaining and maintaining a healthy lifestyle. They advise on how to lose weight by finding a balance between healthy food and exercise. Weight loss consultants set goals together with their clients and keep track of progress during weekly meetings.

candidates.title: animal feed nutritionist
candidates.description: Animal feed nutritionists analyse the nutritional value of animal feeds in order to provide dietary advice to agricultural, manufacturing, zoological and public sector staff. They undertake research on nutritionally balanced food stuffs and maintain awareness of technical and scientific developments on the subject.

candidates.title: food safety specialist
candidates.description: Food safety specialists organise processes and implement procedures to avoid problems with food safety. They comply with regulations.

candidates.title: food biotechnologist
candidates.description: Food biotechnologists study the life cycle of food from its preservation up to the spoilage and the food-borne pathogens. They research and understand food-borne diseases in order to prevent them. They ensure that food products abide by government regulations regarding food health and safety.

description: Dietetics Officer Grade U9 responsible for carrying out tasks related to the management and monitoring of clinical dietetic and community services, planning and providing nutritious and appropriate meals based on the Hospital Diet Manual, giving advice to patients requiring therapeutic diets, and planning and implementing training and research activities related to the field.
tasks: Implementing steps in the nutrition care process, such as nutritional assessment, nutritional prescription, nutrition monitoring, and evaluation for each inpatient or outpatient referred by a doctor to achieve an optimal level of health. Supervising food preparation operations to ensure that normal diets, therapeutic diets, or tube feeding provided to patients are correct, according to prescriptions, and meet care quality standards. Providing training on diet preparation to Cooks, Hostel Supervisors, and Assistant Food Preparation Officers. Attending to acute patients such as those in intensive care, burn patients, and other critically ill patients who require careful diet/feeding regime monitoring. Ensuring patients are given diet prescriptions, understanding how to manage their diet, and attending follow-up care if necessary. Contributing to programmes/activities in health promotion and disease prevention services for hospitals, health clinics, organisations, and the mass media. Focusing on further developing the clinical dietetic specialty to align with treatment advancements implemented by doctors.

candidates.title: dietetic technician

candidates.title: food analyst
candidates.description: Food analysts perform standardised tests to determine the chemical, physical, or microbiological features of products for human consumption.

description: Food Preparation Officer Grade C9 responsible for managing menu planning and the procurement of food ingredients required in standard recipes, and ensuring that food is prepared safely, hygienically, and to a high standard in compliance with established guidelines. Responsible in carrying out procurement of wet/raw and dry food items, managing food storage, pre-preparation cooking and serving food and ensure it is carried out according to established procedures. Supervising members under supervision to ensure compliance with discipline, task execution procedures and occupational safety regulations.
tasks: Placing orders or procures wet/raw and dry food, enteral formulas, infant milk formulas, and special products, and ensuring receipt complies with orders and contract specifications. Managing food and stock storage, including bulk stores, sub-stores, daily stores, chillers, and freezers, in accordance with storage procedures, stock record systems, hygiene, and safety requirements. Supervising and ensuring food preparation complies with menus and standard recipes for normal diets, therapeutic diets, children’s diets, and doctor-on-call diets, while producing high-quality culinary output. Planning menus and standard recipes, including diets with consistent modifications and nutrients. Determining compliance with established quality indicators from the stage of receiving wet/raw and dry food from suppliers to food served to patients. Performing administrative duties related to food services. Ensuring personnel under supervision observe personal hygiene in every work process handled. Recording inventory and capital assets, and inspecting and updating equipment stock to ensure accuracy of equipment records.

candidates.title: food production manager
candidates.description: Food production managers oversee and monitor production and have overall responsibility for staffing and related issues. Hence, they have a detailed knowledge of the manufacturing products and their production processes. On the one hand, they control process parameters and their influence on the product and on the other hand, they ensure that staffing and recruitment levels are adequate.

candidates.title: food safety specialist
candidates.description: Food safety specialists organise processes and implement procedures to avoid problems with food safety. They comply with regulations.

candidates.title: food production operator
candidates.description: Food production operators supply and perform one or more tasks in different stages of the food production process. They perform manufacturing operations and processes to foods and beverages, perform packaging, operate machines manually or automatically, follow predetermined procedures, and take food safety regulations on board.

candidates.title: food production planner
candidates.description: Food production planners prepare production plans, evaluate all the variables in the process and strive to ensure that production objectives be achieved.

candidates.title: food production engineer
candidates.description: Food production engineers oversee the electrical and mechanical needs of the equipment and machinery required in the process of manufacturing food or beverages. They strive to maximise plant productivity by engaging in preventive actions in reference to health and safety, good manufacturing practices (GMP), hygiene compliance, and performance of routine maintenance of machines and equipment.

description: Audiologist assesses, diagnoses, and manages hearing, balance, and related communication disorders across all age groups. They provide treatments such as hearing aids, auditory rehabilitation, and counselling, and collaborate with other healthcare professionals to ensure comprehensive patient care. They work in a hospital, clinic, or educational setting to support auditory and vestibular health.
tasks: Conduct hearing and balance assessments for patients of all ages using appropriate diagnostic equipment. Diagnose auditory and vestibular disorders based on assessment findings. Fit, programme, and evaluate hearing aids and other assistive listening devices for patient use. Provide auditory rehabilitation, counselling, and hearing management education to patients and caregivers. Interpret and communicate assessment results to patients, caregivers, and healthcare teams. Develop and refine clinical testing procedures to improve diagnostic accuracy and patient outcomes. Maintain accurate patient records and clinical documentation. Advise patients on the selection, use, and maintenance of hearing aids and related assistive devices. Refer patients to medical specialists or other healthcare professionals when required.

candidates.title: audiologist
candidates.description: Audiologists assess, diagnose and treat patients ( children or adults) with audiological and vestibular disorders caused by infectious, genetic, traumatic or degenerative conditions, such as hearing loss, tinnitus, dizziness, imbalance, hyperacusis and auditory processing difficulties. They can prescribe a hearing aid and have a role in assessing and managing patients who may benefit from cochlear implants.

candidates.title: audiology technician
candidates.description: Audiology technicians create and service hearing aids and hearing protection products. They dispense, fit and provide hearing aids for those who need them.

candidates.title: audio production technician
candidates.description: Audio production technicians set up, prepare, check and maintain equipment in order to provide optimal sound quality for a live performance. They cooperate with road crew to unload, set up and operate sound equipment and instruments.

candidates.title: audio-visual technician
candidates.description: Audio-visual technicians set up, operate and maintain equipment to record and edit images and sound for radio and television broadcasts, at live events and for telecommunication signals.

candidates.title: audiology equipment shop manager
candidates.description: Audiology equipment shop managers assume responsibility for activities and staff in specialised shops.

candidates.title: audiology equipment specialised seller
candidates.description: Audiology equipment specialised seller sell goods and equipment in specialised shops.

candidates.title: diagnostic radiographer
candidates.description: Diagnostic radiographers plan, prepare and perform diagnostic imaging examinations and post processing, with a wide range of equipment and techniques using X-rays, strong magnetic fields or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and high frequency sound (Ultrasound).

candidates.title: speech and language therapist
candidates.description: Speech and language therapists focus on the aetiology, assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of communication and swallowing disorders in people of all ages in order to help them maintain, promote, improve, initiate, or recover the ability to communicate both verbally and nonverbally. They address the development of language, speech, vocal and hearing functions, and disorders and disabilities in the cranial, facial, and oral area.

description: Speech Therapist assesses, diagnoses, and treats communication and swallowing disorders across all age groups, helping a patient improve verbal and nonverbal communication as well as oral and facial functions. They develop an individualised therapy plan, apply specialised techniques, and monitor patient progress while collaborating with healthcare and educational professionals. They work in a hospital, rehabilitation centre, school, or private clinic to support effective and holistic outcomes.
tasks: Conduct assessments of speech, language, communication, and swallowing disorders using standardised tools, and interpret the results to inform treatment decisions. Develop individualised treatment plans based on assessment results. Provide therapy through individual or group sessions tailored to patient needs. Educate patients, families, and caregivers on communication strategies and home-based techniques. Document and monitor patient progress, update care plans regularly, and maintain therapy reports and clinical documentation. Collaborate with doctors, teachers, psychologists, occupational therapists, and other relevant professionals to ensure holistic care. Develop and improve therapy and assessment techniques, and provide related clinical support.

candidates.title: speech and language therapist
candidates.description: Speech and language therapists focus on the aetiology, assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of communication and swallowing disorders in people of all ages in order to help them maintain, promote, improve, initiate, or recover the ability to communicate both verbally and nonverbally. They address the development of language, speech, vocal and hearing functions, and disorders and disabilities in the cranial, facial, and oral area.

candidates.title: music therapist
candidates.description: Music therapists use music-therapeutic interventions to treat patients with behavioural disorders and pathogenic conditions to prevent, mitigate or eliminate symptoms and to change behaviours and attitudes requiring treatment. They promote and maintain or restore the development, maturity and health of the patient/client by music-therapeutic interventions. Music therapy especially provides help for people with with emotional, somatic, intellectually or socially induced behavioural disorders and pathogenic conditions, such as psychoses (schizophrenic disorders, bipolar disorders) and personality development disorders.

candidates.title: public speaking coach
candidates.description: Public speaking coaches provide, often private, instruction to clients in theory and techniques on how to improve their public speaking skills. They identify each client's strengths and weaknesses and tailor their instruction to their specific needs, which may include improving the client's vocal delivery, articulation, presentation abilities and body language. Depending on the background of the client, be it business, education or otherwise, public speaking coaches also instruct clients or students in persuasive arguing, rhetorical delivery and other debating techniques.

candidates.title: art therapist
candidates.description: Art therapists help patients overcome psychological and emotional difficulties through an artistic process which reflects emotions and feelings, focusing on patients who suffer a variety of problems such as mental, psychological, and behavioural disorders in order to facilitate self-understanding and awareness.

candidates.title: audiologist
candidates.description: Audiologists assess, diagnose and treat patients ( children or adults) with audiological and vestibular disorders caused by infectious, genetic, traumatic or degenerative conditions, such as hearing loss, tinnitus, dizziness, imbalance, hyperacusis and auditory processing difficulties. They can prescribe a hearing aid and have a role in assessing and managing patients who may benefit from cochlear implants.

candidates.title: occupational therapist
candidates.description: Occupational therapists assist individuals or groups who have occupational limitations due to diseases, physical disorders, and temporary or permanent mental disabilities, in regaining their ability to perform daily activities. They provide treatment and rehabilitation to enable them to actively participate in society, to live their lives according to their wishes and to perform those activities that are meaningful to them. Occupational therapists work in public health and social care services, but can also be involved in supporting asylum seekers, refugees and/or homeless people.

candidates.title: speechwriter
candidates.description: Speechwriters research and write speeches on multiple topics. They need to catch and hold the interest of an audience. Speechwriters create presentations in a conversational tone so it looks like if the text was not scripted. They write in a comprehensible manner so the audience gets the message of the speech.

candidates.title: psychotherapist
candidates.description: Psychotherapists assist and treat healthcare users with varying degrees of psychological, psychosocial, or psychosomatic behavioural disorders and pathogenic conditions by means of psychotherapeutic methods. They promote personal development and well-being and provide advice on improving relationships, capabilities, and problem-solving techniques. They use science-based psychotherapeutic methods such as behavioural therapy, existential analysis and logotherapy, psychoanalysis or systemic family therapy in order to guide the patients in their development and help them search for appropriate solutions to their problems. Psychotherapists are not required to have academic degrees in psychology or a medical qualification in psychiatry. It is an independent occupation from psychology, psychiatry, and counselling.

description: Orthoepist specialises in the correct pronunciation of words and the promotion of standard language usage, providing assessment, diagnosis, and treatment for speech, language, voice, fluency, and swallowing disorders across all ages. They support an individual in improving communication and daily functioning, often collaborating with families, educators, and healthcare or rehabilitation professionals to develop a personalised therapy and rehabilitation plan. Their work enhances overall quality of life by combining language correction, functional support, and evidence-based interventions in both clinical and community settings.
tasks: Conduct assessments to evaluate speech, language, voice, fluency, and swallowing disorders across all age groups. Design and implement individualised treatment, rehabilitation, or therapy plans based on assessment findings. Deliver speech, language, voice, fluency, and swallowing therapy sessions in person or via telepractice. Train clients and caregivers in communication strategies and the safe use of assistive communication devices where appropriate. Monitor patient progress and treatment effectiveness, and adjust intervention plans accordingly. Provide counselling, education, and guidance to patients, caregivers, educators, and other relevant professionals. Document assessments, interventions, and patient progress, and coordinate with healthcare and education professionals. Refer patients to relevant specialists and collaborate with healthcare or rehabilitation teams for integrated care.

candidates.title: orthoptist
candidates.description: Orthoptists diagnose and treat anomalies of binocular vision. They examine, assess and treat vision impairments, squint, amblyopia and eye motility disorders. Orthoptists apply these methods in particular in the fields of paediatrics, neurology, neuro-ophthalmology, ophthalmology, orthoptics, optometry, pleoptics and strabology assessing functional diseases of the eye for improving functional disorders of the visual system. They also provide counselling, preventive measures and training activities and may refract and prescribe glasses, such as prism corrective glasses.

candidates.title: prosthetist-orthotist
candidates.description: Prosthetist-orthotists design and custom fit prostheses and orthoses for individuals who are missing a limb from accident, disease or congenital conditions or for individuals who have impairments, deficiences or weaknesses due to injury, pathology or congenital malformation. They mix patient care with the design and fabrication of these devices to address their patients' needs.

candidates.title: speech and language therapist
candidates.description: Speech and language therapists focus on the aetiology, assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of communication and swallowing disorders in people of all ages in order to help them maintain, promote, improve, initiate, or recover the ability to communicate both verbally and nonverbally. They address the development of language, speech, vocal and hearing functions, and disorders and disabilities in the cranial, facial, and oral area.

candidates.title: typist
candidates.description: Typists operate computers to type and revise documents and compile material to be typed, such as correspondence, reports, statistical tables, forms, and audios. They read instructions accompanying material or follow verbal instructions to determine requirements such as number of copies needed, priority and desired format.

candidates.title: aromatherapist
candidates.description: Aromatherapists use essential oils extracted from herbal products at the level of the interface skin and mucous membranes to improve the clients` well-being. They treat a variety of illnesses and physical or psychological conditions, under supervision and on a doctor's order.

candidates.title: orthopaedic footwear technician
candidates.description: Orthopaedic footwear technicians design footwear and make patterns, using manufacturing technology. They compensate and accommodate foot and ankle fitting problems and design and manufacture footwear and its orthopaedic components, including orthoses, insoles, soles and others.

candidates.title: prosthetic-orthotics technician
candidates.description: Prosthetic-orthotics technicians design, create, fit and repair supportive devices, such as braces, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.

candidates.title: orthopaedic supply shop manager
candidates.description: Orthopaedic supply shop managers assume responsibility for activities and staff in specialised shops.They manage employees, monitor the sales of the store, manage budgets and order supplies when a product is out of supply and perform administrative duties if required.

description: Optometrist examines, diagnoses, and manages disorders of the eye and visual system, including vision problems, eye diseases, and abnormalities. They prescribe corrective lenses, optical aids, or other therapies, conduct routine eye assessments, and provide guidance on maintaining eye health. Their work may involve specialised areas such as eye movement and coordination disorders, and they collaborate with an ophthalmologist or other specialists when advanced treatment is required.
tasks: Conduct comprehensive eye examinations to assess vision, eye alignment, eye movement, and overall visual function. Diagnose visual, binocular, and related eye disorders, including refractive errors, strabismus, amblyopia, and other abnormalities. Prescribe, dispense, and fit corrective lenses, contact lenses, prisms, and other visual aids. Develop and implement non-surgical treatment and management plans, including vision therapy and low vision interventions. Monitor patient progress and adjust treatment plans or visual aids as needed. Provide pre-operative and post-operative eye care guidance in coordination with ophthalmologists or other specialists. Educate patients and families on eye health, visual hygiene, and the proper use and care of visual aids. Collaborate with healthcare professionals to support integrated eye care and appropriate follow-up treatment.

candidates.title: optometrist
candidates.description: Optometrists examine and test eyes to identify abnormalities, visual problems, or disease. They prescribe and fit lenses such as spectacles and contacts, and offer advice on visual problems. They may also refer patients to a medical practitioner. Their scope of practice and title varies according to national regulations.

candidates.title: optician
candidates.description: Opticians help to improve and correct an individual's vision. They fit spectacle lenses and frames, contact lenses, and other devices according to the specifications of the individual. Their scope of practice varies according to national regulations and they might operate according to prescriptions provided by a specialised doctor in ophthalmology or an optometrist in the countries where requested.

candidates.title: optical technician
candidates.description: Optical technicians assemble, repair and design various parts of eyewear such as lenses, frames, patterns and eyewear. They cut, inspect, mount and polish all parts using various machinery and hand tools. Optical technicians shape, grind and coat lenses for prescription eyewear. They fit completed lenses into eyeglass frames. Optical technicians ensure that lenses conform to the dispensing optician’s, specialised doctor in ophtalmology's or optometrist's prescriptions. They may also work with other associated optical instrumentation and its maintenance.

candidates.title: eyewear and optical equipment specialised seller
candidates.description: Eyewear and optical equipment specialised sellers sell glasses in specialised shops.

candidates.title: optomechanical engineering technician
candidates.description: Optomechanical engineering technicians collaborate with engineers in the development of optomechanical devices, such as optical tables, deformable mirrors, and optical mounts. Optomechanical engineering technicians build, install, test, and maintain optomechanical equipment prototypes. They determine materials and assembly requirements.

candidates.title: eyewear and optical equipment shop manager
candidates.description: Eyewear and optical equipment shop managers assume responsibility for activities and staff in specialised shops.

candidates.title: optomechanical engineer
candidates.description: Optomechanical engineers design and develop optomechanical systems, devices, and components, such as optical mirrors and optical mounts. Optomechanical engineering combines optical engineering with mechanical engineering in the design of these systems and devices. They conduct research, perform analysis, test the devices, and supervise the research.

candidates.title: optoelectronic engineering technician
candidates.description: Optoelectronic engineering technicians collaborate with engineers in the development of optoelectronic systems and components, such as photodiodes, optical sensors, lasers and LED's. Optoelectronic engineering technicians build, test, install and calibrate optoelectronic equipment. They read blueprint and other technical drawings to develop testing and calibrating procedures.

description: Optometry Officer Grade U9 responsible for carrying out eye examinations to detect visual function anomalies, managing and treating these anomalies using spectacles, contact lenses, prisms, vision therapy, and low vision devices, as well as serving as a consultant on colour vision issues professionally in industry and road driving, and providing advisory services to meet the needs and expectations of stakeholders.
tasks: Performing refractive tests to determine the degree of refractive error and prescribing appropriate spectacles for patients requiring corrective lenses, including those who have or have not undergone surgery. Determining patients’ visual acuity accurately across all age groups, from infants to adults, and assesses suitability for contact lens use, contact lens fitting, and follow-up care. Providing treatment for patients with visual impairment and determining appropriate assistive devices for their use, referring patients to the Department of Social Welfare, Special Education Schools, or the Malaysian Association for the Blind (MAB) where necessary. Measuring corneal curvature in post-surgical patients and identifying sutures that require removal. Performing basic orthoptic examinations for patients with strabismus and providing treatment using spectacles, prisms, or visual therapy. Conducting diabetic eye screening using a fundus camera at district health clinics and refers cases to Ophthalmology Specialists when required. Delivering lectures in the field of Optometry to Medical Officers, Nurses, and Assistant Medical Officers during Hospital CME sessions. Determining clinic schedules, appointments for new and follow-up cases, and referrals to Ophthalmology Specialists, including regular vision and diabetes screenings at Health Clinics. Preparing monthly and annual statistical data of patients treated at the Optometry Clinic.

candidates.description: Optometrists examine and test eyes to identify abnormalities, visual problems, or disease. They prescribe and fit lenses such as spectacles and contacts, and offer advice on visual problems. They may also refer patients to a medical practitioner. Their scope of practice and title varies according to national regulations.

candidates.description: Opticians help to improve and correct an individual's vision. Their scope of practice varies according to national regulations and they might operate according to prescriptions provided by a specialised doctor in ophthalmology or an optometrist in the countries where requested.

They cut, inspect, mount and polish all parts using various machinery and hand tools. Optical technicians shape, grind and coat lenses for prescription eyewear. They fit completed lenses into eyeglass frames. Optical technicians ensure that lenses conform to the dispensing optician’s, specialised doctor in ophtalmology's or optometrist's prescriptions. They may also work with other associated optical instrumentation and its maintenance.

candidates.description: Eyewear and optical equipment shop managers assume responsibility for activities and staff in specialised shops.

candidates.title: eyewear and optical equipment specialised seller
candidates.description: Eyewear and optical equipment specialised sellers sell glasses in specialised shops.

Optomechanical engineering combines optical engineering with mechanical engineering in the design of these systems and devices. They conduct research, perform analysis, test the devices, and supervise the research.

candidates.description: Optomechanical engineering technicians collaborate with engineers in the development of optomechanical devices, such as optical tables, deformable mirrors, and optical mounts. Optomechanical engineering technicians build, install, test, and maintain optomechanical equipment prototypes. They determine materials and assembly requirements.

candidates.title: optical engineer
candidates.description: Optical engineers design and develop different industrial applications with optics. They have knowledge of light, light transmission principles, and optics in order to design engineering specs of equipment such as microscopes, lenses, telescopes, and other optical devices.

description: Radiographer Grade U9 responsible for producing medical images to assist specialists and medical officers in diagnosing diseases, evaluating images and radiography produced as well as managing matters related to the application of radiographic examinations, responsible for the maintenance and quality control of equipment used, as well as planning, management, training, and research tasks to enhance and monitor the quality of services provided by Radiographer.
tasks: Reviewing and examining radiography examination requests and determines the appropriate projections. Providing clear explanations to patients regarding the examination and required preparations in accordance with established instructions. Preparing and attending to all requirements and care for patient examinations. Generating and evaluating images and radiographs, assesses anatomical and structural abnormalities, and recommending additional projections when necessary. Providing radiation protection to all patients and personnel involved. Applying basic electronics and physics knowledge in radiography tasks, including troubleshooting equipment prior to reporting malfunctions. Monitoring and ensuring the maintenance of high-quality radiology service standards. Preparing educational materials and patient preparations for general and specialised radiography examinations. Coordinating identified research activities by preparing literature reviews and developing research methodologies and related technical information.

candidates.title: radiographer
candidates.description: Radiographers use a range of technologies to examine, treat and care for patients. They work in the fields of Medical Imaging, Radiotherapy and Nuclear Medicine and apply ionising radiation, ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and radioactive sources.

candidates.title: diagnostic radiographer
candidates.description: Diagnostic radiographers plan, prepare and perform diagnostic imaging examinations and post processing, with a wide range of equipment and techniques using X-rays, strong magnetic fields or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and high frequency sound (Ultrasound).

candidates.title: nuclear medicine radiographer
candidates.description: Nuclear medicine radiographers plan, prepare and perform nuclear medicine examinations, post-processing and treatment with a wide range of equipment and techniques using X-rays, magnetic resonance imaging and radiopharmaceuticals.

candidates.title: radio technician
candidates.description: Radio technicians install, adjust, test, maintain, and repair mobile or stationary radio transmitting and receiving equipment and two-way radio communications systems. They also monitor their performance and determine causes of faults.

candidates.title: radiation protection technician
candidates.description: Radiation protection technicians monitor radiation levels in buildings and facilities to ensure compliance with health and safety standards, and to prevent dangerous elevations in the radiation level. They take measures to minimise radiation emissions, and to prevent further contamination in the event of radiation pollution, by developing radiation protection plans, in particular for nuclear plants and facilities.

candidates.title: radiation therapist
candidates.description: Radiation therapists are responsible for the accurate delivery of radiotherapy to cancer patients and, as part of the multidisciplinary team, for elements of treatment preparation and patient care. This encompasses the safe and accurate delivery of the radiation dose prescribed and the clinical care and support of the patient throughout the treatment preparation, treatment delivery and immediate post treatment phases.

candidates.title: broadcast technician
candidates.description: Broadcast technicians install, start up, maintain, monitor and repair equipment used for the transmission and reception of television and radio broadcast signals. They ensure that all materials are available in a suitable format of transmittable quality according to the transmission deadline. Broadcast technicians also maintain and repair this equipment.

candidates.title: radio producer
candidates.description: Radio producers are responsible for organising the making of radio shows. They oversee aspects of radio shows such as content, audio production, resource planning and personnel supervision.

description: Instructor Grade U9 responsible for implementing activities related to the planning, preparation, and management of human resource training for paramedic and auxiliary groups, ensuring that the supply of personnel is adequate, qualified, and of high quality to meet current and future needs in the public sector.
tasks: Responsible for teaching and learning aspects of assigned subjects within the relevant unit, including delivering lectures, supervising trainees/instructors under their responsibility, monitoring logbooks, providing appropriate facilities for teaching and learning, and offering guidance and counselling. Assessing the effectiveness of teaching and learning in relation to the content of the assigned subjects. Conducting studies to plan programmes and analysing subject requirements within the relevant unit. Preparing related assessment questions derived from teaching and learning activities. Ensuring continuous professional development among instructors is implemented on an ongoing basis. Managing the scheduling, placement, and transportation of trainees to ensure practical training is conducted as prescribed. Conducting evaluations of trainees and monitoring training activities and logbooks. Coordinating and prepares student academic performance reports and managing examination-related matters.

candidates.title: driving instructor
candidates.description: Driving instructors teach people the theory and practice on how to operate a vehicle safely and according to regulations. They assist students in developing the skills needed to drive and prepare them for the driving theory and the driving examination. They may also supervise driving examinations.

candidates.title: sports instructor
candidates.description: Sports instructors introduce people to a sport and teach them the skills required for the performance of sport. They have a strong grip on one or more sports, which are often adventure sports, and know how to motivate others and share with them the enjoyment of the activity.

candidates.title: prison instructor
candidates.description: Prison instructors educate legal offenders, including prisoners, on social rehabilitation and correctional behaviour. They assist prisoners in gaining skills which could facilitate their reintegration into society and increase their chances at finding employment after release. Prison instructors analyse the students' individual learning needs, plan and prepare teaching materials and sessions and update their learning records. They also ensure the working area and materials are safe from danger and accounted for, and supervise the students at all times.

candidates.title: motorcycle instructor
candidates.description: Motorcycle instructors teach people the theory and practice of how to operate a motorcycle safely and according to regulations. They assist students in developing the skills needed to ride and prepare them for the theory test and the practical riding test.

candidates.title: fitness instructor
candidates.description: Fitness instructors build fitness participation of new and existing members through fitness experiences that meet their needs. They deliver fitness instruction to individuals, with the use of equipment, or to a group, through fitness classes. Both individual and group instructors have the purpose of promoting and delivering safe and effective exercise. Depending on the specific situation, some additional knowledge, skills and competences may be required.

candidates.title: truck driving instructor
candidates.description: Truck driving instructors teach people the theory and practice of how to operate a truck safely and according to regulations. They assist students in developing the skills needed to drive and prepare them for the driving theory tests and the practical driving test.

candidates.title: firefighter instructor
candidates.description: Firefighter instructors train probationary, new academy recruits, or cadets, on the theory and practice necessary to become a firefighter. They conduct theoretical lectures on academic subjects such as law, basic chemistry, safety regulations, risk management, fire prevention, reading blueprints etc. Fire academy instructors also provide more hands-on, practical instruction regarding the usage of assistive equipment and rescue tools such as a fire hose, fire axe, smoke mask etc., but also heavy physical training, breathing techniques, first aid, self defense tactics and vehicle operations. They also prepare and develop lesson plans and new training programmes as new public service-related regulations and issues arise. The instructors monitor the students' progress, evaluate them individually and prepare performance evaluation reports.

candidates.title: ski instructor
candidates.description: Ski instructors teach individuals or groups to ski and advanced skiing techniques. They advise their students on the choice of equipment, instruct skiers in alpine safety rules and plan and prepare ski instruction. Ski instructors demonstrate exercises and techniques during ski lessons and give feedback to their students on how to improve their level.

description: Dental Lecturer Grade DUG13P responsible for giving lectures, tutorials, conducting research, producing publications, and medical/dental practitioner.
tasks: The functions and general duties of a Lecturer position are 20% for research and publication contributions, 50% for teaching and supervision, 5% for academic recognition and leadership, 5% for consultancy, 10% for service to the university, and 10% for service to the community. Conducting research to expand knowledge and support more current and effective teaching. Publishing research findings. Delivering formal teaching as the core duty of academic staff. Supervising final year projects and students’ industrial training. Contributing to academic leadership and attaining awards, including evaluating theses, articles, journals for promotion, reviewing papers, participating in academic and professional associations, invited lectures, keynote speeches, appointment as journal editorial board members, and similar activities. Providing consultancy services within the area of expertise, whether paid or unpaid. Holding university administrative positions, such as Dean/ Director, Deputy Dean/ Deputy Director/ Head of Department/ Chairman/ Coordinator. Contributing to university activities and planning based on individual expertise. Providing services to the community outside the university in non-academic fields.

candidates.title: dentistry lecturer
candidates.description: Dentistry lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, dentistry, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of dentistry, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: higher education lecturer
candidates.description: Higher education lecturers instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, which is predominantly academic in nature. They may have job titles such as senior lecturer or professor. They work with their teaching and research assistants for the preparation of lectures and exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field, publish their findings and liaise with their academic colleagues.

candidates.title: medicine lecturer
candidates.description: Medicine lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, medicine, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of medicine, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: dental practitioner
candidates.description: Dental practitioners prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues.

candidates.title: healthcare specialist lecturer
candidates.description: Healthcare specialist lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of healthcare, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of specialist healthcare, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: mathematics lecturer
candidates.description: Mathematics lecturers instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, mathematics, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of mathematics, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: assistant lecturer
candidates.description: Assistant lecturers share university or college lecturers' academic workload, specifically the provision of lectures to students. They prepare and teach classes, and meet with students privately regarding evaluation. They also combine their lecturing and other academic duties with conducting their own research in their field of study. Assistant lecturers occupy an autonomous, full-time position, despite what the subservience element in the occupation title may suggest.

candidates.title: chemistry lecturer
candidates.description: Chemistry lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, chemistry, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for leading laboratory practices, grading papers and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their field of chemistry, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

description: Pharmacy Lecturer Grade DUF11 responsible for giving lectures, tutorials, conducting research and producing publications, providing clinical services in hospital pharmacies or services in community pharmacies, supervising thesis projects and managing practical work/tutorials, preparing lecture notes/laboratory manuals, conducting examinations, supervising student practical training work, assisting in reviewing/preparing curriculum/syllabus, and engaging in research work and conducting student development efforts.
tasks: Conducting research to expand knowledge and support more effective, up-to-date, and hands-on teaching. Publishing research findings. Delivering teaching and supervision, including teaching according to schedule, supervising final year projects and industrial training, preparing and marking examination scripts, and invigilating examinations. Providing clinical services in hospital or community pharmacy, including dispensing, counselling, Cytotoxic Drug Reconstitution (CDR), Therapeutic Drug Monitoring (TDM), Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN), Drug Information Service, Medication Therapy Adherence Clinic (MTAC), stock management, and pharmaceutical advisory services. Contributing to academic leadership, recognition, and distinction, including evaluating theses, articles, journals for promotion, reviewing papers, participating in academic and professional associations, invited lectures, keynote speeches, appointment as journal editorial board members, and others. Providing consultancy services within the area of expertise, whether paid or unpaid. Contributing to university service, either through administrative positions such as Dean/ Director, Deputy Dean/ Deputy Director/ Head of Department/ Chairman/ Coordinator, or based on individual expertise. Providing services to the community outside the university, particularly in non-academic activities.

candidates.title: pharmacy lecturer
candidates.description: Pharmacy lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, pharmacy, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for leading laboratory practices, grading papers and exams and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their field of pharmacy, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: pharmacist
candidates.description: Pharmacists prepare, dispense, and provide prescriptions for, over the counter medication. They offer clinical information on medicines, report suspected adverse reactions, and provide personalised support to patients. Pharmacists formulate and test medications in laboratories, and store, preserve, and distribute them.

candidates.title: medicine lecturer
candidates.description: Medicine lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, medicine, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of medicine, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: pharmacy technician
candidates.description: Pharmacy technicians, under the supervision of a pharmacist, check incoming goods, control stock, handle and store pharmaceuticals properly. Where permitted by national rules, they dispense medication and provide advice on their appropriate use.

candidates.title: pharmacy assistant
candidates.description: Pharmacy assistants perform general duties, such as stock management, serving at the cash desk, or performing administrative duties. They deal with the inventory within the pharmacy under the supervision of a pharmacist.

candidates.title: chemistry lecturer
candidates.description: Chemistry lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, chemistry, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for leading laboratory practices, grading papers and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their field of chemistry, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: hospital pharmacist
candidates.description: Hospital pharmacists prepare, dispense and provide medication to patients in hospitals. They collaborate with healthcare personnel such as doctors and nurses to treat patients and also offer advice and information on medications.

candidates.title: pharmaceutical quality specialist
candidates.description: Pharmaceutical quality specialists perform inspections and precision measurements in order to test and ensure the quality of pharmaceutical products. They are involved in the whole development phase of a pharmaceutical product until it is ready for the market. They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques the students must subsequently master for an industrial arts-related profession, working with wood and metal, such as carpenter or sheet metal worker. Industrial arts vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of industrial arts through assignments, tests and examinations.

candidates.title: business administration vocational teacher
candidates.description: Business administration vocational teachers instruct students in their specialised field of study, business administration, which is predominantly practical in nature. They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques the students must subsequently master for a business administration-related profession, such as accountant or banker. Business administration vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of business administration through assignments, tests and examinations.

candidates.title: armed forces training and education officer
candidates.description: Armed forces training and education officers train probationary, new academy recruits, or cadets, on the theory and practice necessary to become a soldier or a military officer, and need experience as a military officer themselves as a requirement to instruct. They prepare and present theoretical courses and materials during training on subjects such as law, national and international regulations, defense and offense models, world affairs etc. They also conduct the physical training of the cadets, teaching them care and usage of weapon and machinery, first aid, self defense and offense techniques, military vehicle operations, and putting them through a series of heavy drills and physical training. Armed forces training and education officers manage training plans by developing and updating the curriculum and field training exercises when necessary. They also assist senior officers in preparation for a promotion and generally monitor the cadets' progress and evaluate their performance through a series of theoretical and physical tests. They prepare performance and evaluation reports for each cadet individually.

candidates.title: employment and vocational integration consultant
candidates.description: Employment and vocational integration consultants offer assistance to unemployed individuals in finding jobs or vocational training opportunities, according to their educational or professional background and experience. They advise them on how to market their skills in the job-hunting process. Employment and vocational integration consultants help job-seekers write CVs and cover letters, prepare for a job interview and indicate where to search for new job or training opportunities.

candidates.title: food service vocational teacher
candidates.description: Food service vocational teachers for food service instruct students in their specialised field of study, food service, which is predominantly practical in nature. They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques the students must subsequently master for a food service-related profession. Food service vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of food service through assignments, tests and examinations.

candidates.title: corporate training manager
candidates.description: Corporate training managers coordinate all the training activities and development programmes in a company. They also design and develop new training modules and supervise all the activities related to the planning and delivery of these programmes.

role_title: Assistant Vocational Training Officer Grade DV5, DV6, DV7, DV8
description: Assistant Vocational Training Officer Grade DV5, DV6, DV7, DV8 responsible for planning, developing, and implementing teaching and learning (T&L) tasks related to vocational skills according to training curricula based on the National Occupational Skills Standard (NOSS) or other relevant standards, encompassing infrastructure development, curriculum development, teaching and learning (T&L), skills development, research and development (R&D), advisory and consultancy services, organisational/institutional management, compliance with procedures, safety and hygiene, and strategic collaboration.
tasks: Assisting in coordinating the accreditation process for Skills Training Providers (PLK) or existing accredited centres under the Department of Skills Development or other relevant accrediting bodies. Coordinating the formulation of assessment questions and the conduct of final evaluations, ensuring quality assurance in the implementation of final assessments at accredited centres meets the required standards. Assisting in coordinating inspection and monitoring of training programmes. Assisting in coordinating the student/trainee intake process. Assisting in preparing analyses, reports, and statistics on the workforce, finances, industry, and economy to identify training needs, target groups, skills areas, and levels of technology used. Assisting in preparing and implementing full-time and part-time programmes, and conducting studies and prepares evaluation reports on the progress and effectiveness of training. Delivering vocational skills training according to the training curriculum based on NOSS or other established standards. Undertaking management and supervision duties within the area of specialisation, including industrial training and support for student/trainee placement in industry. Preparing, controlling, recording, and updating training materials, machinery, and equipment requirements. Responsible for compliance with procedures, safety, cleanliness, and organisation within workspaces/workshops.

candidates.description: Vocational teachers instruct students in their specialised field of study, which is predominantly practical in nature. They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques that the students must subsequently master in the specialised vocation of their choice and aid in the development of the according attitudes and values. Vocational teachers monitor the students progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject through assignments, tests and examinations.

They induce students in the convenient social frameworks of their field of study and teach the appropriate attitudes and values. Physical education vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of physical education through assignments, tests and examinations.

They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques the students must subsequently master for a food service-related profession. Food service vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of food service through assignments, tests and examinations.

candidates.title: hospitality vocational teacher
candidates.description: Hospitality vocational teachers instruct students in their specialised field of study, hospitality, which is predominantly practical in nature. They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques the students must subsequently master for a hospitality-related profession, such as hotel receptionist or housekeeper. Hospitality vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of hospitality through assignments, tests and examinations.

They prepare and present theoretical courses and materials during training on subjects such as law, national and international regulations, defense and offense models, world affairs etc. They also conduct the physical training of the cadets, teaching them care and usage of weapon and machinery, first aid, self defense and offense techniques, military vehicle operations, and putting them through a series of heavy drills and physical training. Armed forces training and education officers manage training plans by developing and updating the curriculum and field training exercises when necessary. They also assist senior officers in preparation for a promotion and generally monitor the cadets' progress and evaluate their performance through a series of theoretical and physical tests.
