description: Software Trainer develops, designs, and delivers training programmes on software applications, both in-person and online. They assess training needs, prepare instructional materials, conduct workshops or sessions for individuals and groups, support learners in effectively using software tools, and may utilise technologies such as satellite systems to reach remote participants while monitoring learning outcomes and ensuring clear communication between trainers and learners.
tasks: Carry out training needs analyses and develop training curricula and instructional materials tailored to user needs. Conduct classroom or virtual training sessions for individuals or groups, and demonstrate software features and functions clearly to learners. Assess trainee understanding through quizzes, feedback, or assignments. Set up and manage training environments, including information technology (IT) equipment and training resources. Troubleshoot technical or user issues during training sessions. Liaise with relevant stakeholders and technical teams to support training delivery. Monitor programme quality and learner engagement, and provide ongoing learner support and training updates.

candidates.title: ICT trainer
candidates.description: ICT trainers conduct training-needs analysis and design programs to train students in the use of software packages and information systems accordingly. They produce and update existing training materials (content and method), deliver effective training in classroom, online or informally, monitor, evaluate and report effectiveness of training. They maintain and update expertise on specialised ICT subjects and evaluate and report on students' performance.

candidates.title: corporate trainer
candidates.description: Corporate trainers train, coach, and guide employees of a company to teach and improve their skills, competences and knowledge in accordance with the needs of the company. They develop the existing potential of the employees to increase their efficiency, motivation, job satisfaction, and employability.

candidates.title: software manager
candidates.description: Software managers oversee the acquisition and development of software systems in order to provide support to all organisational units. They also monitor the results and quality of the different software solutions and projects implemented in the organisation.

candidates.title: software developer
candidates.description: Software developers implement or program all kinds of software systems based on specifications and designs by using programming languages, tools, and platforms.

candidates.title: personal trainer
candidates.description: Personal trainers design, implement and evaluate exercise or physical activity programmes for one or more individual clients by collecting and analysing client information. They strive to ensure the effectiveness of personal exercise programmes. A personal trainer should also actively encourage potential clients to participate in and adhere to regular programmes, employing appropriate motivational strategies.

candidates.title: software analyst
candidates.description: Software analysts elicit and prioritise user requirements, produce and document software specifications, test their application, and review them during software development. They act as the interface between the software users and the software development team.

candidates.title: software tester
candidates.description: Software testers perform software tests. They may also plan and design them. They may also debug and repair software although this mainly corresponds to designers and developers. They ensure that applications function properly before delivering them to internal and external clients.

candidates.title: ski instructor
candidates.description: Ski instructors teach individuals or groups to ski and advanced skiing techniques. They advise their students on the choice of equipment, instruct skiers in alpine safety rules and plan and prepare ski instruction. Ski instructors demonstrate exercises and techniques during ski lessons and give feedback to their students on how to improve their level.

description: Operation Research Analyst studies an organisation’s structures, methods, systems, and procedures to support management in decision-making and strategic planning. They apply mathematical, statistical, and analytical techniques, including predictive modelling and optimisation, to solve problems, improve processes, and enhance efficiency. The role may also involve designing and maintaining data systems, ensuring data quality, and providing analytical support for reporting and organisational insights.
tasks: Collect and analyse data on organisational processes, systems, and procedures to identify inefficiencies and opportunities for improvement. Develop mathematical, statistical, and analytical models to support decision-making, forecasting, and the simulation of business scenarios. Evaluate current systems, workflows, and organisational structures to recommend process and efficiency improvements. Design and maintain data systems, databases, and related processes that support analysis, reporting, and organisational insights. Collaborate with departments and stakeholders to gather requirements and support the implementation of analytical solutions. Prepare reports and communicate analytical findings, recommendations, and insights to management for strategic planning and decision-making. Provide analytical support and guidance to improve organisational effectiveness and continuous improvement initiatives.

candidates.title: business analyst
candidates.description: Business analysts research and understand the strategic position of businesses and companies in relation to their markets and their stakeholders. They analyse and present their views on how the company, from many perspectives, can improve its strategic position and internal corporate structure. They assess needs for change, communication methods, technology, IT tools, new standards and certifications.

candidates.title: occupational analyst
candidates.description: Occupational analysts collect and analyse occupational information within one field or company in order to make recommendations for reducing costs and general business improvements. They provide technical assistance to employers in dealing with problematic staff recruitment and development and with staff restructuring. Occupational analysts study and write job descriptions and prepare occupational classification systems.

candidates.title: securities analyst
candidates.description: Securities analysts perform research activities to gather and analyse financial, legal and economic information. They interpret data on the price, stability and future investment trends in a certain economic area and make recommendations and forecasts to business clients.

candidates.title: operations manager
candidates.description: Operations managers plan, oversee and coordinate the daily operations of production of goods and provision of services. They also formulate and implement company policies and plan the use of human resources and materials.

candidates.title: logistics analyst
candidates.description: Logistics analysts streamline product manufacturing, transportation, storage and distribution. They assess production and supply chain problems to determine economically efficient solutions. They assists company managers in decision-making processes and direct programs designed to provide subcontractors, managers and customers with logistic technology.

candidates.title: data analyst
candidates.description: Data analysts import, inspect, clean, transform, validate, model, or interpret collections of data with regard to the business goals of the company. They ensure that the data sources and repositories provide consistent and reliable data. Data analysts use different algorithms and IT tools as demanded by the situation and the current data. They might prepare reports in the form of visualisations such as graphs, charts, and dashboards.

candidates.title: ICT business analyst
candidates.description: ICT business analysts are in charge of analysing and designing an organisation's processes and systems, assessing the business model and its integration with technology. They also identify change needs, assess the impact of the change, capture and document requirements and then ensure that these requirements are delivered whilst supporting the business through the implementation process.

candidates.title: market research analyst
candidates.description: Market research analysts collect the information gathered in the market research and study it to draw conclusions. They define the potential customers of a product, the target group and the way they can be reached. Market research analysts analyse the position of products in the market from different perspectives such as features, prices and competitors. They analyse cross selling and interdependencies between different products and their placement. Market research analysts prepare information helpful for the development of marketing strategies.

description: Staff Training Officer plans, develops, and delivers a training programme to enhance employee skills and competencies in alignment with organisational goals. They assess training needs, design instructional content or customised learning materials, facilitate sessions in various formats, and evaluate outcomes to ensure training effectiveness and support overall workforce development and performance improvement.
tasks: Identify training needs through assessments, surveys, interviews, and feedback to determine skill gaps and development priorities. Set training objectives aligned with organisational goals, and evaluate learning outcomes and training effectiveness. Develop and update training programmes, instructional content, manuals, visual aids, and online materials. Design, schedule, and deliver in-person and virtual training sessions, workshops, and demonstrations for individuals and groups, ensuring engagement and comprehension. Collaborate with department heads and subject matter experts to ensure content accuracy and alignment with organisational needs. Evaluate participant feedback and performance results, and implement improvements to training programmes. Maintain accurate records of training activities, participant progress, and programme outcomes. Stay updated on trends, tools, and best practices in staff training and workforce development.

candidates.title: armed forces training and education officer
candidates.description: Armed forces training and education officers train probationary, new academy recruits, or cadets, on the theory and practice necessary to become a soldier or a military officer, and need experience as a military officer themselves as a requirement to instruct. They prepare and present theoretical courses and materials during training on subjects such as law, national and international regulations, defense and offense models, world affairs etc. They also conduct the physical training of the cadets, teaching them care and usage of weapon and machinery, first aid, self defense and offense techniques, military vehicle operations, and putting them through a series of heavy drills and physical training. Armed forces training and education officers manage training plans by developing and updating the curriculum and field training exercises when necessary. They also assist senior officers in preparation for a promotion and generally monitor the cadets' progress and evaluate their performance through a series of theoretical and physical tests. They prepare performance and evaluation reports for each cadet individually.

candidates.title: corporate training manager
candidates.description: Corporate training managers coordinate all the training activities and development programmes in a company. They also design and develop new training modules and supervise all the activities related to the planning and delivery of these programmes.

candidates.title: human resources officer
candidates.description: Human resources officers develop and implement strategies that help their employers select and retain appropriately qualified staff within that business sector. They recruit staff, prepare job advertisements, interview and short-list people, negotiate with employment agencies, and set up working conditions. Human resources officers also administer the payroll, review salaries and advise on remuneration benefits and employment law. They arrange for training opportunities to enhance employees' performance.

candidates.title: police trainer
candidates.description: Police trainers train probationary, new academy recruits, or cadets, and seasoned veterans on the theory and practice necessary to become a police officer. They conduct theoretical lectures on academic subjects such as law, government regulations, community relations and human diversity. Police academy instructors also provide more hands-on, practical instruction regarding physical training, the care of firearms, first aid, self defensive tactics and vehicle operations. They also prepare and develop lesson plans and new training programmes as new law enforcement-related regulations and issues arise. The instructors monitor the students' progress, evaluate them individually and prepare performance evaluation reports.

candidates.title: armed forces officer
candidates.description: Armed forces officers supervise operations and manoeuvres, assign duties, and command subordinate staff. They ensure efficient communication within and between units and perform training duties. They also operate equipment and supervise equipment maintenance.

candidates.title: defence administration officer
candidates.description: Defence administration officers perform managerial duties and administrative tasks in defense institutions, such as maintenance of records, management of staff, and handling of accounts.

candidates.title: corporate trainer
candidates.description: Corporate trainers train, coach, and guide employees of a company to teach and improve their skills, competences and knowledge in accordance with the needs of the company. They develop the existing potential of the employees to increase their efficiency, motivation, job satisfaction, and employability.

candidates.title: chief operating officer
candidates.description: Chief operating officers are the right hand and second in command of a company's chief executive officer. They ensure that the daily operations of the company run smoothly. Chief operating officers also develop company policies, rules and goals.

description: Agro-Based Biotech Food Researcher conducts scientific research and development in agricultural biotechnology to improve a food product and production method. They work on enhancing crop performance, nutritional value, and food safety through biotechnological techniques, including genetically modified crops, while developing sustainable production practices. The role involves laboratory experimentation, collaboration with interdisciplinary teams, and communicating research findings to stakeholders.
tasks: Design and conduct experiments, and carry out research and development (R&D) activities to develop or improve agro-based food products and agricultural biotechnology applications. Analyse and interpret research data on nutritional value, food safety, and production outcomes. Collaborate with scientists, research institutions, and agricultural specialists to improve crop yield, quality, resilience, and sustainable production practices. Evaluate research findings for practical application and technological development in agro-based food and agricultural biotechnology. Ensure compliance with national and international food safety and biotechnology standards. Document research methods, processes, and results, and prepare detailed reports for publication, policy, and stakeholder use. Monitor and apply technological advancements and innovations in agro-based food and agricultural biotechnology.

candidates.title: food biotechnologist
candidates.description: Food biotechnologists study the life cycle of food from its preservation up to the spoilage and the food-borne pathogens. They research and understand food-borne diseases in order to prevent them. They ensure that food products abide by government regulations regarding food health and safety.

candidates.title: agricultural scientist
candidates.description: Agricultural scientists research and study soil, animals and plants with the objective of improving agricultural processes, the quality of agricultural products or the impact of agricultural processes on the environment. They plan and implement projects such as development projects on behalf of clients or institutions.

candidates.title: food analyst
candidates.description: Food analysts perform standardised tests to determine the chemical, physical, or microbiological features of products for human consumption.

candidates.title: food technologist
candidates.description: Food technologists develop processes for manufacturing foodstuffs and related products based on chemical, physical, and biological principles and technology. They design and plan layouts or equipment, oversee staff, engage in controlling, and improve food technologies in food production processes.

candidates.title: food science lecturer
candidates.description: Food science lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, food science, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, grading papers and exams and leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their field of food science, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: food production engineer
candidates.description: Food production engineers oversee the electrical and mechanical needs of the equipment and machinery required in the process of manufacturing food or beverages. They strive to maximise plant productivity by engaging in preventive actions in reference to health and safety, good manufacturing practices (GMP), hygiene compliance, and performance of routine maintenance of machines and equipment.

candidates.title: agronomic crop production team leader
candidates.description: Agronomic crop production team leaders are responsible for leading and working with a team of crop production workers. They organise the daily work schedules for crop production and participate in the production.

candidates.title: agricultural engineer
candidates.description: Agricultural engineers intervene in a variety of matters within the agriculture field in combination with engineering concepts. They design and develop machinery and equipment for an efficient and sustainable exploitation of the land. They advise on the use of resources in agricultural sites comprising the usage of water and soil, harvesting methods, and waste management.

description: Aquaculture Biotech Researcher studies and analyses aquatic organisms and ecosystems to improve aquaculture practices and support sustainable management of marine and freshwater resources. They conduct scientific research on the health, breeding, and nutrition of fish and aquatic plants, applying biotechnological techniques to enhance productivity, feed efficiency, and overall sustainability in aquaculture environments. Their work integrates field and laboratory studies to address environmental, biological, and human factors affecting aquatic life.
tasks: Conduct scientific research to improve aquaculture practices and support sustainable marine and freshwater resource management. Manage and operate aquaculture systems, including monitoring water quality and environmental conditions. Oversee the breeding, rearing, and health management of aquatic species. Conduct laboratory and field experiments, and analyse biological and ecological samples. Develop and apply technologies and strategies to improve aquaculture sustainability and ecosystem management. Monitor and evaluate aquaculture environments and marine biodiversity to support conservation and sustainable use. Collaborate with research institutions, industry partners, and government agencies, and coordinate related research activities. Prepare scientific reports, documentation, and research findings for practical application and development purposes.

candidates.title: aquaculture biologist
candidates.description: Aquaculture biologists apply knowledge gained from research about aquatic animals and plant life and their interactions with each other and the environment, in order to improve aquaculture production, prevent animal health and environmental problems and to provide solutions if necessary.

candidates.title: aquaculture environmental analyst
candidates.description: Aquaculture environmental analysts assess, plan and implement programmes to recognise, monitor and control environmental factors that can potentially affect the health of aquatic animals and plants.

candidates.title: water-based aquaculture technician
candidates.description: Water-based aquaculture technicians coordinate and supervise activities on fattening aquaculture organisms in suspended systems (floating or submerged structures). They participate in extraction operations and handling organisms for commercialisation. Water-based aquaculture technicians supervise maintenance of equipment and facilities (cages, rafts, longlines, bouchot).

candidates.title: water-based aquaculture worker
candidates.description: Water-based aquaculture workers carry out manual activities in the ongrowing processes of cultured aquatic organisms in water-based suspended systems (floating or submerged structures). They participate in extraction operations and the handling of organisms for commercialisation. Water-based aquaculture workers maintain and clean facilities (nets, mooring ropes, cages).

candidates.title: aquaculture cage technician
candidates.description: Aquaculture cage technicians operate in the production of aquatic organisms in water-based (freshwater, brackish water, salt water) on-growing processes in cages.

candidates.title: aquaculture production manager
candidates.description: Aquaculture production managers plan, direct and coordinate the production of fish, shellfish or other forms of aquatic life such as cash crops, in large-scale aquaculture operations to culture and harvest or for release into fresh, brackish or salt water.

candidates.title: aquaculture site supervisor
candidates.description: Aquaculture site supervisors supervise production processes in large-scale aquaculture operations and inspect aquaculture sites to maintain and improve performance. They maintain the health, safety and security of the workplace, develop management plans to reduce the risks from pests, predators and diseases and supervise both the disposal of bio and chemical waste and the maintenance of equipment and machinery.

candidates.title: aquaculture harvesting worker
candidates.description: Aquaculture harvesting workers work in the harvesting of those aquatic organisms cultured in land-based on-growing processes.

description: Research and Development Executive leads and manages research initiatives to develop and improve products and processes. They plan and execute projects aimed at enhancing productivity, sustainability, and innovation, oversee testing and evaluation, and ensure compliance with regulatory and industry standards. The role involves collaboration with cross-functional teams to optimise processes, maintain data integrity, and support organisational growth through new methods, products, and technologies.
tasks: Conduct research to develop new and innovative products and processes. Improve the quality, performance, and efficiency of existing products and processes through testing and refinement. Design and implement research trials and experiments for product and process development. Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and industry standards. Collaborate with production, quality assurance, engineering, and other cross-functional teams. Evaluate research outcomes for practical application and process or product improvement. Prepare technical reports, documentation, and maintain detailed research and development records. Coordinate research and development activities and optimise processes to improve productivity and innovation.

candidates.title: research and development manager
candidates.description: Research and development managers coordinate the efforts of scientists, academical researchers, product developers, and market researchers towards the creation of new products, the improvement of current ones or other research activities, including scientific research. They manage and plan research and development activities of an organisation, specify goals and budget requirements and manage the staff.

candidates.title: research manager
candidates.description: Research managers oversee the research and development functions of a research facility or program or university. They support the executive staff, coordinate work activities, and monitor staff and research projects. They may work in a wide array of sectors, such as the chemical, technical and life sciences sector. Research managers can also advise on research and execute research themselves.

candidates.title: ICT research manager
candidates.description: ICT research managers plan, manage and monitor research activities and evaluate emerging trends in the information and communication technology field to assess their relevance. They also design and oversee staff training on the use of new technology and recommend ways to implement new products and solutions that will maximise benefits for the organisation.

candidates.title: community development officer
candidates.description: Community development officers develop plans to improve quality of life in local communities. They investigate and assess the community's issues and needs, manage resources, and develop implementation strategies. They communicate with the community for investigation purposes, and to inform the community on development plans.

candidates.title: product development manager
candidates.description: Product development managers coordinate the development of new products from beginning to end. They receive briefings and start envisioning the new product considering design, technical and cost criteria. They conduct research on market needs and create prototypes of new products for untapped market opportunities. Product development managers also improve and boost technological quality.

candidates.title: economic development coordinator
candidates.description: Economic development coordinators outline and implement policies for the improvement of a community's, government's or institution's economic growth and stability. They research economic trends and coordinate cooperation between institutions working in economic development. They analyse potential economic risks and conflicts and develop plans to resolve them. Economic development coordinators advise on the economic sustainability of institutions and economic growth.

candidates.title: innovation officer
candidates.description: Innovation officers are the link between industrial production and innovation strategies for a company. They work to improve the company responses to sudden change in the markets through innovation with the aim of prevent and deal with business disruptions. They manage and train a team of workers who focus on innovative projects or ideas. They supervise and plan changes in products and process to achieve better organizational efficiency and help the company to be more competitive. They work side-by-side with other executives to make sure they would support initiatives aimed at fostering innovation.

candidates.title: regional development policy officer
candidates.description: Regional development policy officers research, analyse and develop regional development policies. They implement policies that aim at reducing regional disparities by fostering economic activities in a region and structural changes such as supporting multi-level governance, rural development and improvement of infrastructure. They work closely with partners, external organisations or other stakeholders and provide them with regular updates.

description: Research Officer plans, conducts, and manages a research project to generate new knowledge, develop an innovative solution, and support organisational objectives across scientific, technical, and industrial fields. They design and implement experiments, collect and analyse data, and contribute to the development of new processes, technologies, or products.
tasks: Collect, manage and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data. Design and execute research projects to generate new knowledge and improve technologies or processes. Develop and optimise experimental methods for research activities. Evaluate research findings for potential development and practical application. Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders to support research and development objectives. Prepare accurate reports and documentation on research methods, findings and process improvements. Ensure research activities comply with ethical, safety and environmental requirements. Stay updated on current scientific and technological developments in the relevant field. Support the coordination of research and development initiatives.

candidates.title: research manager
candidates.description: Research managers oversee the research and development functions of a research facility or program or university. They support the executive staff, coordinate work activities, and monitor staff and research projects. They may work in a wide array of sectors, such as the chemical, technical and life sciences sector. Research managers can also advise on research and execute research themselves.

candidates.title: research and development manager
candidates.description: Research and development managers coordinate the efforts of scientists, academical researchers, product developers, and market researchers towards the creation of new products, the improvement of current ones or other research activities, including scientific research. They manage and plan research and development activities of an organisation, specify goals and budget requirements and manage the staff.

candidates.title: innovation officer
candidates.description: Innovation officers are the link between industrial production and innovation strategies for a company. They work to improve the company responses to sudden change in the markets through innovation with the aim of prevent and deal with business disruptions. They manage and train a team of workers who focus on innovative projects or ideas. They supervise and plan changes in products and process to achieve better organizational efficiency and help the company to be more competitive. They work side-by-side with other executives to make sure they would support initiatives aimed at fostering innovation.

candidates.title: intelligence officer
candidates.description: Intelligence officers develop and execute plans to gather information and intelligence. They investigate the lines of enquiry which would provide them with the necessary intelligence, and contact and interview people who may provide intelligence. They write reports on their results, and perform administrative duties to ensure records maintenance.

candidates.title: research engineer
candidates.description: Research engineers combine research skills and knowledge of engineering principles to assist in the development or design of new products and technology. They also improve existing technical processes, machines and systems and create new, innovative technologies. The duties of research engineers depend on the branch of engineering and the industry in which they work. Research engineers generally work in an office or laboratory, analysing processes and conducting experiments.

candidates.title: ICT research manager
candidates.description: ICT research managers plan, manage and monitor research activities and evaluate emerging trends in the information and communication technology field to assess their relevance. They also design and oversee staff training on the use of new technology and recommend ways to implement new products and solutions that will maximise benefits for the organisation.

candidates.title: policy officer
candidates.description: Policy officers research, analyse and develop policies in various public sectors, and shape and implement these policies to improve the existing regulation around the sector. They evaluate effects of existing policies and report findings to the government and members of the public. Policy officers work closely with partners, external organisations or other stakeholders and provide them with regular updates.

candidates.title: university research assistant
candidates.description: University research assistants conduct academic research for the university or college they are employed in. They may assist professors they are affiliated with, their supervisor, in their research or develop their own in the related field of that professor.

description: Research Officer Grade Q9 carry out research and development (R&D) tasks, provide expert services, training, consultancy, presentations, and diagnostics (including technical reports, research highlights, and policy briefs).
tasks: Carrying out existing or new research projects, including laboratory or field work, as well as the management and collection of research data. Developing the RTP reactor model using MCNP software and conducts neutron flux measurements at the TRIGA PUSPATI Reactor. Performing quality assurance activities for GMP Tc-99m generators and undertakes studies to enhance the production of nuclear products for medical use. Conducting research activities related to Nuclear Impact on Ecosystem, including the sub-project Study of Gaharu by-products, as well as the development of innovative rock-based materials. Disseminating research findings through the preparation of scientific or technical reports, presentations, whether oral or poster, and publication of articles. Utilising scientific equipment and software accurately and appropriately in research activities. Managing and performing specialised diagnostic work, including quality management activities such as Internal Quality Control (IQC), External Quality Control (EQC), and test accreditation. Carrying out research management duties, including processing project registrations, obtaining ethical approvals, submitting grant applications, and monitoring project progress. Managing and coordinating quality and administrative activities, including ISO implementation, 5S Practices, asset verification, course and conference management, as well as updating the International Nuclear Information System (INIS) and WINSPIR databases. Contributing to intellectual development.

candidates.title: research manager
candidates.description: Research managers oversee the research and development functions of a research facility or program or university. They support the executive staff, coordinate work activities, and monitor staff and research projects. They may work in a wide array of sectors, such as the chemical, technical and life sciences sector. Research managers can also advise on research and execute research themselves.

candidates.title: research and development manager
candidates.description: Research and development managers coordinate the efforts of scientists, academical researchers, product developers, and market researchers towards the creation of new products, the improvement of current ones or other research activities, including scientific research. They manage and plan research and development activities of an organisation, specify goals and budget requirements and manage the staff.

candidates.title: intelligence officer
candidates.description: Intelligence officers develop and execute plans to gather information and intelligence. They investigate the lines of enquiry which would provide them with the necessary intelligence, and contact and interview people who may provide intelligence. They write reports on their results, and perform administrative duties to ensure records maintenance.

candidates.title: research engineer
candidates.description: Research engineers combine research skills and knowledge of engineering principles to assist in the development or design of new products and technology. They also improve existing technical processes, machines and systems and create new, innovative technologies. The duties of research engineers depend on the branch of engineering and the industry in which they work. Research engineers generally work in an office or laboratory, analysing processes and conducting experiments.

candidates.title: ICT research manager
candidates.description: ICT research managers plan, manage and monitor research activities and evaluate emerging trends in the information and communication technology field to assess their relevance. They also design and oversee staff training on the use of new technology and recommend ways to implement new products and solutions that will maximise benefits for the organisation.

candidates.title: innovation officer
candidates.description: Innovation officers are the link between industrial production and innovation strategies for a company. They work to improve the company responses to sudden change in the markets through innovation with the aim of prevent and deal with business disruptions. They manage and train a team of workers who focus on innovative projects or ideas. They supervise and plan changes in products and process to achieve better organizational efficiency and help the company to be more competitive. They work side-by-side with other executives to make sure they would support initiatives aimed at fostering innovation.

candidates.title: chief technology officer
candidates.description: Chief technology officers contribute to a company's technical vision and lead all aspects of technology development, according to its strategic direction and growth objectives. They match technology with business needs.

candidates.title: health and safety officer
candidates.description: Health and safety officers execute plans for the improvement of work environments and cultures. They assess risks and interview employees to ensure the work environment is compliant with health and safety rules, as well as ensuring the interaction within the workplace occurs in a positive and productive manner. If employed in a healthcare facility the health and safety officer has to investigate infections spreading across a facility and advice all employees how to combat and prevent infections. Furthermore health physics is applied at facilities where people are exposed to ionizing radiation such as nuclear power plants and research institutions.

description: Scientific Officer Grade C9 responsible for the operation of teaching laboratories or research laboratories within the scope of procurement. Responsible for the management of practical teaching laboratories in accordance with academic programmes, and for ensuring that the scientific training of final year students is conducted smoothly. Manage the operation of fieldwork activities of subordinate staff in accordance with established procedures. Ensure that quality control management is implemented. Plan the development of knowledge and skills of organisational members. Plan and control the organisation’s finances and equipment. Manage and take action on customer complaints. Plan and monitor practical activities, and manage safety briefings. Ensure that the organisation’s quality development is continuously updated. Plan human resources requirements.
tasks: Managing and ensuring that all laboratory equipment functions properly, is safe for use, and complies with the prescribed procedures and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Coordinating and carrying out periodic calibration of laboratory equipment in accordance with the established schedule. Ensuring that the storage of chemicals and consumable materials complies with safety and storage procedures. Managing practical preparation requirements based on the prescribed practical handbook. Managing the payment process to suppliers related to laboratory requirements. Managing the operation of fieldwork activities (practical and research), including task allocation and compliance with procedures. Reviewing, identifying, and verifying applications for work conducted outside the office and outside normal working hours. Ensuring that technical requirements for research activities and fieldwork are fulfilled. Managing, monitoring, and providing guidance to students undergoing scientific training regarding the use and borrowing of laboratory equipment. Managing laboratory quality control, including the preparation of usage logbooks, maintenance records, and instrumentation documentation.

candidates.title: scientific laboratory technician
candidates.description: Scientific laboratory technicians carry out laboratory-based research, analysis and testing and support life science professionals. They sample, test, measure, research and analyse in areas such as biology, biotechnology, environmental science, forensic science and pharmacology. Scientific laboratory technicians also observe and monitor laboratory activities, record test sequences and analyse the results.

candidates.title: research manager
candidates.description: Research managers oversee the research and development functions of a research facility or program or university. They support the executive staff, coordinate work activities, and monitor staff and research projects. They may work in a wide array of sectors, such as the chemical, technical and life sciences sector. Research managers can also advise on research and execute research themselves.

candidates.description: Health and safety officers execute plans for the improvement of work environments and cultures. They assess risks and interview employees to ensure the work environment is compliant with health and safety rules, as well as ensuring the interaction within the workplace occurs in a positive and productive manner. If employed in a healthcare facility the health and safety officer has to investigate infections spreading across a facility and advice all employees how to combat and prevent infections. Furthermore health physics is applied at facilities where people are exposed to ionizing radiation such as nuclear power plants and research institutions.

candidates.description: Intelligence officers develop and execute plans to gather information and intelligence. They investigate the lines of enquiry which would provide them with the necessary intelligence, and contact and interview people who may provide intelligence. They write reports on their results, and perform administrative duties to ensure records maintenance.

candidates.title: medical laboratory manager
candidates.description: Medical laboratory managers oversee the daily operations of a medical laboratory. They manage employees and communicate the schedule of activities. They monitor and ensure all laboratory operations are performed according to specifications, arrange the necessary laboratory equipment and assure that the appropriate health and safety standards are followed.

candidates.title: monitoring and evaluation officer
candidates.description: Monitoring and evaluation officers are responsible for the conceptualisation, design, implementation and follow-up of the monitoring and evaluation activities of projects, programmes, policies, strategies, institutions or processes, along the relevant programming cycle. They develop monitoring, inspection and evaluation methods and instruments needed to collect and analyse data, and report on results by applying structured M&E frameworks, theories, approaches and methodologies. M&E officers inform decision-making through reporting, learning products or activities and knowledge management. They can also engage in capacity development activities by providing training and capacity building support within their organizations or for clients and partners.

candidates.title: chief technology officer
candidates.description: Chief technology officers contribute to a company's technical vision and lead all aspects of technology development, according to its strategic direction and growth objectives. They match technology with business needs.

candidates.title: police officer
candidates.description: Police officers use investigation methods to prevent crime, to pursue and apprehend criminals, and protect the public from violent and criminal activities. They perform surveillance and patrol activities to prevent crimes and apprehend offenders. They provide support to victimised parties and the public at large, and fulfil administrative duties.

description: Technical Sales Engineer combines engineering expertise with commercial skills to promote and sell a product or system. They assess customer needs, provide technical advice, recommend appropriate solutions, and support clients throughout the purchasing process. The role involves building client relationships, representing the business professionally, and ensuring that solutions meet technical and operational requirements.
tasks: Develop and maintain professional relationships with clients throughout the sales process. Identify and pursue new technical sales opportunities. Deliver product presentations and demonstrations to clients. Prepare quotations and technical proposals for clients. Collaborate with engineering and product teams to develop suitable solutions for customer requirements. Advise clients on product selection and implementation requirements. Monitor customer feedback and report it for product and service improvement. Track market trends and competitor activities to support sales strategies. Coordinate with manufacturers to fulfil customer technical and operational requirements. Plan and execute technical sales activities to meet business objectives.

candidates.title: sales engineer
candidates.description: Sales engineers provide technical customisation of products based on customers requests and needs (mainly heavy duty), such as building equipment. They take care of business to business contact and assume responsibility for complex repairs and maintenance process.

candidates.description: Technical sales representatives act for a business to sell its merchandise while providing technical insight for customers.

description: Product Specialist is responsible for managing and promoting a specific product within a market, combining technical expertise, market analysis, and customer insight to ensure the product meets quality standards and market demands. They support sales and marketing initiatives, provide technical guidance and product evaluations, and offer feedback to drive improvements and enhance overall customer satisfaction. The role integrates product assessment, compliance checks, and continuous support to optimise performance and market impact.
tasks: Support the achievement of sales targets for assigned product lines through product expertise and customer support. Conduct product demonstrations and provide technical guidance to clients. Prepare technical proposals, product documentation, and client reports. Analyse market trends and customer feedback to support product strategies and improvements. Support product launches, promotional activities, and advertising campaigns to enhance market visibility. Respond to customer enquiries, diagnose technical issues, and coordinate solutions with engineering teams. Maintain accurate technical knowledge and product content, and ensure compliance with relevant guidelines. Coordinate timely product availability and advise clients on product implementation strategies.

candidates.title: advertising specialist
candidates.description: Advertising specialists provide advice to companies and organisations about the development of their advertising strategies and on advertising-related topics covering a more general strategic approach. They combine knowledge of marketing, budgets, and psychology with a creative mind to develop advertising campaigns. They propose alternatives to clients that promote their organisations, products, or projects.

candidates.title: product manager
candidates.description: Product managers are responsible for managing the lifecycle of a product. They research and develop new products in addition to managing existing ones through market research and strategic planning. Product managers perform marketing and planning activities to increase profits.

candidates.title: pricing specialist
candidates.description: Pricing specialists analyse production prices, market trends and competitors in order to establish the right price, taking brand and marketing concepts into consideration.

candidates.title: chief product officer
candidates.description: Chief Product Officers conduct the product strategy of a company, define the product vision, prioritise customer needs and design the product roadmap. Key drivers of innovation product processes and revenue growth, they are responsible for the entire product development process and product-related activities which involve design, elaboration, product strategy setting, creating multi-functional partnerships, and new products launch. Moreover, they lead the organisation’s product management team and closely work with the marketing department.

candidates.title: product development manager
candidates.description: Product development managers coordinate the development of new products from beginning to end. They receive briefings and start envisioning the new product considering design, technical and cost criteria. They conduct research on market needs and create prototypes of new products for untapped market opportunities. Product development managers also improve and boost technological quality.

candidates.title: product development engineering technician
candidates.description: Product development engineering technicians improve efficiency of product development, set up equipment and develop and test solutions to solve technical problems. They work closely with engineers and technologists, inspect products, conduct tests and collect data.

candidates.title: chemical application specialist
candidates.description: Chemical application specialists develop chemical products according to the needs and expectation of the clients. They conduct development of formulas and processes of formulation as well as evaluation of the efficiency and performances of the formulations.

candidates.title: specialist pharmacist
candidates.description: Specialist pharmacists provide specialist services for companies in the pharmacy industry and in hospital pharmacies. The role of the specialist pharmacist varies throughout Europe, subject to national rules and training.

description: Sales Representative (Medical) promotes and sells pharmaceutical products, medical devices and related healthcare services to healthcare professionals and institutions. The role involves providing accurate and compliant information on product indications, usage and benefits, advising on appropriate application and, where relevant, supporting the installation and operational use of medical equipment. They are responsible for developing client relationships and achieving agreed sales objectives within the healthcare sector.
tasks: Identify potential clients among healthcare professionals and institutions in hospitals and clinics. Deliver sales presentations and product demonstrations on pharmaceutical products, medical devices, and related healthcare services. Build and maintain long-term client relationships, and provide after-sales support on product application and use. Assess clients’ needs and recommend appropriate pharmaceutical products, medical devices, or related healthcare services. Gather and analyse market intelligence and client feedback to support sales strategies. Prepare regular sales and client activity reports for management. Stay updated on product indications, usage, benefits, and healthcare industry developments to provide accurate and compliant information.

candidates.title: medical sales representative
candidates.description: Medical sales representatives promote and sell medical devices, equipment and pharmaceutical products to healthcare professionals. They provide product information and demonstrate features to healthcare professionals. Medical representatives negotiate and close sales contracts.

candidates.description: Customer service representatives handle complaints and are responsible for maintaining overall goodwill between an organisation and its customers. They manage data regarding customer satisfaction and report it.

description: Application Specialist (Haematology) provides technical and application support for haematology analysers and related diagnostic systems used in clinical and near-patient testing environments. The role involves assisting with installation, calibration and maintenance of equipment, delivering user training, and advising laboratory and healthcare personnel on the appropriate use of devices to ensure accurate and efficient diagnostic outcomes.
tasks: Install, configure, calibrate, and maintain haematology analysers and related diagnostic systems to ensure optimal performance. Provide hands-on training and application guidance to laboratory and clinical staff on the proper use of equipment. Assist customers with equipment installation, validation, and troubleshooting, both on-site and remotely. Provide technical product demonstrations and application support to customers and internal teams. Monitor device performance and carry out preventive maintenance and routine servicing in accordance with operational requirements. Maintain accurate service, support, and compliance documentation, and prepare related reports in accordance with regulatory standards. Analyse user feedback and device performance data to support service quality and product improvement. Provide technical advice and application information to customers, laboratory personnel, and internal teams.

candidates.title: chemical application specialist
candidates.description: Chemical application specialists develop chemical products according to the needs and expectation of the clients. They conduct development of formulas and processes of formulation as well as evaluation of the efficiency and performances of the formulations.

candidates.title: anatomical pathology technician
candidates.description: Anatomical pathology technicians assist specialised doctors in pathology in conducting post-mortem examinations, keeping records of the samples, specimens, organs and the respective findings and taking care of their appropriate disposal under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: specialist biomedical scientist
candidates.description: Specialist biomedical scientists lead a department or specialist area, undertaking clinical research projects and working as a diagnostic partner within the health care team (investigating and diagnosing patient illnesses like, cancer, diabetes, haematological disorders and coagulation, in the areas of molecular biology or genomics, among others) using several methods, digital tools, and bioinformatics.

candidates.title: healthcare specialist lecturer
candidates.description: Healthcare specialist lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of healthcare, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of specialist healthcare, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: application engineer
candidates.description: Application engineers deal with the technical requirements, management, and design for the development of various engineering applications, such as systems, new product designs, or the improvements of processes. They are responsible for the implementation of a design or process improvement, they offer technical support for products, answer questions about the technical functionality and assist the sales team.

candidates.title: specialised doctor
candidates.description: Specialised doctors prevent, diagnose and treat diseases depending on their medical or surgical specialty.

candidates.title: medical laboratory manager
candidates.description: Medical laboratory managers oversee the daily operations of a medical laboratory. They manage employees and communicate the schedule of activities. They monitor and ensure all laboratory operations are performed according to specifications, arrange the necessary laboratory equipment and assure that the appropriate health and safety standards are followed.

candidates.title: medical physics expert
candidates.description: Medical physics experts advice on matters related to radiation physics applied to medical exposure. They are responsible for dosimetry and the optimisation of the radiation protection of patients and other individuals subjected to medical exposure, including the application and use of diagnostic reference levels. Medical physics experts are involved in the selection of medical radiological equipment, the quality assurance including acceptance testing, the preparation of technical specifications, and the installation, design and surveillance of the medical radiological installations. They also analyse the events involving accidental or unintended medical exposures and are responsible for the training of practitioners and other staff in relevant aspects of radiation protection.

description: Sales Representative (Information and Communications Technology) is responsible for marketing and selling ICT products and services, including software, hardware, telecommunications and cloud solutions, to business or individual clients. They assess customer requirements, recommend suitable technology solutions, prepare proposals and negotiate terms of sale. The role also involves coordinating related services such as installation and providing relevant product information to ensure customer satisfaction throughout the sales process.
tasks: Identify potential business opportunities and assess customer requirements for suitable Information and Communications Technology (ICT) products and services. Prepare and present solution proposals and product demonstrations to clients. Sell ICT products and services, including software, hardware, telecommunications and cloud solutions, to businesses or individuals. Advise customers on how ICT products and services meet their operational requirements. Negotiate prices, terms of sale and contracts, and complete related order documentation. Coordinate delivery, installation and related services for sold products and solutions. Maintain long-term customer relationships and provide post-sale support to ensure customer satisfaction. Report customer feedback, requirements and market information to manufacturers and internal teams. Collaborate with technical and support teams to deliver tailored ICT solutions.

description: Digital Banking-Internet Technology Specialist sells and promotes information and communications technology products and services, while supporting the implementation and integration of these solutions within digital banking environments. The role is responsible for the development, maintenance and enhancement of internet and mobile banking platforms, ensuring that systems are secure, user-oriented and compliant with regulatory requirements. They contribute to technological improvements that strengthen customer experience and operational efficiency in digital banking services.
tasks: Design, develop, maintain, and enhance internet and mobile banking systems. Integrate new digital services into existing digital banking platforms. Ensure digital banking solutions comply with security, regulatory, and internal standards. Analyse system performance and troubleshoot technical issues in digital banking platforms. Collaborate with cybersecurity, compliance, business development, and related teams to support digital banking solutions. Advise customers on digital banking products and services based on their needs. Coordinate delivery, installation, and service provision for digital banking solutions.

candidates.title: bank manager
candidates.description: Bank managers oversee the management of one or several bank activities. They set policies which promote safe banking operations, ensure the economic, social and commercial targets are met and that all the bank departments, activities and commercial policies are in compliance with legal requirements. They also manage employees and maintain an effective working relationship among the staff.

candidates.title: banking products manager
candidates.description: Banking products managers study the market of banking products and adapt the existing ones to the characteristics of this evolution or create new products to suit clients needs. They monitor and evaluate the performance indicators of these products and suggest improvements. Banking products managers assist with the sales and marketing strategy of the bank.

candidates.title: bank account manager
candidates.description: Bank account managers advise prospective clients on the type of banking accounts suitable for their needs. They work with clients to set up the bank account and remain their primary point of contact in the bank, assisting with all necessary documentation. Bank account managers may recommend their clients to contact other departments in the bank for other specific needs.

candidates.title: corporate banking adviser
candidates.description: Corporate banking advisers offer advice on a broad range of financial goods and services such as securities services, credit services, cash management, insurance products, leasing, information on merges and acquisitions and capital markets activities, to institutions and organisations.

candidates.title: relationship banking manager
candidates.description: Relationship banking managers retain and expand existing and prospective customer relationships. They use cross-selling techniques to advise and sell various banking and financial products and services to customers. They also manage the total relationship with customers and are responsible for optimising business results and customer satisfaction.

candidates.title: digital marketing manager
candidates.description: Digital marketing managers are responsible for the elaboration of the company's digital marketing strategy with the goal of improving brand recognition and brand awareness, in line with the company's mission and vision. They oversee the execution of digital marketing and communication strategies involving the use of social media, email marketing, marketing automation, search engine optimisation, online events and online advertisement through data driven methodologies and by measuring and monitoring digital marketing KPIs in order to promptly implement corrective action plan. They manage and interpret competitors and consumers' data and conduct research on market conditions.

candidates.title: bank teller
candidates.description: Bank tellers deal most frequently with customers of the bank. They promote the banks products and services, and provide information about the customers personal accounts and related transfers, deposits, savings etc. They order bank cards and checks for the customers, receive and balance cash and checks and ensure compliance with internal policies. They work on client accounts, deal with payments and manage the use of vaults and safe deposit boxes.

candidates.title: ICT account manager
candidates.description: ICT account managers build business relationships with customers to facilitate the sale of hardware, software, telecommunications or ICT services. They also identify opportunities and manage sourcing and delivery of products to customers. They achieve sales targets and maintain profitability.

description: Management Information Systems (MIS) Analyst designs, develops, and enhances an information system to collect, process, and analyse business data for reporting and decision-making. They implement and maintain MIS solutions, produce reports and dashboards, ensure data accuracy, and recommend system improvements to support and optimise organisational performance.
tasks: Collect and analyse organisational data to generate insights that support business decision-making. Design, develop, enhance and maintain management information systems, including data reporting tools and automated dashboards. Gather and define user requirements for Management Information Systems (MIS) solutions in collaboration with business stakeholders. Ensure data accuracy, integrity and consistency across multiple systems and databases. Monitor and evaluate system performance, and resolve technical or data-related issues. Prepare and present reports, dashboards and analytical outputs to support organisational reporting and decision-making. Manage and maintain data resources used for organisational analysis and reporting. Provide user support and training on Management Information Systems (MIS) tools, systems and reporting platforms.

candidates.title: ICT system analyst
candidates.description: ICT system analysts specify the system needs to meet the end user requirements. They analyse system functions in order to define their goals or purposes and to discover operations and procedures for accomplishing them most efficiently. They also design new IT solutions to improve business efficiency and productivity, produce outline designs and estimate costs of new systems, specify the operations the system will perform, and the way data will be viewed by the end user. They present the design to the users and work closely with the users to implement the solution.

candidates.title: information manager
candidates.description: Information managers are responsible for systems that provide information to people. They assure access to the information in different work environments (public or private) based on theoretical principles and hands-on capabilities in storing, retrieving and communicating information.

candidates.title: ICT business analysis manager
candidates.description: ICT business analysis managers identify areas where information system changes are needed to support business plans and monitor the impact in terms of change management. They contribute to the general ICT functional requirements of the business organisation. ICT business analysis managers analyse business needs and translate them into ICT solutions.

candidates.title: ICT business analyst
candidates.description: ICT business analysts are in charge of analysing and designing an organisation's processes and systems, assessing the business model and its integration with technology. They also identify change needs, assess the impact of the change, capture and document requirements and then ensure that these requirements are delivered whilst supporting the business through the implementation process.

candidates.title: ICT information and knowledge manager
candidates.description: ICT information and knowledge managers contribute to the definition of organisational information strategy and apply information and knowledge creation, editing, storage, and distribution policies. They manage the maintenance and evolution of structured and unstructured information. They create digital structures to enable exploitation and optimisation of information and knowledge, manage data analysis and enable business intelligence.

candidates.title: data analyst
candidates.description: Data analysts import, inspect, clean, transform, validate, model, or interpret collections of data with regard to the business goals of the company. They ensure that the data sources and repositories provide consistent and reliable data. Data analysts use different algorithms and IT tools as demanded by the situation and the current data. They might prepare reports in the form of visualisations such as graphs, charts, and dashboards.

candidates.title: business analyst
candidates.description: Business analysts research and understand the strategic position of businesses and companies in relation to their markets and their stakeholders. They analyse and present their views on how the company, from many perspectives, can improve its strategic position and internal corporate structure. They assess needs for change, communication methods, technology, IT tools, new standards and certifications.

candidates.title: ICT operations manager
candidates.description: ICT operations managers coordinate ICT services and infrastructure ensuring that the organisation has the required infrastructural resources. They also plan and monitor stages of either a business process or a computer process, negotiate contracts and take mitigation action in case of non-fulfilment of agreements. They oversee the day-to-day tasks involving infrastructure components, ICT systems and software.

description: Technical Specialist (.Net) designs, develops, and maintains software applications using the Microsoft .NET framework, translating business and user requirements into functional solutions. They analyse organisational IT needs, provide technical guidance, and ensure that systems and applications are well-integrated, performant, and reliable across platforms. The role also involves resolving technical issues, optimising backend services, and supporting the implementation of tailored IT solutions to meet business objectives.
tasks: Analyse business and user requirements to determine appropriate system functionalities and technical solutions. Design and develop scalable .NET software applications, web components, and related system solutions. Prepare technical specifications, application designs, and system documentation for development and implementation. Collaborate with developers, engineers, and stakeholders to integrate and deploy IT systems and applications. Test, debug, and verify software and systems to ensure functionality, quality, and compatibility. Maintain, update, and troubleshoot existing .NET applications and IT systems to ensure reliable performance. Identify technical issues or system inefficiencies and recommend improvements to optimise performance. Manage system configuration and software upgrades in line with operational and technical requirements. Support system implementation activities and monitor system performance after deployment. Provide technical guidance, documentation, and user support for system usage and maintenance.

candidates.title: technical communicator
candidates.description: Technical communicators prepare clear, concise and professional communication from product developers to users of the products such as online help, user manuals, white papers, specifications and industrial videos. For this, they analyse products, legal requirements, markets, customers and users. They develop information and media concepts, standards, structures and software tool support. They plan the content creation and media production processes, develop written, graphical, video or other contents, generate media output, release their information products and receive feedback from the users.

candidates.title: technical director
candidates.description: Technical directors realise the artistic visions of the creators within technical constraints. They perform network address assignment, management and implementation of routing protocols such as ISIS, OSPF, BGP, routing table configurations and certain implementations of authentication. They perform maintenance and administration of servers (file servers, VPN gateways, intrusion detection systems), desktop computers, printers, routers, switches, firewalls, phones, IP communications, personal digital assistants, smartphones, software deployment, security updates and patches as well as a vast array of additional technologies inclusive of both hardware and software.

candidates.title: computer hardware engineering technician
candidates.description: Computer hardware engineering technicians collaborate with computer hardware engineers in the development of computer hardware, such as motherboards, routers, and microprocessors. Computer hardware engineering technicians are responsible for building, testing, monitoring, and maintaining the developed computer technology.

candidates.title: ICT system administrator
candidates.description: ICT system administrators are responsible for the upkeep, configuration, and reliable operation of computer and network systems, servers, workstations and peripheral devices. They may acquire, install, or upgrade computer components and software; automate routine tasks; write computer programs; troubleshoot; train and supervise staff; and provide technical support. They ensure optimum system integrity, security, backup and performance.

candidates.title: ICT network technician
candidates.description: ICT network technicians install, maintain and troubleshoot networks, data communications equipment and network installed devices such as printers and storage area networks. They also analyse and fix network-related problems reported by users.

candidates.title: computer hardware engineer
candidates.description: Computer hardware engineers design and develop computer hardware systems and components, such as circuit boards, modems, and printers. They draught blueprints and assembly drawings, develop and test the prototypes, and supervise the production process.

candidates.title: ICT network engineer
candidates.description: ICT network engineers implement, maintain and support computer networks. They also perform network modelling, analysis, and planning. They may also design network and computer security measures. They may research and recommend network and data communications hardware and software.

candidates.title: computer scientist
candidates.description: Computer scientists conduct research in computer and information science, directed toward greater knowledge and understanding of fundamental aspects of ICT phenomena. They write research reports and proposals. Computer scientists also invent and design new approaches to computing technology, find innovative uses for existing technology and studies and solve complex problems in computing.

candidates.title: user interface developer

candidates.title: user interface designer

candidates.title: digital games designer

candidates.title: digital games developer

Data protection officers lead investigations into potential data breaches, conduct internal audits and act as point of contact within the organisation on any matters related to the processing of personal data. Data protection officers may develop training programmes and provide training to other employees on data protection procedures.

candidates.description: Data quality specialists review organisation's data for accuracy, recommend enhancements to record systems and data acquisition processes and assess referential and historical integrity of data. They also develop documents and maintain data quality goals and standards and oversee an organisation's data privacy policy and monitor compliance of data flows against data quality standards.

candidates.title: ICT security technician
candidates.description: ICT security technicians propose and implement necessary security updates and measures whenever is required. They advise, support, inform and provide training and security awareness.

candidates.title: data scientist

Evaluate and analyse threat intelligence and security data to support risk management and operational improvements.

Embedded systems security engineers help to keep attackers at bay by implementing safeguards that prevent intrusions and breaches.

description: Test Analyst (Information Technology) is responsible for ensuring the quality, reliability, and security of IT systems and software. They design, develop, and execute test plans and cases to evaluate functionality and performance, identify issues or defects, and document findings. Working closely with development and business teams, they help ensure software meets technical specifications and user requirements throughout the software development life cycle.
