candidates.description: Dental practitioners prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues.

candidates.title: healthcare assistant
candidates.description: Healthcare assistants work in teams of nurses within the occupational fields of nursing, social care, clinical care and care of people of all age-groups. Healthcare assistants assist in the promotion and restoration of patients' health by providing physical and psychological support to patients, friends and families.

candidates.title: medical administrative assistant
candidates.description: Medical administrative assistants work very closely with health professionals. They provide office support such as correspondence, fixing appointments and answering queries of patients.

candidates.title: dental hygienist
candidates.description: Dental hygienists work in cleaning and polishing teeth, supra- and sub-gingival scaling of the teeth, application of prophylactic materials to the teeth, collecting data, administering comprehensive advice on oral hygiene and the care of the mouth, according to patients` needs under the supervision of dental practitioners following her/his directions.

candidates.title: dental technician
candidates.description: Dental technicians manufacture dental custom-made devices like bridges, crowns, dentures and appliances under the supervision of dental practitioners following their directions and specifications.

description: Dental Therapist Grade U5 provides dental services in terms of diagnosis, treatment, prevention, and health promotion for children aged 17 years and below, with a focus on pre-school children, primary school, and secondary school students nationwide. Responsible for providing specialised dental services to achieve the goal of ensuring the community attains optimal oral health.
tasks: Performing dental examination, diagnosis, and treatment (school children, pre-school/special needs children), infection control, and health safety. Delivering health messages, nutritional advice, toothbrushing instruction, fissure sealing, health promotion, leaflets/posters, and participating in community projects under the dental health programme. Providing counselling on periodontium/orthodontic conditions, dental health education, and instruction on toothbrushing techniques and the use of specialised toothbrushes. Conducting periodontium, orthodontic, paediatric, and oral surgical treatment, including prophylaxis, scaling, polishing, root canal treatment, sedation, STO/dressing, and regimen monitoring. Managing clinical data and records, daily/annual statements, and supports clinical audit, ISO, QAP, accreditation, and incident reporting.

candidates.title: dental hygienist
candidates.description: Dental hygienists work in cleaning and polishing teeth, supra- and sub-gingival scaling of the teeth, application of prophylactic materials to the teeth, collecting data, administering comprehensive advice on oral hygiene and the care of the mouth, according to patients` needs under the supervision of dental practitioners following her/his directions.

candidates.title: dental practitioner
candidates.description: Dental practitioners prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues.

candidates.title: specialist dentist
candidates.description: Specialist dentists prevent, diagnose and treat anomalies and diseases affecting the teeth, mouth, jaws and adjoining tissues specialised in oral surgery or orthodontics.

candidates.title: dental technician
candidates.description: Dental technicians manufacture dental custom-made devices like bridges, crowns, dentures and appliances under the supervision of dental practitioners following their directions and specifications.

candidates.title: dental chairside assistant
candidates.description: Dental chairside assistants support dental practitioners in clinical treatments, as preparation and helping in practical execution and follow-up, and administrative tasks under supervision and following the orders of the dental practitioner.

candidates.title: dentistry lecturer
candidates.description: Dentistry lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, dentistry, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of dentistry, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: occupational therapist
candidates.description: Occupational therapists assist individuals or groups who have occupational limitations due to diseases, physical disorders, and temporary or permanent mental disabilities, in regaining their ability to perform daily activities. They provide treatment and rehabilitation to enable them to actively participate in society, to live their lives according to their wishes and to perform those activities that are meaningful to them. Occupational therapists work in public health and social care services, but can also be involved in supporting asylum seekers, refugees and/or homeless people.

candidates.title: complementary therapist
candidates.description: Complementary therapists use a range of complementary and alternative therapies to work simultaneously with the clients` body, mind, and spirit in a holistic approach. They offer practices and services for holistic wellbeing, health maintenance, health education, health promotion and prevention of illness, along with the sustainable treatment of certain illnesses, especially chronic illnesses. Their practices include but are not limited to acupuncture, aromatherapy, banotherapy, homeopathy, and herbal medicine.

description: Community Health Promoter engages with an individual or group to raise awareness of health issues, encourage healthy behaviours, and support access to health services. They act as a link between a healthcare provider and the community, providing culturally relevant health education and guidance, particularly in an underserved area. Their work typically focuses on preventive and advisory health activities, including chronic disease prevention, maternal and child health, immunisation, nutrition, mental health, and infectious disease control.
tasks: Conduct health education and awareness programmes within the community to promote healthy behaviours. Provide guidance on disease prevention, hygiene, nutrition, and healthy lifestyle practices. Conduct household and institutional visits to assess community health needs. Facilitate referrals to healthcare and social service providers. Support immunisation campaigns, health screenings, and other preventive health initiatives. Develop and distribute culturally appropriate health communication materials for the local population. Assist in collecting health data, conducting surveys, and evaluating health programmes. Collaborate with local leaders to promote community participation in health programmes.

candidates.title: community health worker
candidates.description: Community health workers provide advice and information about various health subjects to the community. They can assist with pre- and post-natal care, give nutritional advice and help individuals stop smoking. Community health workers develop health and prevention programmes.

candidates.title: community development officer
candidates.description: Community development officers develop plans to improve quality of life in local communities. They investigate and assess the community's issues and needs, manage resources, and develop implementation strategies. They communicate with the community for investigation purposes, and to inform the community on development plans.

candidates.title: promoter
candidates.description: Promoters work with artists (or their agents) and venues on to arrange a show. They liaise with bands and agents to agree on a date for a performance and negotiate a deal. They book a venue and promote the upcoming gig. They make sure everything the band needs is in place and set up soundcheck times and the running order of the show. Some promoters work freelance, but they may also be tied to a single venue or festival.

candidates.title: adult community care worker
candidates.description: Adult community care workers perform assessment and care management of communities of adults who live with physical impairments or convalescing states. They aim to improve their life in the community and enable them to live safely and independently at their own home.

candidates.title: public health policy officer
candidates.description: Public health policy officers develop and implement strategies for the improvement of a community's health care policy. They advise governments on policy changes and identify problems in current health care policies.

candidates.title: community artist
candidates.description: Community artists research, plan, organise and lead artistic activities for people brought together by a shared interest, capacity, environment or condition. They manage and coordinate creative projects with local groups and individuals to foster their artistic creativity and improve their quality of life. Community artists make the arts accessible to the community they work for, and provide opportunities for participants to shape their artistic programme.

candidates.title: health psychologist
candidates.description: Health psychologists deal with the various aspects of health related behaviour of individuals and groups, by helping individuals or groups prevent illness and promote healthy behaviours by also providing counseling services. They perform tasks for the development of health promotion activities and projects on the basis of psychological science, research findings, theories, methods and techniques. They also engage in research about health related issues to influence public policy on health care issues.

candidates.title: community care case worker
candidates.description: Community care case workers perform assessment and care management. They organise domiciliary services to support vulnerable adults who are living with physical impairment or convalescing, aiming to improve their lives in the community and enabling them to live safely and independently at their own home.

description: Village Health Worker provides basic healthcare services within a community, particularly in rural or underserved areas. They promote health awareness, support disease prevention, assist with simple medical procedures, and educate the community on hygiene, maternal and child health, immunisation, nutrition, and sanitation. Acting as a link between the public and a healthcare institution, they conduct home visits, maintain community health records, and help individuals or families access broader health and social services.
tasks: Conduct community outreach to promote healthy behaviours and disease prevention. Educate individuals and families on nutrition, hygiene, immunisations, maternal and child health, and advise on preventive health practices. Support immunisation drives and health screening campaigns. Provide first aid and basic health treatments. Monitor vulnerable populations, including pregnant women, infants, and the elderly. Refer patients to clinics or hospitals for further care. Distribute medications and basic health supplies. Collect, organise, and report health data to relevant authorities. Conduct home visits to provide basic health services and information on health and social services.

candidates.title: community health worker
candidates.description: Community health workers provide advice and information about various health subjects to the community. They can assist with pre- and post-natal care, give nutritional advice and help individuals stop smoking. Community health workers develop health and prevention programmes.

candidates.title: care home worker
candidates.description: Care home workers provide domiciliary services to vulnerable adults including frail elderly or disabled people who are living with physical impairment or convalescing, following a specific plan to provide day-to-day care to clients. They look after the physical and mental wellbeing of clients by providing them social care. These services could be developed in residential homes, care homes or in the patient's home. In relation to this last case, they aim to improve patients' lives in the community and assure patients can live safely and independently in their own home.

candidates.title: adult community care worker
candidates.description: Adult community care workers perform assessment and care management of communities of adults who live with physical impairments or convalescing states. They aim to improve their life in the community and enable them to live safely and independently at their own home.

candidates.title: community care case worker
candidates.description: Community care case workers perform assessment and care management. They organise domiciliary services to support vulnerable adults who are living with physical impairment or convalescing, aiming to improve their lives in the community and enabling them to live safely and independently at their own home.

candidates.title: hospital social worker
candidates.description: Hospital social workers provide counselling to patients and their families helping them to better cope with the illness, the emotions surrounding diagnosis, and with social and financial problems. They work in cooperation with doctors, nurses and other health professionals sensitising them on the emotional aspects of a patient. They act as link between patients and medical staff. Hospital social workers also support the patients and their families with the discharge from the hospital.

candidates.title: youth worker
candidates.description: Youth workers support, accompany and counsel young people, focusing on their personal and social development. They are involved in managing community projects and services through one-to-one or group-based activities. Youth workers can be volunteers or paid professionals who facilitate non-formal and informal learning processes. They are engaged in a large spectrum of activities by, with and for young people.

candidates.title: social care worker
candidates.description: Social care workers provide support and help people with care services. They help people to live full and valued lives in the community. They assist babies, young children, adolescents, adults and older adults.They attend to the psychological, social, emotional and physical needs of service users. They work in a large variety of settings with individuals, families, groups, organisations and communities.

candidates.title: animal shelter worker
candidates.description: Animal shelter workers provide animal care routine services at the animal shelter. They receive animals brought to the shelter, respond to calls about lost or injured animals, nurse animals, clean cages, handle papers for adoption of animals, transport animals to the veterinarian and maintain database with the animals present in the shelter.

description: Community Nurse Grade U1 responsible as a health worker who performs various duties and is a member of the health team who serves the community directly.
tasks: Performing nursing practice, adhering to ethics, and ensuring annual practice is always up to date. Conducting antenatal clinic, interviews, physical examinations, collection of blood/urine samples, injections, vitamins, and referral of high-risk cases. Managing deliveries at clinics/Alternative Birthing Centres (ABC), including partogram monitoring, maternal and neonatal care, resuscitation, and administration of Vitamin K1 ampoule/BCG injections. Providing postnatal care at home, including maternal and neonatal examinations, guidance on exercise/nutrition, family planning, and referral of exceptional cases. Preparing equipment for child clinic sessions, physical examinations, growth monitoring, immunisation, minor illness treatment, FCM, nutrition, and referral of special cases. Motivating mothers on family planning methods, health examinations, Pap smear, and referral for contraceptives or health issues. Conducting home visits for high-risk pregnant mothers, children with incomplete immunisation, special needs cases, and investigates maternal/child deaths. Providing health education, breastfeeding guidance, infant care, nutrition, health activity demonstrations, and family counselling. Managing and operating rural clinics, including preparation of medicines/vaccines, hygiene, safety, documentation, patient registration, minor treatments, and first aid. Supporting nursing training, quality programmes, meetings/committees, community/village midwife collaboration, and routine clinic documentation.

candidates.title: community health worker
candidates.description: Community health workers provide advice and information about various health subjects to the community. They can assist with pre- and post-natal care, give nutritional advice and help individuals stop smoking. Community health workers develop health and prevention programmes.

candidates.title: adult community care worker
candidates.description: Adult community care workers perform assessment and care management of communities of adults who live with physical impairments or convalescing states. They aim to improve their life in the community and enable them to live safely and independently at their own home.

candidates.title: nurse assistant
candidates.description: Nurse assistants provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. They perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, move patients or change linens and may transfer or transport patients.

candidates.title: specialist nurse
candidates.description: Specialist nurses promote and restore people's health, and diagnose and care within a specific branch of the nursing field. Examples of such specialist nursing jobs include but are not restricted to; ambulatory care nurse, advanced practice nurse, cardiac nurse, dental nurse, community health nurse, forensic nurse, gastroenterology nurse, hospice and palliative care nurse, paediatric nurse, public health nurse, rehabilitation nurse, renal nurse and school nurse. Specialist nurses are general care nurses prepared beyond the level of a nurse generalist and authorised to practice as specialists with specific expertise in a branch of the nursing field.

candidates.title: community care case worker
candidates.description: Community care case workers perform assessment and care management. They organise domiciliary services to support vulnerable adults who are living with physical impairment or convalescing, aiming to improve their lives in the community and enabling them to live safely and independently at their own home.

candidates.title: nurse responsible for general care
candidates.description: Nurses responsible for general care are in charge of promoting and restoring patients` health by providing physical and psychological support to patients, friends, and families. They also supervise assigned team members.

candidates.title: advanced nurse practitioner
candidates.description: Advanced nurse practitioners are in charge of promoting and restoring patients` health, provide diagnosis and care in advanced settings, coordinating care within areas of chronic disease management, providing integrated care, and supervising assigned team members. Advanced nurse practitioners are general care nurses who have acquired an expert knowledge base, complex decision making skills and clinical competencies for expanded clinical practice on advanced level.

candidates.title: midwife
candidates.description: Midwives assist women in childbirth by providing the necessary support, care and advice during pregnancy, labour and the postpartum period, conduct births and provide care for the new-born. They advise on health, preventive measures, preparation for parenthood, detection of complications in mother and child, accessing of medical care, promoting normal birth and carrying out emergency measures.

description: Optician provides professional vision care by fitting, dispensing, and advising on a corrective lens, including a spectacle or contact lens, according to a prescription from an optometrist or ophthalmologist. They assess a client’s visual needs, perform precise measurements, ensure optimal lens fit and comfort, and guide on the proper use and care of the eyewear to support visual health and comfort.
tasks: Interpret optical and contact lens prescriptions accurately. Advise patients on suitable lenses, frames, and styles. Measure, fit, adjust, and repair lenses and eyewear to ensure comfort and proper function. Educate patients on lens care, hygiene, insertion, removal, and maintenance procedures. Examine and verify received lenses against specifications and quality standards. Manage inventory, ordering, and sales of optical products and accessories. Collaborate and coordinate with optometrists, ophthalmologists, and other eye care professionals. Conduct patient follow-ups to monitor adaptation and address vision-related concerns.

candidates.title: optician
candidates.description: Opticians help to improve and correct an individual's vision. They fit spectacle lenses and frames, contact lenses, and other devices according to the specifications of the individual. Their scope of practice varies according to national regulations and they might operate according to prescriptions provided by a specialised doctor in ophthalmology or an optometrist in the countries where requested.

candidates.title: optical technician
candidates.description: Optical technicians assemble, repair and design various parts of eyewear such as lenses, frames, patterns and eyewear. They cut, inspect, mount and polish all parts using various machinery and hand tools. Optical technicians shape, grind and coat lenses for prescription eyewear. They fit completed lenses into eyeglass frames. Optical technicians ensure that lenses conform to the dispensing optician’s, specialised doctor in ophtalmology's or optometrist's prescriptions. They may also work with other associated optical instrumentation and its maintenance.

candidates.title: optometrist
candidates.description: Optometrists examine and test eyes to identify abnormalities, visual problems, or disease. They prescribe and fit lenses such as spectacles and contacts, and offer advice on visual problems. They may also refer patients to a medical practitioner. Their scope of practice and title varies according to national regulations.

candidates.title: eyewear and optical equipment shop manager
candidates.description: Eyewear and optical equipment shop managers assume responsibility for activities and staff in specialised shops.

candidates.title: eyewear and optical equipment specialised seller
candidates.description: Eyewear and optical equipment specialised sellers sell glasses in specialised shops.

candidates.title: optical engineer
candidates.description: Optical engineers design and develop different industrial applications with optics. They have knowledge of light, light transmission principles, and optics in order to design engineering specs of equipment such as microscopes, lenses, telescopes, and other optical devices.

candidates.title: optomechanical engineering technician
candidates.description: Optomechanical engineering technicians collaborate with engineers in the development of optomechanical devices, such as optical tables, deformable mirrors, and optical mounts. Optomechanical engineering technicians build, install, test, and maintain optomechanical equipment prototypes. They determine materials and assembly requirements.

candidates.title: optomechanical engineer
candidates.description: Optomechanical engineers design and develop optomechanical systems, devices, and components, such as optical mirrors and optical mounts. Optomechanical engineering combines optical engineering with mechanical engineering in the design of these systems and devices. They conduct research, perform analysis, test the devices, and supervise the research.

description: Massage Therapist manipulates the soft tissues of the body, including muscles, tendons, ligaments, and skin, to relieve pain, rehabilitate an injury, reduce stress, and promote overall wellness. They assess a client’s condition, determine a suitable treatment method, and provide guidance on post-treatment care. They may work in a spa, wellness centre, hotel, rehabilitation facility, or healthcare institution, delivering personalised therapy in a professional and hygienic environment.
tasks: Evaluate clients’ physical condition and determine treatment needs through consultation and assessment. Apply appropriate massage techniques to improve circulation, relieve tension, and support muscle recovery and well-being. Advise clients on posture, stretching, strengthening, relaxation techniques, rehabilitative exercises, and injury prevention practices. Adapt massage treatments based on client progress, feedback, and medical conditions. Maintain hygiene standards and ensure a clean, safe, and relaxing therapy environment. Document treatment sessions, track client progress, and record client feedback. Collaborate with physiotherapists and other healthcare professionals when necessary.

candidates.title: massage therapist
candidates.description: Massage therapists provide therapeutic massage treatments to improve the well-being of their clients. They perform a variety of massage types such as shiatsu and swedish massage, according to their client's needs and preferences.

candidates.title: animal massage therapist
candidates.description: Animal massage therapists provide a therapeutic treatment following veterinary diagnosis or referral concentrating on manual and mechanical manipulation of soft tissues to promote healing and recovery in animals in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: sport therapist
candidates.description: Sport therapists program and supervise rehabilitation exercises for individuals and groups. They work with individuals that have chronic health conditions or are at high risk of developing them. They communicate with medical and healthcare professionals about participants' conditions using correct medical terminology, and with an understanding of the standard treatment options for an individual’s condition. Sport therapists take a holistic approach to the wellness of their clients that includes advising on lifestyle, food or time management. They do not have a medical background and do not require medical qualifications.

candidates.title: herbal therapist
candidates.description: Herbal therapists use herbal medicine to relief pain and treat illnesses such as allergies, chronic physical conditions or stress-related conditions. They study the properties and benefits of plants and create a personalised treatment plan for the patients.

candidates.title: recreational therapist
candidates.description: Recreational therapists offer treatment to persons who have behavioural disorders or conditions. They use techniques and interventions such as art, music, animals and dance to promote, maintain and restore the development and health of the patient.

candidates.title: dance therapist
candidates.description: Dance therapists support individuals with their emotional, mental or physical health problems helping them to improve their body awareness, self-esteem, social integration and personal development through dance and movement patterns within a therapeutic environment.

candidates.title: physiotherapist
candidates.description: Physiotherapists are autonomous health professionals who are responsible for developing, maintaining or restoring motor function and movement throughout the lifespan using evidence-based practice. They relieve pain and treat or prevent physical conditions associated with injury, disease or other impairments. Physiotherapists empower patients and their carers to manage the condition outside clinical settings. They work within their scope of practice and their professional Code of Conduct.

candidates.title: complementary therapist
candidates.description: Complementary therapists use a range of complementary and alternative therapies to work simultaneously with the clients` body, mind, and spirit in a holistic approach. They offer practices and services for holistic wellbeing, health maintenance, health education, health promotion and prevention of illness, along with the sustainable treatment of certain illnesses, especially chronic illnesses. Their practices include but are not limited to acupuncture, aromatherapy, banotherapy, homeopathy, and herbal medicine.

description: Physiotherapy Technician assists licensed physiotherapists in supporting patients recover from physical impairment, injury, or illness. They prepare equipment and therapy room, guide the patient through exercises or specialised treatments such as electrotherapy, hydrotherapy, or shiatsu, and monitor progress while documenting outcomes. Working under professional supervision, they help implement treatment plans effectively to enhance mobility, reduce pain, and promote overall rehabilitation and well-being.
tasks: Assist physiotherapists during therapy sessions, including supporting patient assessment and treatment delivery. Apply physiotherapy techniques and exercise programmes as directed. Guide and supervise patients in prescribed exercises and the safe use of assistive and mobility devices. Advise patients on correct body posture, injury prevention, and rehabilitation practices. Monitor and record patient responses and progress during therapy sessions. Maintain, prepare, and ensure proper hygiene of therapy equipment and treatment environments. Coordinate patient care activities, including appointment scheduling, clinical documentation, record management, and referrals to healthcare professionals. Educate patients on therapy procedures, home exercise programmes, and complementary rehabilitation practices.

candidates.title: physiotherapist
candidates.description: Physiotherapists are autonomous health professionals who are responsible for developing, maintaining or restoring motor function and movement throughout the lifespan using evidence-based practice. They relieve pain and treat or prevent physical conditions associated with injury, disease or other impairments. Physiotherapists empower patients and their carers to manage the condition outside clinical settings. They work within their scope of practice and their professional Code of Conduct.

candidates.title: physiotherapy assistant
candidates.description: Physiotherapy assistants work under supervision, within defined contexts using agreed treatment protocols and procedures such as collecting client data and maintaining the equipment required in physiotherapy interventions. The overall responsibility is retained by the delegating professional.

candidates.title: advanced physiotherapist
candidates.description: Advanced physiotherapists are highly specialised. They make complex decisions and manage risks in unpredictable contexts and within a defined area. They may focus on a specific area of clinical practice, education, research or professional management.

candidates.title: respiratory therapy technician
candidates.description: Respiratory therapy technicians assist doctors and surgeons to treat respiratory problems. They work in hospitals and medical facilities where they operate medical equipment to test patients' respiratory conditions and aid in their treatment. Respiratory therapy technicians also tend to breathing equipment and machines during surgery.

candidates.title: animal physiotherapist
candidates.description: Animal physiotherapists provide a therapeutic treatment following veterinary diagnosis or referral. They concentrate on the application of physical therapy and exercise procedures to support animal rehabilitation after a surgery or an injury, aiming to return the animals to normal function and/or maintain performance in accordance with national legislation.

candidates.title: physics technician
candidates.description: Physics technicians monitor physical processes and perform tests for manufacturing, educational or scientific purposes. They work in laboratories, schools or production facilities where they assist physicists in their work. Physics technicians perform technical or practical work and report about their results.

candidates.title: mechanical engineering technician
candidates.description: Mechanical engineering technicians provide technical support to mechanical engineers in producing and manufacturing mechanical machinery. They help make designs and adjustments, and perform tests. They also develop layouts and drawings, collate and interpret data and write reports.

candidates.title: sports equipment repair technician
candidates.description: Sports equipment repair technicians maintain and repair recreational sports equipment such as tennis rackets, archery tools and camping equipment. They use specialised hand tools or mechanical tools to restore damaged parts.

description: Stress Therapist assists individuals, family, or group in managing stress and improving mental well-being. They assess stress-related issues, develop personalised treatment plans, and use therapeutic techniques to help patients cope effectively, often working with a child, adolescent, or adult. They collaborate with another healthcare professionals to provide comprehensive care and may also be known as mental health counsellors or psychotherapists.
tasks: Conduct individual or group therapy sessions and identify individuals or groups requiring stress management support. Assess clients’ mental health and identify stress-related issues affecting emotional and psychological well-being. Develop and implement personalised stress management plans, including coping mechanisms and relaxation techniques. Monitor client progress and adjust stress management interventions as needed. Provide holistic psychosocial support by addressing stress-related issues and offering guidance to improve mental well-being. Collaborate with other professionals and utilise community resources to support clients’ mental health needs. Research and apply appropriate stress management and mental health support resources.

candidates.title: massage therapist
candidates.description: Massage therapists provide therapeutic massage treatments to improve the well-being of their clients. They perform a variety of massage types such as shiatsu and swedish massage, according to their client's needs and preferences.

candidates.title: psychotherapist
candidates.description: Psychotherapists assist and treat healthcare users with varying degrees of psychological, psychosocial, or psychosomatic behavioural disorders and pathogenic conditions by means of psychotherapeutic methods. They promote personal development and well-being and provide advice on improving relationships, capabilities, and problem-solving techniques. They use science-based psychotherapeutic methods such as behavioural therapy, existential analysis and logotherapy, psychoanalysis or systemic family therapy in order to guide the patients in their development and help them search for appropriate solutions to their problems. Psychotherapists are not required to have academic degrees in psychology or a medical qualification in psychiatry. It is an independent occupation from psychology, psychiatry, and counselling.

candidates.title: sport therapist
candidates.description: Sport therapists program and supervise rehabilitation exercises for individuals and groups. They work with individuals that have chronic health conditions or are at high risk of developing them. They communicate with medical and healthcare professionals about participants' conditions using correct medical terminology, and with an understanding of the standard treatment options for an individual’s condition. Sport therapists take a holistic approach to the wellness of their clients that includes advising on lifestyle, food or time management. They do not have a medical background and do not require medical qualifications.

candidates.title: art therapist
candidates.description: Art therapists help patients overcome psychological and emotional difficulties through an artistic process which reflects emotions and feelings, focusing on patients who suffer a variety of problems such as mental, psychological, and behavioural disorders in order to facilitate self-understanding and awareness.

candidates.title: social counsellor
candidates.description: Social counsellors provide support and guidance to individuals in the social work area, to help them solve specific problems in their personal life. It involves addressing personal and relationship issues, dealing with inner conflicts, crisis moments such as depression and addiction, in an attempt to empower individuals to achieve change and improve their life quality.

candidates.title: occupational therapist
candidates.description: Occupational therapists assist individuals or groups who have occupational limitations due to diseases, physical disorders, and temporary or permanent mental disabilities, in regaining their ability to perform daily activities. They provide treatment and rehabilitation to enable them to actively participate in society, to live their lives according to their wishes and to perform those activities that are meaningful to them. Occupational therapists work in public health and social care services, but can also be involved in supporting asylum seekers, refugees and/or homeless people.

candidates.title: mental health support worker
candidates.description: Mental health support workers assist and provide treatment to people with mental, emotional, or substance abuse problems. They focus on personalised cases and monitor the recovery process of their clients, providing also therapy, crisis intervention, client advocacy and education.

candidates.title: complementary therapist
candidates.description: Complementary therapists use a range of complementary and alternative therapies to work simultaneously with the clients` body, mind, and spirit in a holistic approach. They offer practices and services for holistic wellbeing, health maintenance, health education, health promotion and prevention of illness, along with the sustainable treatment of certain illnesses, especially chronic illnesses. Their practices include but are not limited to acupuncture, aromatherapy, banotherapy, homeopathy, and herbal medicine.

description: Medical Laboratory Assistant performs essential support functions in a clinical or research laboratory, assisting health and medical professionals with specimen collection, sample preparation, and basic tests. They perform administrative tasks, maintain laboratory cleanliness and equipment sterilisation, and ensure adherence to safety protocols to support accurate and efficient patient care.
tasks: Collect and label patient samples, including blood, urine, and tissue specimens. Prepare, process, and handle specimens for laboratory analysis. Perform basic laboratory tests under supervision. Assist medical technologists and pathologists in routine laboratory procedures. Record and enter test data accurately into Laboratory Information Systems (LIS). Maintain, clean, and sterilise laboratory equipment while ensuring compliance with infection control and laboratory safety regulations. Support basic health education activities for patients and individuals under supervision.

candidates.title: medical laboratory assistant
candidates.description: Medical laboratory assistants work under supervision of the biomedical scientist and carry out basic laboratory procedures. They work in the pre-analytical handling of samples such as checking the details of specimens received for analysis, maintaining analysers, loading reagents, and packaging specimens. They also perform clerical tasks such as monitoring the stock levels of reagents used in analysis.

candidates.title: medical laboratory manager
candidates.description: Medical laboratory managers oversee the daily operations of a medical laboratory. They manage employees and communicate the schedule of activities. They monitor and ensure all laboratory operations are performed according to specifications, arrange the necessary laboratory equipment and assure that the appropriate health and safety standards are followed.

candidates.title: doctors' surgery assistant
candidates.description: Doctors' surgery assistants support doctors of medicine in medical measures, in performing simple support activities during medical procedures, standardised diagnostic programmes and standardised point-of-care tests, ensuring surgery hygiene, cleaning, disinfecting, sterilising and maintaining medical devices and performing the organisational and administrative tasks required for operating a doctor`s surgery under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: medical administrative assistant
candidates.description: Medical administrative assistants work very closely with health professionals. They provide office support such as correspondence, fixing appointments and answering queries of patients.

candidates.title: medical laboratory technology vocational teacher
candidates.description: Medical laboratory technology vocational teachers technology instruct students in their specialised field of study, medical laboratory technology, which is predominantly practical in nature. They provide theoretical instruction in service of the practical skills and techniques the students must subsequently master for a medical laboratory technology-related profession. Medical laboratory technology vocational teachers monitor the students' progress, assist individually when necessary, and evaluate their knowledge and performance on the subject of medical laboratory technology through assignments, tests and examinations.

candidates.title: healthcare assistant
candidates.description: Healthcare assistants work in teams of nurses within the occupational fields of nursing, social care, clinical care and care of people of all age-groups. Healthcare assistants assist in the promotion and restoration of patients' health by providing physical and psychological support to patients, friends and families.

candidates.title: scientific laboratory technician
candidates.description: Scientific laboratory technicians carry out laboratory-based research, analysis and testing and support life science professionals. They sample, test, measure, research and analyse in areas such as biology, biotechnology, environmental science, forensic science and pharmacology. Scientific laboratory technicians also observe and monitor laboratory activities, record test sequences and analyse the results.

candidates.title: assistant clinical psychologist
candidates.description: Assistant clinical psychologists aid psychologists in their work. They work in healthcare facilities or private practices where they assist psychologists with their treatment of patients. Assistant clinical psychologists are healthcare professionals that can assess patients with psychological tests and aid with therapy, as well as performing administrative functions.

description: Hospital Assistant performs basic clinical and administrative tasks to support patient care under the supervision of medical practitioners or healthcare professionals. They assist patients with daily activities, take vital signs, manage medical records, support minor medical procedures, and help maintain cleanliness and hygiene within a healthcare facility. Acting as a key link between the patient and medical staff, they ensure efficient healthcare operations and contribute to patient comfort and well-being.
tasks: Assist patients with personal care activities, including bathing, dressing, feeding, and mobility support. Monitor and record patient vital signs such as temperature, pulse, and blood pressure. Assist doctors and medical staff during consultations, examinations, and minor procedures. Collect and label specimens for laboratory testing. Maintain patient records, documentation, clerical tasks, and manage medical supplies and inventory. Ensure cleanliness, hygiene, infection control, and sterilisation of medical equipment and patient care areas. Educate patients on basic health practices, preventive care, and post-treatment instructions.

candidates.title: healthcare assistant
candidates.description: Healthcare assistants work in teams of nurses within the occupational fields of nursing, social care, clinical care and care of people of all age-groups. Healthcare assistants assist in the promotion and restoration of patients' health by providing physical and psychological support to patients, friends and families.

candidates.title: medical administrative assistant
candidates.description: Medical administrative assistants work very closely with health professionals. They provide office support such as correspondence, fixing appointments and answering queries of patients.

candidates.title: doctors' surgery assistant
candidates.description: Doctors' surgery assistants support doctors of medicine in medical measures, in performing simple support activities during medical procedures, standardised diagnostic programmes and standardised point-of-care tests, ensuring surgery hygiene, cleaning, disinfecting, sterilising and maintaining medical devices and performing the organisational and administrative tasks required for operating a doctor`s surgery under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: nurse assistant
candidates.description: Nurse assistants provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. They perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, move patients or change linens and may transfer or transport patients.

candidates.title: medical laboratory assistant
candidates.description: Medical laboratory assistants work under supervision of the biomedical scientist and carry out basic laboratory procedures. They work in the pre-analytical handling of samples such as checking the details of specimens received for analysis, maintaining analysers, loading reagents, and packaging specimens. They also perform clerical tasks such as monitoring the stock levels of reagents used in analysis.

candidates.title: administrative assistant
candidates.description: Administrative assistants provide administrative and office support for supervisors. They perform a variety of tasks, such as answering telephone calls, receiving and directing visitors, ordering office supplies, maintaining the office facilities running smoothly, and ensuring that equipment and appliances work properly.

candidates.title: pharmacy assistant
candidates.description: Pharmacy assistants perform general duties, such as stock management, serving at the cash desk, or performing administrative duties. They deal with the inventory within the pharmacy under the supervision of a pharmacist.

candidates.title: hospital pharmacist
candidates.description: Hospital pharmacists prepare, dispense and provide medication to patients in hospitals. They collaborate with healthcare personnel such as doctors and nurses to treat patients and also offer advice and information on medications.

description: Diagnostic Imaging Equipment Technician operates and maintains medical imaging and diagnostic equipment to capture accurate images or recording of the internal body structure or physiological function. They prepare and monitor patients during procedures, ensure the equipment is safe and calibrated, and assist medical practitioners in interpreting results to support diagnosis and treatment. Their work is essential in a hospital, clinic, or diagnostic centre, contributing to early disease detection, cardiac and neurological assessment, and overall patient care.
tasks: Perform diagnostic imaging procedures, including X-rays, Computed Tomography (CT) scans, Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI), mammography, fluoroscopy, Electrocardiograms (ECGs), and Electroencephalograms (EEGs). Prepare and position patients for imaging or diagnostic tests, ensuring comfort and safety. Operate, maintain, calibrate, and perform quality checks on imaging and diagnostic equipment. Adhere to radiation protection, infection control, and safety protocols for patients and staff. Record, manage, and maintain accurate patient diagnostic data and documentation. Assist healthcare professionals during diagnostic procedures and provide basic patient support as required. Collaborate with radiologists and medical staff to support the review and handling of diagnostic results. Support scheduling, reporting, and administrative tasks within the diagnostic imaging department. Assist and support junior staff or trainees in routine diagnostic imaging operations.

candidates.title: diagnostic radiographer
candidates.description: Diagnostic radiographers plan, prepare and perform diagnostic imaging examinations and post processing, with a wide range of equipment and techniques using X-rays, strong magnetic fields or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and high frequency sound (Ultrasound).

candidates.title: medical device engineering technician
candidates.description: Medical device engineering technicians collaborate with medical device engineers in the design, development and production of medical-technical systems, installations, and equipment such as pacemakers, MRI machines, and X-ray devices. They build, install, inspect, modify, repair, calibrate, and maintain medical-technical equipment and support systems. Medical device engineering technicians are responsible for the operational readiness, safe use, economic operation and the appropriate procurement of medical equipment and facilities in hospitals.

candidates.title: anatomical pathology technician
candidates.description: Anatomical pathology technicians assist specialised doctors in pathology in conducting post-mortem examinations, keeping records of the samples, specimens, organs and the respective findings and taking care of their appropriate disposal under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: construction equipment technician
candidates.description: Construction equipment technicians inspect, maintain and repair heavy-duty vehicles used in construction, forestry and earthworks such as bulldozers, excavators and harvesters. They perform evaluations of the equipment, and ensure the safety and optimal efficiency of the machinery.

candidates.title: office equipment repair technician
candidates.description: Office equipment repair technicians provide services to businesses related to installing, maintaining and repairing new or existing equipment such as printers, scanners and modems, on the clients' premises. They keep records of performed services and return equipment to a repair centre if needed.

candidates.title: instrument technician
candidates.description: Instrument technicians assist and support musicians before, during and after the performance to ensure the instruments and the connected equipment, the backline, are setup properly. They maintain, check, tune and repair instruments and assist with quick changes.

candidates.title: reprographics technician
candidates.description: Reprographics technicians are responsible for the full or partial process of reproduction of graphical documents through mechanical-driven or digital means, such as photography, scanning or digital printing. These activities are commonly performed for purposes of maintaining archives or other structured catalogues.

candidates.title: radiation protection technician
candidates.description: Radiation protection technicians monitor radiation levels in buildings and facilities to ensure compliance with health and safety standards, and to prevent dangerous elevations in the radiation level. They take measures to minimise radiation emissions, and to prevent further contamination in the event of radiation pollution, by developing radiation protection plans, in particular for nuclear plants and facilities.

description: Sonographer performs diagnostic medical ultrasound examinations to create an image of the internal body structure, assisting a physician in diagnosing and monitoring medical conditions. They prepare patients for procedures, operate and maintain ultrasound equipments, analyse images for preliminary findings, ensure patient comfort, and maintain accurate clinical records under the direct supervision of medical practitioners or other health professionals.
tasks: Conduct ultrasound examinations of various body parts, including abdomen, pelvis, thyroid, breast, musculoskeletal, obstetric, and vascular areas. Analyse sonographic images and provide preliminary findings to support medical diagnosis and treatment planning. Collaborate with physicians and healthcare teams by providing imaging findings to assist in patient diagnosis and management. Prepare, operate, and perform routine maintenance checks to ensure proper functioning of ultrasound equipment. Ensure patient safety, comfort, and confidentiality during ultrasound procedures. Maintain accurate patient records, imaging data, and examination documentation in accordance with clinical standards. Provide guidance and support to junior staff during ultrasound procedures as required.

candidates.title: cartographer
candidates.description: Cartographers create maps by combining various scientific informations depending of the purpose of the map (e.g. topographic, urban, or political maps). They combine the interpretation of mathematical notes and measurements with the aesthetics and visual depiction of the site for developing the maps. They may also work on developing and improving geographic information systems and may perform scientific research within cartography.

candidates.title: diagnostic radiographer
candidates.description: Diagnostic radiographers plan, prepare and perform diagnostic imaging examinations and post processing, with a wide range of equipment and techniques using X-rays, strong magnetic fields or Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and high frequency sound (Ultrasound).

candidates.title: radiographer
candidates.description: Radiographers use a range of technologies to examine, treat and care for patients. They work in the fields of Medical Imaging, Radiotherapy and Nuclear Medicine and apply ionising radiation, ultrasound, magnetic resonance imaging and radioactive sources.

candidates.title: oceanographer
candidates.description: Oceanographers study and perform research on matters related to the sea and oceans. Oceanographers divide their expertise in different branches of research which are physical oceanographers whose research focus on waves and tides, chemical oceanographers whose study address the chemical constitution of sea waters, and geological oceanographer whose research refers to the bottom of seas and their plaques.

candidates.title: geographer
candidates.description: Geographers are scholars who study human and physical geography. Depending on their specialisation, they study political, economical and cultural aspects of humanity contained within human geography. Moreover, they study land formations, soils, natural frontiers, and water flows contained in physical geography.

candidates.title: hydrographic surveying technician
candidates.description: Hydrographic surveying technicians perform oceanographic and surveying operations in marine environments. They assist hydrographic surveyors, using specialised equipment to map and study underwater topography and morphology of bodies of water. They assist in the installation and deployment of hydrographic and surveying equipment and report about their work.

candidates.title: audiologist
candidates.description: Audiologists assess, diagnose and treat patients ( children or adults) with audiological and vestibular disorders caused by infectious, genetic, traumatic or degenerative conditions, such as hearing loss, tinnitus, dizziness, imbalance, hyperacusis and auditory processing difficulties. They can prescribe a hearing aid and have a role in assessing and managing patients who may benefit from cochlear implants.

candidates.title: metrologist
candidates.description: Metrologists study and practice the science of measurement. They develop quantity systems, units of measurement and measuring methods to be used in science. Metrologists establish new methods and tools to quantify and better understand information.

description: Clinical Instructor guides and supervises students in a clinical setting, bridging classroom learning with hands-on patient care. They support healthcare delivery under professional supervision, mentor students, assess competencies, provide feedback, and ensure adherence to medical and educational standards, while collaborating with an institution to maintain records, develop curricula, and uphold healthcare regulations.
tasks: Plan and coordinate clinical placements for students in hospitals or clinical settings. Supervise and guide students during clinical training sessions to ensure safe and effective practice. Assess student competencies using structured evaluation methods and document their progress. Provide feedback and mentoring to support the development of clinical skills and professional practice. Collaborate with healthcare teams to align clinical learning experiences with curriculum outcomes. Utilise clinical simulation tools and training equipment to enhance student learning and competency development. Participate in academic meetings, quality assurance activities, and continuous improvement of clinical education programmes.

candidates.title: first aid instructor
candidates.description: First aid instructors teach students immediate lifesaving emergency measures, such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation, the recovery position, and injury care. They provided practice materials such as a specialised manikin.

candidates.title: survival instructor
candidates.description: Survival instructors guide groups into vast, natural areas, and assist them in a self-directed instruction of basic survival needs without any comfort facilities or modern gear to fall back on. They coach the participants into mastering survival skills such as fire making, producing primitive equipment, shelter construction and procurement of water and nourishment. They ensure the participants are aware of certain safety measures without diminishing the level of adventure, of environment protection and of risk management. They encourage efforts of leadership from the group and mentor the participants individually so as to push their limits responsibly and help overcome potential fears.

candidates.title: medicine lecturer
candidates.description: Medicine lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of study, medicine, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of medicine, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: sports instructor
candidates.description: Sports instructors introduce people to a sport and teach them the skills required for the performance of sport. They have a strong grip on one or more sports, which are often adventure sports, and know how to motivate others and share with them the enjoyment of the activity.

candidates.title: healthcare specialist lecturer
candidates.description: Healthcare specialist lecturers are subject professors, teachers, or lecturers, and often doctors who instruct students who have obtained an upper secondary education diploma in their own specialised field of healthcare, which is predominantly academic in nature. They work with their university research assistants and university teaching assistants for the preparation of lectures and of exams, for grading papers and exams, for leading laboratory practices, and for leading review and feedback sessions for the students. They also conduct academic research in their respective field of specialist healthcare, publish their findings and liaise with other university colleagues.

candidates.title: firefighter instructor
candidates.description: Firefighter instructors train probationary, new academy recruits, or cadets, on the theory and practice necessary to become a firefighter. They conduct theoretical lectures on academic subjects such as law, basic chemistry, safety regulations, risk management, fire prevention, reading blueprints etc. Fire academy instructors also provide more hands-on, practical instruction regarding the usage of assistive equipment and rescue tools such as a fire hose, fire axe, smoke mask etc., but also heavy physical training, breathing techniques, first aid, self defense tactics and vehicle operations. They also prepare and develop lesson plans and new training programmes as new public service-related regulations and issues arise. The instructors monitor the students' progress, evaluate them individually and prepare performance evaluation reports.

candidates.title: driving instructor
candidates.description: Driving instructors teach people the theory and practice on how to operate a vehicle safely and according to regulations. They assist students in developing the skills needed to drive and prepare them for the driving theory and the driving examination. They may also supervise driving examinations.

candidates.title: motorcycle instructor
candidates.description: Motorcycle instructors teach people the theory and practice of how to operate a motorcycle safely and according to regulations. They assist students in developing the skills needed to ride and prepare them for the theory test and the practical riding test.

description: Ophthalmic Assistant supports an ophthalmologist or other eye care professional by performing basic clinical and administrative tasks to ensure smooth patient care. They conduct an eye test, assist with a diagnostic or surgical procedure, prepare a patient for treatment, and maintain a clinical and sterile environment, while also managing scheduling and inventory to support the efficient operation of an ophthalmic clinic or hospital.
tasks: Conduct visual acuity tests, tonometry, and assist with ophthalmic imaging techniques. Prepare patients for ophthalmic procedures, assist during surgeries, and maintain sterile conditions. Guide patients through clinical visits and provide pre- and post-procedure instructions related to eye care procedures. Schedule procedures, manage operating theatre bookings, and monitor ophthalmic supplies and inventory. Maintain accurate patient records, clinical documentation, and administrative data in accordance with healthcare standards. Assist in providing treatment for minor eye conditions under the supervision of an ophthalmologist or optometrist. Perform basic ophthalmic clinical procedures, such as administering eye drops and preparing instruments. Provide guidance and support to junior staff during clinical activities when required.

candidates.title: doctors' surgery assistant
candidates.description: Doctors' surgery assistants support doctors of medicine in medical measures, in performing simple support activities during medical procedures, standardised diagnostic programmes and standardised point-of-care tests, ensuring surgery hygiene, cleaning, disinfecting, sterilising and maintaining medical devices and performing the organisational and administrative tasks required for operating a doctor`s surgery under supervision, following the orders of the doctor of medicine.

candidates.title: optician
candidates.description: Opticians help to improve and correct an individual's vision. They fit spectacle lenses and frames, contact lenses, and other devices according to the specifications of the individual. Their scope of practice varies according to national regulations and they might operate according to prescriptions provided by a specialised doctor in ophthalmology or an optometrist in the countries where requested.

candidates.title: optometrist
candidates.description: Optometrists examine and test eyes to identify abnormalities, visual problems, or disease. They prescribe and fit lenses such as spectacles and contacts, and offer advice on visual problems. They may also refer patients to a medical practitioner. Their scope of practice and title varies according to national regulations.

candidates.title: dental chairside assistant
candidates.description: Dental chairside assistants support dental practitioners in clinical treatments, as preparation and helping in practical execution and follow-up, and administrative tasks under supervision and following the orders of the dental practitioner.

candidates.title: eyewear and optical equipment shop manager
candidates.description: Eyewear and optical equipment shop managers assume responsibility for activities and staff in specialised shops.

candidates.title: optical technician
candidates.description: Optical technicians assemble, repair and design various parts of eyewear such as lenses, frames, patterns and eyewear. They cut, inspect, mount and polish all parts using various machinery and hand tools. Optical technicians shape, grind and coat lenses for prescription eyewear. They fit completed lenses into eyeglass frames. Optical technicians ensure that lenses conform to the dispensing optician’s, specialised doctor in ophtalmology's or optometrist's prescriptions. They may also work with other associated optical instrumentation and its maintenance.

candidates.title: pharmacy assistant
candidates.description: Pharmacy assistants perform general duties, such as stock management, serving at the cash desk, or performing administrative duties. They deal with the inventory within the pharmacy under the supervision of a pharmacist.

candidates.title: chiropractic assistant
candidates.description: Chiropractic assistants perform routine and administrative tasks to support patient care and work under the sole direction and supervision of a Chiropractor or Specialized Chiropractor. They may interview patients, keep records of the case history, assist Chiropractors or Specialized Chiropractors in providing patients examination and perform administrative tasks. Chiropractic assistants work within defined contexts using agreed protocols and procedures.

description: Assistant Medical Officer Grade U5 responsible for providing health services to the community from the aspects of curative, preventive prevention, promotion, and rehabilitation in the health service system in Malaysia. Provides curative treatment, preventive care, and emergency assistance services at health centres including Static and Mobile Dispensaries, General Health Outpatient Department, and Accident and Emergency Department. Provides early and immediate treatment and support for all emergency cases and refer the cases for further handling to medical officers, provides assistance services in various Departments of Expertise, ward institutions and other programme.
tasks: Examining and treating patients in accordance with Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) and Clinical Practice Guideline (CPG), including basic initial treatment, asthma management, intravenous therapy, and patient preparation for specific treatment procedures. Administering medications and injections according to protocol, monitoring treatment progress, reporting abnormal conditions/adverse effects, and recording vital signs and patient intake/output charts. Attending to the special needs of patients, determining special diets, and collecting laboratory test samples in accordance with procedures. Educating patients on health care related to diseases, and participating in health programmes/promotions such as PROSTAR, health camps, and national/state health campaigns. Implementing patient rehabilitation, providing counselling for HIV/AIDS, drug addiction, psychoeducation for mental health patients, and dietary counselling for patients with conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, and renal failure.

candidates.title: health and safety officer
candidates.description: Health and safety officers execute plans for the improvement of work environments and cultures. They assess risks and interview employees to ensure the work environment is compliant with health and safety rules, as well as ensuring the interaction within the workplace occurs in a positive and productive manner. If employed in a healthcare facility the health and safety officer has to investigate infections spreading across a facility and advice all employees how to combat and prevent infections. Furthermore health physics is applied at facilities where people are exposed to ionizing radiation such as nuclear power plants and research institutions.

candidates.title: public health policy officer
candidates.description: Public health policy officers develop and implement strategies for the improvement of a community's health care policy. They advise governments on policy changes and identify problems in current health care policies.

candidates.title: nurse assistant
candidates.description: Nurse assistants provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. They perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, move patients or change linens and may transfer or transport patients.

candidates.title: medical practice manager
candidates.description: Medical practice managers manage the day-to-day operations of a medical practice. They oversee the staff and business side of the practice.

description: Public Health Unit Inspector enforces health, safety, and sanitation regulations to protect community well-being. They conduct inspections of food establishments, water supply, waste management systems, nursing homes, or other public facilities, ensuring compliance with laws and standards. Their role includes investigating health complaints, promoting hygienic practices, monitoring occupational and environmental safety, and collaborating with relevant agencies during a health or safety emergency.
tasks: Conduct routine inspections of public facilities, workplaces, food establishments, vehicles, and residential care facilities to ensure compliance with health, hygiene, and safety regulations. Inspect machinery, equipment, and production, transport, storage, and handling processes to ensure conformity with applicable laws, standards, and specifications. Collect samples of water, food, and other materials for laboratory analysis to monitor quality, hygiene, and safety. Investigate complaints and reported violations related to public health, sanitation, and safety, and recommend appropriate corrective actions. Advise employers, workers, businesses, and the public on hygiene, sanitation, occupational safety, and regulatory compliance. Prepare detailed inspection reports, documentation, and certification of compliance or non-compliance. Collaborate with health agencies, government authorities, and relevant professionals during disease outbreaks, public health emergencies, and safety investigations. Evaluate standards of care, emergency preparedness, staffing, cleanliness, and safety protocols in residential care facilities. Provide training and education to staff, business operators, and communities on health, hygiene, and safety practices. Monitor waste management practices, emissions, and environmental or product-related risks to prevent contamination and hazards.

candidates.title: environmental health inspector
candidates.description: Environmental health inspectors carry out investigations to ensure that areas, organisations and companies comply with environmental and public health legislation. They evaluate environmental complaints, provide reports on their findings and work to prevent future hazards or noncompliance with current policies. Environmental health inspectors perform consultations to promote public health and safety.

candidates.title: health and safety inspector
candidates.description: Health and safety inspectors investigate the implementation and application of labour standards and policies in a workplace. They advise employers as well as employees on the improvement of policy and legislation implementation, ensure that the law is adhered to, and that matters of equality and labour rights are respected. They write reports and communicate with authorities.

candidates.title: healthcare inspector
candidates.description: Healthcare inspectors visit healthcare facilities to ensure proper care is given to all patients in accordance with legal requirements. They also inspect if equipment, processes and staff operate adequately to prevent the spreading of infections and diseases.

candidates.title: occupational health and safety inspector
candidates.description: Occupational health and safety inspectors perform workplace audits to ensure compliance with government and environment legislation. They also investigate work accidents. Occupational health and safety inspectors interview employees to ensure the work environment is compliant with health and safety rules, inspect the physical work site and analyse legal paperwork.

candidates.title: food safety inspector
candidates.description: Food safety inspectors carry out inspections in food processing environments from a food safety standpoint. They are part of official control bodies who check and control food products and processes to ensure compliance with regulations and laws governing safety and health.

candidates.title: health and safety officer

Furthermore health physics is applied at facilities where people are exposed to ionizing radiation such as nuclear power plants and research institutions.

candidates.title: hazardous waste inspector
candidates.description: Hazardous waste inspectors inspect industrial sites to ensure they adhere to waste disposal legislation, and inspect their equipment to see if it is operational and functions according to regulations. They also aim to educate the public on hazardous substances and on hazardous waste handling regulations.

candidates.title: transport health and safety inspector
candidates.description: Transport health and safety inspectors are responsible for maintaining safety standards, reducing risk to company, staff and customers and achieving industry standards. They evaluate existing security systems to determine potential risks in all transport sectors such as road and sea transport, and develop policies and procedures that minimise the risk to properties, employees and computer systems.

description: Occupational Safety and Health Inspector assesses and monitors workplaces or environmental conditions to ensure compliance with health, safety, and hygiene regulations. They conduct inspections, evaluate risks, enforce occupational safety law, implement safety programs, and provide guidance to prevent accidents, injury, or occupational illnesses. This role includes auditing workplaces, investigating incidents, promoting safe practices, and ensuring public and employee wellbeing across various industries, including specialised settings such as beauty salons or production facilities.
tasks: Conduct workplace inspections to ensure compliance with occupational safety, health, hygiene, and sanitation regulations. Identify and assess workplace hazards, including chemical, physical, biological, and ergonomic risks, and recommend appropriate control measures. Advise employers, workers, and relevant stakeholders on safe work practices and regulatory requirements. Investigate workplace accidents, incidents, and complaints, and recommend appropriate corrective actions. Conduct risk assessments, safety audits, and environmental monitoring, and maintain accurate documentation. Coordinate and deliver occupational safety and health training programmes for employees. Review and monitor workplace safety policies, procedures, and management systems to ensure regulatory compliance. Liaise with regulatory bodies, government agencies, and relevant authorities on occupational safety and health matters. Inspect machinery, equipment, and production, transport, handling, and storage areas to ensure regulatory conformity.

Occupational health and safety inspectors interview employees to ensure the work environment is compliant with health and safety rules, inspect the physical work site and analyse legal paperwork.
